structure.title: Summary of Banque Postale Group’s sustainable performance
structure.heading: Summary of Banque Postale Group’s sustainable performance
structure.summary:
- Focus: Summary of La Banque Postale Group’s sustainable performance and ESG strategy, structured by ESRS topics (E1–E5, S1–S4, G1) following a double materiality analysis covering own operations and financed activities.
- Governance and strategy:
  - Mission-led company embedding impact culture and impact finance; ESG fully integrated into strategy.
  - Strong Supervisory and Executive Boards’ oversight; variable executive remuneration linked to sustainability targets.
  - Issues highlighted as specific to the Group: impact culture, impact finance, cybersecurity.
  - Comprehensive policies: risk management; Responsible Financing and Investment Charter with exclusions (coal, oil, gas, environmental controversies); sector principles (aeronautics); responsible operations (energy efficiency, digital, mobility, purchasing).
- Key financial/ESG scale:
  - Total income: €41.1bn.
  - €390bn of outstanding financial assets under management with ESG filters.
- Climate (E1):
  - Net zero by 2040 with an ambitious Transition Plan across operations and CIB portfolios.
  - Risks/opportunities managed (physical/transition risks, pricing/lending integration via ESG checklist and Impact Weighting Factor).
  - Financing the transition: “just transition” offers for retail, green offers for businesses, Climate & Biodiversity Impact Fund, GREaT investment methodology, shareholder engagement.
  - Financing of renewable energy projects: €5bn (LBP SA scope).
  - GHG metrics (2024): Scope 3 Cat.15 financed emissions 62,598 ktCO2e; operational scope 367 ktCO2e.
  - Targets: Scopes 1–2 -65% (2021–2030); financed emissions reduction pathways including home loans -43.6% (2022–2030) and commercial real estate -53% (2022–2030).
- Nature: Pollution, Water, Biodiversity (E2–E4):
  - Group-level biodiversity and water policies; exclusions (e.g., pesticides) and deforestation/land-conversion criteria; CNP Assurances “Green Works” Charter; LBP AM Biodiversity Policy (engagement, advocacy, exclusions).
  - Commitment to support high-impact, nature-dependent sectors and align nature goals with climate ambition.
  - TNFD-aligned biodiversity footprinting of financing and investment portfolios.
  - Metrics: static land impacts 55 MSA.km²; dynamic land impacts 4,180 MSA.km².
  - Actions: measure impacts/dependencies (incl. pollution, water stress), fund protection/restoration projects, active stewardship, sustainable forestry, water/sanitation components in green loans.
- Circular economy (E5):
  - Resources & Circular Economy policy to reduce consumption and optimize end-of-life; “Green Works” in real estate.
  - Financed activities: no dedicated waste policy in CIB portfolios; contribution to La Poste Group’s resource footprint and reduction pathways.
  - Metrics (operations): total waste 1,435 t; WEEE 575 t; non-recycled waste 253 t (17.6%).
- Social – Own workforce (S1):
  - Policies on quality of work life, fair pay, human rights, disability, diversity/equality, and employee experience.
  - Actions: prevention plans, diversity/disability agreements, engagement surveys, monitoring discrimination incidents, social dialogue.
  - Metrics: 14,512 employees; 100% covered by collective agreements; 98.77% adequate wages; 54.8% women; gender pay gap 4.53%; 16.7% workers with disabilities; 0 serious human rights incidents.
- Social – Workers in the value chain (S2):
  - Policies: Responsible/Ethical Purchasing and supplier assessment; Group Human Rights policy; Responsible Financing & Investment Charter; LBP AM Human Rights policy.
  - Actions: whistleblowing and protection, ESG supplier audits and listening questionnaires, stewardship with financed entities.
  - Metrics (La Poste workers for LBP): 19,382 workers; 61% women; 79% full-time.
- Social – Affected communities (S3):
  - Human rights alignment with UNGPs, ILO, OECD; controversy monitoring and stewardship.
  - Strong regional commitment: financing for local authorities and essential services (infrastructure, mobility, energy transition; hospitals; social housing); support for SMEs/ISEs; charity financing; wide regional coverage via La Poste; societal sponsorship.
  - Metrics: annual premium income—local economy €1.94bn; social housing/health/non-profit €1.53bn; local authorities €5.8bn.
- Social – Customers and end-users (S4):
  - Customer-centric codes of conduct; policies for vulnerable customers; data protection and information systems security.
  - Actions: accessible banking “by design,” identification and support of vulnerable customers (e.g., L’Appui), regional access, customer dialogue and complaints handling, cybersecurity plan (2021–2027), ESG product assessment (checklist), impact products (green loans, impact cards).
  - Metrics: 14 CNP Assurances products improving access for vulnerable groups; 418,840 holders of the Simplicité low-cost account option; 30% of new offers identified as sustainable.
- Governance – Business conduct (G1):
  - Code of conduct, whistleblowing and protection systems, anti-corruption prevention/detection with mandatory training, ESG integration in supplier selection/monitoring, responsible purchasing and timely payments, and lobbying for ethics/impact finance.
  - Metrics: average supplier invoice payment time 51.6 days; 0 anti-corruption convictions; 98.7% employees trained in AML/CFT.
- Reporting framework (ESRS 2):
  - First CSRD-compliant sustainability report (2024 data; published 2025), transitioning from former Non-Financial Statement to ESRS-aligned structure with EFRAG code tagging.
  - Expanded disclosures on the climate transition plan and biodiversity footprint.
  - Positioned within a broader reporting suite: integrated report, mission report, and a dedicated Climate & Nature report.

structure.title: Sustainability Report
structure.heading: Sustainability Report
structure.start_phrase: In this sustainability report, the data points to which La Banque Postale Group has responded are identified at the end of each paragraph using the corresponding EFRAG code.
structure.summary:
- La Banque Postale’s first sustainability report for FY2024 (published 2025) prepared under the CSRD and ESRS, as transposed into the French Commercial Code (Article L. 233-28-4).
- Shift from the former Non-Financial Statement (NFS) in the Universal Registration Document to an ESRS-aligned structure, with expanded disclosures.
- Note to reader: data points are tagged with EFRAG/ESRS codes (e.g., [E1_1_01]) for traceability.
- Focus areas enhanced this year include the climate transition plan and measurement of the biodiversity footprint of financing and investment portfolios.
- The sustainability report is part of a broader reporting suite:
  - Integrated report: concise overview of strategy, transformation, and ESG highlights.
  - Mission report: the Group’s mission, commitments, targets, and Mission Committee’s assessment.
  - Climate and Nature report: detailed impacts on climate and biodiversity, and alignment of decarbonization with conservation targets.
- Report structure mirrors ESRS:
  - Environment: E1 Climate change, E2 Pollution, E3 Water and marine resources, E4 Biodiversity and ecosystems, E5 Circular economy.
  - Social: S1 Own workforce, S2 Workers in the value chain, S3 Affected communities, S4 Customers and end-users.
  - Governance: G1 Business conduct.
  - General information (ESRS 2).
- Reference to a glossary (page 808) for CSR terms.

nodes.title: General information on the preparation of sustainability reports [ESRS 2]
nodes.heading: 2.1 General information on the preparation of sustainability reports [ESRS 2]
nodes.start_phrase: In 2025, La Banque Postale is publishing its first sustainability report for 2024, in accordance with the requirements of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (“CSRD”), transposed into Article L. 233-28-4 of the French Commercial Code , and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) issued by the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group (EFRAG).
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and context: La Banque Postale’s first sustainability report for 2024, prepared under the CSRD and ESRS (EFRAG) framework, replacing the former Non-Financial Statement in the Universal Registration Document. Paragraphs tag data points with ESRS/EFRAG codes (e.g., [E1_1_01]).
- Focus areas: New structure aligned to ESRS with added detail on the climate transition plan and measurement of the biodiversity footprint of financing and investment portfolios.
- Report ecosystem: Positioned alongside the Integrated Report, Mission Report, Climate and Nature Report, standalone Transition Plan, and the UNEP FI PRB report; subsidiaries’ climate and nature commitments also reported (notably in Article 29 LEC responsible investment reports).
- Assurance and governance: Forms part of the Group’s management report; sustainability information certified by Statutory Auditors per CSRD, with the certification report in Section 2.6.
- Standards application and maturity: First-time CSRD/ESRS application involves interpretation uncertainties and reliance on judgments (e.g., double materiality thresholds, IRO assessment). The methodology, thresholds, and data sources are described in Sections 2.1.4.1 and 2.1.4.3 and will be reviewed annually as part of continuous improvement.
- Structure of disclosures: ESRS-aligned chapters covering Environment (E1–E5: climate, pollution, water/marine, biodiversity, circular economy), Social (S1–S4: own workforce, value chain workers, affected communities, customers/end-users), Governance (G1), and general information.
- Scope declaration and perimeter: Consolidated at Group level consistent with financial consolidation (excluding non-material CNP Europe Life), with CNP Santander Insurance Services Ireland included for social data. Clear naming conventions for Group, La Banque Postale (banking scope), and CNP Assurances (insurance scope). Full disclosure for all financially consolidated subsidiaries (qualitative and quantitative, including GHG).
- Exclusions and partial coverage: Excludes CNP Cyprus Insurance Holding (non-material, in process of sale) and CNP Europe Life (run-off, no employees). Partial coverage for CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (only S1 social stock this year). Additional qualitative disclosures on key entities (e.g., CNP Assurances, LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier, LBP Consumer Finance, Louvre Banque Privée).
- Carbon footprint boundary: Covers the full consolidated scope, entities under operational control, and value chain interests.
- Cross-reporting: La Banque Postale is also included in La Poste Group and CDC consolidated sustainability reports; CNP Assurances is included here and publishes its own report.
- Subsidiary exemptions: Louvre Banque Privée and La Banque Postale Consumer Finance meet eligibility for standalone sustainability reports but are exempt as they are covered within the Group report and are not listed on a regulated market.
- Methodology and metrics: Centralized methodological choices and calculation details in Section 2.1.1.2, with topic-specific methodologies referenced (decarbonization targets 2.2.1.4.1; GHG emissions 2.2.1.7.3; workforce indicators 2.3.1.7; supplier payment practices 2.4.1.4.3). Detailed treatment of financed/investment emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15), including components, scopes, financing shares; future alignment of approaches across entities planned.
- Data quality and estimates: Use of estimates, extrapolations, and interim dates where more reliable (e.g., 30 June 2024 for La Banque Postale financed emissions; 31 Dec 2023 for LBP AM). No comparative data for new indicators in this first year. All figures to be read considering these methodological notes.
- Internal control and improvement: Internal control system in place to enhance data reliability, with potential refinements over time; commitment to continuous improvement as guidance and best practices evolve.
- Navigation aids: Coverage of disclosure requirements in Section 2.5.1.1; reporting scope in 2.1.1.1 (with employee scope in 2.3.1.1.1); additional methodological details provided within each relevant section; glossary available for CSR terms.

nodes.title: General information on the preparation of sustainability reports [ESRS 2] - Introduction
nodes.source_title: General information on the preparation of sustainability reports [ESRS 2]
nodes.source_heading: General information on the preparation of sustainability reports [ESRS 2]
nodes.heading: 2.1 General information on the preparation of sustainability reports [ESRS 2]
nodes.start_phrase: In 2025, La Banque Postale is publishing its first sustainability report for 2024, in accordance with the requirements of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (“CSRD”), transposed into Article L. 233-28-4 of the French Commercial Code , and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) issued by the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group (EFRAG).
nodes.summary: La Banque Postale’s first CSRD-aligned sustainability report (reporting year 2024, published 2025) complies with ESRS issued by EFRAG and French Commercial Code Article L.233-28-4, replacing the former NFS in the URD and adding topics such as the climate transition plan and measurement of the biodiversity footprint of financing and investment portfolios. It sits alongside the Group’s integrated, mission, and Climate & Nature reports, the UNEP FI PRB report, and subsidiary publications by CNP Assurances, LBP AM, and Louvre Banque Privée (incl. Article 29 LEC reports). The report follows the ESRS structure (Environment E1–E5, Social S1–S4, Governance G1, and General information), forms part of the management report, and is certified by Statutory Auditors (see Section 2.6). Given first-time application, the Group notes interpretive uncertainties, reliance on judgments for double materiality (thresholds and value chain), and use of estimates/extrapolations; in some cases interim data were used (e.g., 30 June 2024 for La Banque Postale’s financed emissions, 31 December 2023 for LBP AM). Methodological references include materiality methodology (2.1.4.1), data sources (2.1.4.3), disclosure coverage (2.5.1.1), reporting scope (2.1.1.1) and employee scope (2.3.1.1.1), calculation methods (2.1.1.2), decarbonisation targets (2.2.1.4.1), GHG methods (2.2.1.7.3), workforce indicators (2.3.1.7), supplier payment practices (2.4.1.4.3), and detailed treatment of Scope 3 Category 15 investment emissions, with planned alignment across entities. No comparative data are provided for new indicators. An internal control system supports data reliability, with a stated commitment to continuous improvement as market guidance evolves.

nodes.title: Basis for preparation of the sustainability report
nodes.heading: 2.1.1 Basis for preparation of the sustainability report
nodes.start_phrase: The sustainability report is prepared on a consolidated basis (La Banque Postale Group) in line with the scope of consolidation of the financial statements presented in Sections 5.1 “Consolidated financial statements” and 5.2 “Notes to the consolidated financial statements” of the Universal Registration Document, excluding CNP Europe Life(1).
nodes.summary:
- Context and framework: Outlines general information on preparing La Banque Postale Group’s sustainability report under ESRS 2, emphasizing continuous improvement, potential refinement of estimates, and an internal control system to ensure data reliability, with possible future enhancements.

- Basis of preparation: Reporting is on a consolidated basis aligned with the Group’s financial consolidation perimeter (Universal Registration Document Sections 5.1 and 5.2), with clear terminology for La Banque Postale Group (banking and insurance), La Banque Postale (banking), and CNP Assurances (insurance scope).

- Scope of disclosure: All financially consolidated subsidiaries are fully disclosed, including qualitative information and quantitative indicators such as greenhouse gas emissions.

- Exclusions and partial inclusions:
  - Excludes CNP Cyprus Insurance Holding and its three subsidiaries (non-material; in disposal process as of 31/12/2024).
  - Excludes CNP Europe Life (run-off; no employees).
  - Partially includes CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (only social stock information S1 consolidated for the year).

- Additional qualitative disclosures: Provides significant qualitative information for specific entities (CNP Assurances; La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring; LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier; La Banque Postale Consumer Finance; Louvre Banque Privée and its subsidiary).

- Non-consolidated entities: Generally excluded unless a significant impact is identified by internal experts, in which case narrative disclosures may be provided (e.g., MicroDon, L’Envol).

- Carbon footprint boundary: Covers the entire consolidated scope, subsidiaries under operational control, and investees within the value chain.

- Reporting relationships: La Banque Postale is included in the consolidated sustainability reports of La Poste Group and Caisse des Dépôts; CNP Assurances is included in La Banque Postale’s report, while CNP Assurances SA also publishes its own report.

- Subsidiary reporting exemption: Louvre Banque Privée and La Banque Postale Consumer Finance meet eligibility criteria for standalone sustainability reports but are exempted as they are covered within the Group report and are not listed on a regulated market.

- References: Full consolidation scope is detailed in Note 3.1 (Section 5.2) of the Universal Registration Document; glossary of CSR terms referenced.

nodes.title: Scope declaration
nodes.heading: 2.1.1.1 Scope declaration
nodes.start_phrase: The sustainability report is prepared on a consolidated basis (La Banque Postale Group) in line with the scope of consolidation of the financial statements presented in Sections 5.1 “Consolidated financial statements” and 5.2 “Notes to the consolidated financial statements” of the Universal Registration Document, excluding CNP Europe Life(1).
nodes.summary:
- Context and intent: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document covering ESRS 2 “General information on the preparation of sustainability reports,” with a glossary reference. Emphasis on continuous improvement, potential refinement of estimates, and a new internal control system to enhance data reliability.

- Basis for preparation and scope:
  - Report prepared on a consolidated Group basis aligned with the financial statement consolidation scope, with terminology clarified for Group, banking, and insurance perimeters.
  - Full disclosure for all financially consolidated subsidiaries, including qualitative data and quantitative indicators (notably GHG emissions).
  - Specific inclusions/exclusions:
    - Added: CNP Santander Insurance Services Ireland for social information.
    - Excluded as non-material/in transition: CNP Cyprus Insurance Holding and its entities; CNP Europe Life.
    - Partial exclusion: CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (only social stock data S1 in 2024).
    - Additional qualitative disclosures for select entities (CNP Assurances; LBP Leasing & Factoring; LBP AM and LFDE; LBP Consumer Finance; Louvre Banque Privée).
    - Non-consolidated entities reported only if impacts are significant (e.g., MicroDon, L’Envol).
  - Carbon footprint boundary includes the entire consolidated scope, entities under operational control, and value chain holdings where relevant.

- Value chain coverage:
  - Own operations and services: suppliers, buildings, IT, energy/resources, employment; customer transactions, payments, insurance services.
  - Financed activities: lending to retail and business clients; investment portfolios.

- Group reporting relationships and exemptions:
  - La Banque Postale is included in La Poste Group and CDC consolidated sustainability reports.
  - CNP Assurances is covered within La Banque Postale’s report and also issues its own report.
  - Louvre Banque Privée and La Banque Postale Consumer Finance qualify for standalone reports but are exempt due to inclusion in the Group report and absence of listed securities.

- Transparency choices under ESRS:
  - No omission of information on intellectual property/know-how.
  - No exemption used for imminent developments or matters under negotiation.

- Calculation methods and data quality:
  - Social and governance data sourced directly across the value chain.
  - Environmental data estimated using indirect sources:
    - GHG emission factors from ADEME’s Footprint database (physical and monetary ratios).
    - Financed emissions methodologies detailed in dedicated sections; uncertainty levels vary by metric and are broken down elsewhere.
  - Uncertainty reduction roadmap:
    - Prioritize actual activity data and physical factors over monetary ones where possible.
    - Improve financed emissions accuracy via counterparty emissions disclosures.
    - Enhance biodiversity measurement with physical metrics.

- Key metrics with higher uncertainty, assumptions, and sources:
  - Scope 3 GHG (categories 1 and 2): reliance on monetary factors and purchase allocations; factor and allocation uncertainties.
  - Scope 3 GHG (category 15 – financed emissions): use of data provider models or PCAF sector factors when counterparty data is missing; model/factor uncertainties.
  - Portfolio biodiversity footprint: Global Biodiversity Score using sector/country outstandings; uncertainties from model and input data; use of financial data for multiple portfolio types.
  - Resources allocated to action plans: expert-based allocations with associated uncertainty.

nodes.title: Calculation methods and details of published indicators
nodes.heading: 2.1.1.2 Calculation methods and details of published indicators
nodes.start_phrase: All social and governance information is calculated from direct sources, across the entire value chain.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and coverage: The sustainability report spans La Banque Postale Group’s full value chain—own operations (suppliers, buildings, IT, energy, employment), service activities (customer transactions, payments, insurance), and financed activities (credit to retail and businesses, investment portfolios). No information is omitted for IP/innovation or due to imminent developments.

- Reporting framework: First-time application of CSRD and ESRS, with a continuous improvement approach. A double materiality analysis defines the reporting scope by assessing both environmental/social impacts and related financial risks and opportunities.

- Data sources and methodologies: Social and governance indicators rely on direct data across the value chain. Environmental metrics use indirect estimates, notably ADEME’s Footprint database (physical and monetary factors) for GHGs and methodologies for biodiversity footprinting.

- Uncertainty management: A single uncertainty figure is not feasible; uncertainty breakdowns are provided by scope elsewhere in the report. To improve accuracy, the Group prioritizes actual activity data and physical ratios, greater disclosure of financed companies’ emissions, and incorporation of physical biodiversity metrics.

- High-uncertainty areas: 
  - Scope 3 (Categories 1–2) GHGs use monetary factors on purchases/capex, with uncertainties in factors and account allocation.
  - Scope 3 (Category 15) financed emissions may use data provider models or PCAF sectoral factors, with model/factor uncertainties.
  - Portfolio biodiversity footprint uses Global Biodiversity Score based on sector/country exposures, with model/input data uncertainties.
  - Resource allocation to action plans relies on expert judgment, introducing allocation uncertainty.

- Historical data: Where 2023 entity-specific metrics exist, historical values are shown; methodological changes that revise 2023 figures are flagged at the metric level.

- No incorporation by reference: The sustainability report does not include information incorporated by reference.

- Governance integration: ESG is embedded in the Group’s dual governance (Executive Board and Supervisory Board). The Executive Board sets operational ESG guidelines; the Executive Committee implements them; the Sustainability Department and business lines deploy actions.

- Oversight and committees: The Supervisory Board, supported by specialized committees (Strategy & CSR, Risk, Financial Statements), oversees ESG strategy and the preparation of the sustainability report. An external Mission Committee (since 2021) advises annually to deepen the sustainability strategy.

- Roles in managing ESG IROs: The Supervisory Board handles strategic decisions on ESG impacts, risks, and opportunities; the Executive Board ensures collective alignment; the Executive Committee steers operational execution. Managers across functions own associated IROs.

nodes.title: Changes compared to previous reports
nodes.heading: 2.1.1.3 Changes compared to previous reports
nodes.start_phrase: The presentation and content of this report differ from previous years.
nodes.summary:
- Context and scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document under “Sustainable performance,” with a note to consult the glossary on page 808 for CSR terms.
- Reporting framework and changes: The sustainability report has been restructured to align with the EU CSRD and ESRS. A double materiality analysis was conducted to assess the Group’s environmental and social impacts as well as related financial risks and opportunities, informing the reporting scope. First-time ESRS application is pursued with a continuous improvement approach; historical values from 2023 are shown for certain entity‑specific metrics and are revised where methodological changes require it.
- Information incorporated by reference: None; the sustainability report is self-contained.
- Governance model: La Banque Postale operates with a dual structure—Executive (Management) Board and Supervisory Board—aimed at balanced oversight for stakeholders. ESG is embedded into core governance:
  - Executive Board manages the Group, relying on the Executive Committee to implement strategic and operational ESG guidelines, which are deployed by the Sustainability Department, business lines, and subsidiaries.
  - Supervisory Board oversees ESG strategies and actions via specialized committees. The Financial Statements Committee, in coordination with the Strategy and CSR Committee and the Risk Committee, monitors preparation of the sustainability report and presents it to the Supervisory Board.
  - An external Mission Committee (established 2021) reports annually to the Supervisory Board to enrich sustainability strategy discussions.
- Governance roles in ESG impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs): Responsibilities are clearly delineated:
  - Supervisory Board oversees strategic decisions on IROs, supported by specialized committees (including the Strategy and CSR Committee for target-setting).
  - Executive Board sets operational ESG guidelines and ensures collective alignment.
  - Executive Committee steers operational implementation of the ESG strategy.
  - Managers across relevant functions monitor related impacts, risks, and opportunities, as illustrated in an internal governance infographic.

nodes.title: Information incorporated by reference
nodes.heading: 2.1.1.4 Information incorporated by reference
nodes.start_phrase: No information has been incorporated by reference in the Group's sustainability report.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and standards: The sustainability reporting is aligned with the European CSRD and ESRS, representing the first year of ESRS application by La Banque Postale, with a continuous improvement approach.
- Double materiality: A double materiality analysis was conducted to assess the Group’s environmental and social impacts and the related financial risks and opportunities, which informed the reporting scope.
- Historical metrics: Entity-specific metrics from 2023 are included; where methodologies changed, 2023 figures were revised and disclosed alongside the relevant metrics.
- No incorporation by reference: The sustainability report does not incorporate external information by reference.
- Governance model: La Banque Postale operates a dual governance structure (Executive Board and Supervisory Board) to balance powers and integrate ESG into strategy and operations.
- ESG integration and oversight: 
  - Management/Executive Boards set and supervise ESG strategy and operational guidelines.
  - The Executive Committee steers implementation; the Sustainability Department, business lines, and subsidiaries execute rollout.
  - The Supervisory Board, supported by specialized committees (Strategy and CSR Committee, Risk Committee, and Financial Statements Committee), oversees ESG targets and the preparation of the sustainability report.
- External advisory: A Mission Committee, created in 2021, reports annually to the Supervisory Board to inform and enhance the sustainability strategy.
- Governance of impacts, risks, and opportunities: ESG IROs are fully embedded in governance; responsible managers oversee them. The Supervisory Board oversees IROs, the Executive Board sets operational ESG guidelines and ensures alignment, and the Executive Committee ensures operational execution.

nodes.title: Committed governance on sustainability issues - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.1.2 Committed governance on sustainability issues
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale is a French private limited company (société anonyme) with an Executive Board and a Supervisory Board.
nodes.summary: Overview of La Banque Postale’s ESG governance: the company operates a dual structure with an Executive/Management Board managing under a Supervisory Board to balance powers, and explicitly embeds ESG into group governance. The Executive Committee implements ESG-related operational and strategic guidelines, which are deployed by the Sustainability Department, business lines, and subsidiaries. The Supervisory Board oversees actions via specialized committees: the Strategy and CSR Committee, the Risk Committee, and the Financial Statements Committee, which monitors preparation of the sustainability report and presents it to the Supervisory Board. An external Mission Committee, created in 2021, reports annually to enrich discussions and strengthen the Group’s sustainability strategy. The section introduces governance’s role in managing ESG impacts, risks, and opportunities.

nodes.title: Role of governance in managing ESG impacts, risks and opportunities
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.1 Role of governance in managing ESG impacts, risks and opportunities
nodes.start_phrase: Sustainability matters, including impact, risk and opportunity management, are fully integrated into La Banque Postale’s governance.
nodes.summary:
- The report adopts the CSRD and ESRS frameworks for the first time, introduces a double materiality analysis, and defines a revised reporting scope. It follows a continuous improvement approach, provides historical values for certain entity-specific metrics, and flags any 2023 restatements due to methodology changes.
- No information is incorporated by reference.
- Governance integrates ESG at all levels within a dual structure (Executive Board and Supervisory Board). Specialized committees oversee key areas: Strategy & CSR (strategy and targets), Risk (ESG risk review), Financial Statements (sustainability reporting integrity), Remuneration (non-financial targets in variable pay), Appointments & Governance (board skills mix). An external Mission Committee advises annually.
- Clear allocation of responsibilities for managing ESG impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs):
  - Sustainability Department leads environmental strategy execution and transition plan.
  - Group Risk Department sets and monitors the ESG risk framework.
  - Compliance Department manages business conduct, ethics, and regulatory compliance.
  - HR oversees employee-related matters; Purchasing oversees value-chain workers.
  - Customers and affected communities are managed operationally across business lines.
- Internal control encompasses ESG risks via three lines of defense (operational/support/regulatory functions; permanent controls by Risk and Compliance; Internal Audit).
- 2024 IRO process: identification and assessment by Sustainability and Finance & Strategy with Group Risk, based on risk mapping; validation by Executive Committee and Executive Board; presentation to the Supervisory Board’s Strategy & CSR Committee and the Mission Committee; annual review from 2025.
- Target-setting and monitoring:
  - Certain impacts and all identified risks have targets, supervised by the Supervisory Board through annual risk appetite approval.
  - Executive Board oversees mission-led targets (notably ESRS E1, S3, S4); quarterly operational monitoring by a Steering Committee with audit trail.
  - Risk monitoring uses indicators and thresholds, managed by Group Risk and overseen by the Executive and Supervisory Boards.
  - A network of 244 ESG ambassadors (110 advisory, 134 volunteer) supports deployment across the Group.
- Conduct of business:
  - Responsible purchasing policy approved in 2023; Executive Board ensures consistent deployment and compliance with social, environmental, and contractual criteria.
  - Lobbying is guided and supervised by the Executive Board to ensure alignment with strategy, ethics, and regulations, under Supervisory Board oversight.
  - Ethics and anti-corruption systems are overseen by the Executive Board, with controls, training, and detection processes managed by the Ethics team and internal control functions.
  - The Executive Committee coordinates and validates priorities across suppliers, lobbying, and ethics/anti-corruption.
- Board competencies and training:
  - Skills mapping includes 16 criteria, with two ESG-focused; periodic self-assessments and an external review (2024) inform development.
  - As of 31 Dec 2024, 14/15 members have compliance/AML-CFT expertise and 11/15 have ESG/just transition expertise.
  - The Appointments & Governance Committee defines an annual training program for Supervisory Board members, supported by operational teams and external experts.

nodes.title: Skills and expertise of the Supervisory Board on sustainability issues
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.2 Skills and expertise of the Supervisory Board on sustainability issues
nodes.start_phrase: The skills and expertise of the Supervisory Board are regularly assessed and updated (additional information is available in Section 3.1.2.1.2 E “Information and training for the Supervisory Board members” of the Universal Registration Document).
nodes.summary:
- Governance and oversight of sustainability: Supervisory Board approves annual risk appetite and oversees risk management; Executive Board defines and monitors mission-led company targets tied to ESRS E1, S3, S4, presents them to the Supervisory Board via the Strategy and CSR Committee.
- Operational monitoring: A quarterly Steering Committee tracks ESG/mission metrics, reports to Internal Audit for mission report audit trail; Group Risk Department monitors risks using indicators and thresholds.
- ESG culture and engagement: A network of 244 ESG ambassadors (110 advisory ambassadors from Executive Committee sponsorship; 134 volunteer ambassadors) promotes ESG across business units.
- Responsible purchasing, lobbying, and ethics: Executive Board approved a responsible purchasing policy in 2023 with ESG criteria and oversees its deployment; supervises lobbying activities and reporting to ensure alignment with strategy, ethics, and regulation; oversees anti‑corruption and ethics frameworks, internal controls, training, and risk detection. Executive Committee coordinates across functions, validating strategic priorities.
- Supervisory Board skills and training: Skills mapping across 16 criteria (including two ESG) and periodic external reviews (in 2024) assess Board capabilities. As of 31 Dec 2024, 14/15 members have AML‑CFT expertise; 11/15 have ESG/just transition expertise.
- Ongoing ESG education: Annual ESG training since 2022; 2023 focused on CSRD; 2024 on biodiversity and the climate transition plan (impacts/dependencies on ecosystems, risk management, reporting, integration of biodiversity risks/opportunities, decarbonisation strategy, target setting and implementation). Additional ethics and code of conduct training provided in 2022–2023. ESG skills on governance bodies are being strengthened, supported by the Group’s mission-led culture.
- Composition and diversity of governance bodies: Supervisory Board has 15 members, including five employee representatives; each specialised committee includes at least one employee representative. Executive Board has three members (since 25 Jan 2024). Emphasis on diversity, gender balance, and independence (at least one‑third independent; a lead independent member helps prevent and manage conflicts of interest).
- Gender metrics: Among Executive and Supervisory Board members (excluding employee representatives), women represent 46.15% and men 53.85%; gender diversity ratio on the Supervisory Board is 50% women (employee representatives excluded per regulation).

nodes.title: Management and supervisory bodies
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.3 Management and supervisory bodies
nodes.start_phrase: The Supervisory Board has 15 members.
nodes.summary:
- Focus of section: Governance and oversight of sustainability (ESG/CSR) at La Banque Postale, within the 2024 Universal Registration Document (ESRS 2 context), including training, board composition, expertise, decision processes, materiality integration, and remuneration alignment.

- ESG training and culture:
  - Since 2022, annual ESG training for governance bodies; 2023 focused on CSRD; 2024 on biodiversity and the climate transition plan.
  - 2024 topics: Climate & Nature report; assessing ecosystem impacts/dependencies; managing and reporting biodiversity risks/opportunities; decarbonisation strategy and implementation.
  - 2022–2023 ethics and code of conduct training for Supervisory and Executive Boards.
  - ESG skills on boards are being strengthened; mission-led corporate culture supports focus on impacts, risks, and opportunities.

- Management and supervisory bodies:
  - Supervisory Board: 15 members, incl. 5 employee representatives; ensures at least one-third independent members per Afep‑Medef; appoints a lead independent member to prevent/manage conflicts of interest.
  - Executive Board: 3 members since 25 January 2024.
  - Gender diversity: 46.15% women (Exec + Supervisory Boards, excluding employee reps); Supervisory Board gender diversity ratio 50% (excluding employee reps).
  - Independence: 40% of Supervisory Board members are independent (excluding employee reps).
  - Board expertise: Strong banking/financial sector knowledge across members, including independent experts and long-tenured employee representatives.

- Integration of CSR and sustainability into governance:
  - Sustainability Department oversees due diligence for identifying impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs) and tracks effectiveness of policies, actions, metrics, and targets.
  - Update cadence: Scopes 1–2 annually; Scope 3 semiannually for La Banque Postale SA.
  - Regular governance touchpoints:
    - Supervisory Board: climate strategy at least twice yearly.
    - Management Board: reviews/adapts climate and nature strategies at least twice yearly.
    - Mission Committee: climate discussed at each meeting (≥3 per year).
    - Executive Committee: climate and nature on agenda at least monthly.
    - Group Risk Steering Committee: monthly.
  - CNP Assurances: Executive Committee, CSR Committee, Audit & Risk Committee, and Board receive updates on significant IROs and the transition plan; CSR Committee met five times in 2024.
  - 88% of material IROs from double materiality analysis already embedded in the updated “La Banque Postale 2030” strategic plan; IROs list referenced elsewhere in the document.

- Remuneration and sustainability:
  - Remuneration framework aligned with Afep‑Medef and the 3 November 2014 Order (ACPR supervision); detailed in the Universal Registration Document.
  - Supervisory Board remuneration is fixed (attendance/responsibilities-based) and not linked to climate targets.

nodes.title: CSR and sustainability issues taken into account by governance bodies
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.4 CSR and sustainability issues taken into account by governance bodies
nodes.start_phrase: During quarterly Steering Committee meetings, the Sustainability Department ensures the implementation of due diligence for the identification of the Group's IROs as well as the results and effectiveness of policies, actions, metrics and targets in relation thereto.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on sustainability governance under ESRS 2, within La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document
- Supervisory Board expertise: deep banking/financial sector knowledge via executive roles at La Poste/Caisse des Dépôts, independent members’ senior experience in finance/insurance, and employee representatives with long tenure across business lines and internal control
- Governance integration of CSR and sustainability issues: the Sustainability Department leads due diligence on IROs and tracks policy effectiveness; Scope 1–2 decarbonization pathway updated annually; Scope 3 pathway updated semi-annually for LBP SA
- Regular oversight cadence:
  - Supervisory Board: climate strategy at least twice a year
  - Management Board: reviews/adapts climate and nature strategies at least twice a year
  - Mission Committee: climate at every meeting (≥3 per year)
  - Executive Committee: climate and nature monthly
  - Group Risk Steering Committee: monthly
- CNP Assurances governance: Executive Committee, CSR Committee, Audit and Risk Committee, and Board of Directors monitor significant impacts, risks, opportunities, due diligence, transition plan, and performance; CSR Committee met five times in 2024
- Integration with strategy: 88% of material IROs from double materiality analysis already embedded in the “La Banque Postale 2030” strategic plan; significant IROs tracked in dedicated tables (Section 2.1.3.2)
- Remuneration alignment framework: policy prepared per Afep‑Medef Code and French ACPR internal control requirements; details in Section 3.2
- Supervisory Board remuneration: fixed, not linked to climate targets; amounts reflect responsibilities and attendance
- Supervisory Board independence rate: 40% (excluding employee representatives)

nodes.title: Alignment of remuneration with La Banque Postale's sustainability targets
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.5 Alignment of remuneration with La Banque Postale's sustainability targets
nodes.start_phrase: Lastly, to frame its remuneration policy, La Banque Postale has adopted principles and rules determining the remuneratio n of corporate officers, based on the work of its Remuneration Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Governance and expertise: Composition and competencies of La Banque Postale’s Supervisory Board, highlighting deep sector knowledge from La Poste/Caisse des Dépôts, independent members’ financial-sector backgrounds, and long-tenured employee representatives; Supervisory Board independence rate of 40% (excluding employee reps).

- ESG oversight by governance bodies: Regular, structured monitoring of climate and sustainability topics across the Supervisory Board (at least twice yearly), Management Board (at least twice yearly), Mission Committee (each meeting), Executive Committee (monthly), and Group Risk Steering Committee (monthly). Sustainability Department leads due diligence and IRO monitoring; Scope 1–2 low‑carbon pathway updated annually and Scope 3 semiannually for LBP SA.

- CNP Assurances governance: Executive Committee, CSR Committee, Audit and Risk Committee, and Board informed on significant impacts, risks and opportunities; CSR Committee met five times in 2024.

- Integration of material IROs: Due diligence outputs feed the transition plan; 88% of material IROs already embedded in the updated “La Banque Postale 2030” strategic plan; detailed IRO lists referenced elsewhere in the document.

- Remuneration alignment with sustainability:
  - Policy framework aligned with Afep‑Medef Code and ACPR requirements.
  - Supervisory Board: fixed remuneration not tied to climate targets; amounts reflect responsibilities and attendance.
  - Executive Board: 15% of annual variable pay tied to ESG criteria—5% accessible banking mission; 5% climate target (SBTi/NZBA alignment with the Paris Agreement, mission target 3.4); 5% progress of the sustainability programme. Performance assessed by the Supervisory Board with criterion scores from 0–120%, overall capped at 100%, and trigger thresholds for financial criteria.
  - Employee remuneration: Growing weight of non‑financial criteria; target 40% ESG weighting in individual variable pay by 2030 across banking and insurance; collective profit‑sharing set 50% on non‑financial indicators.

- 2024 sustainability programme milestones: Establish governance for non‑financial (ESG) data; implement climate pathway management systems for coverage and trading per SBTi/NZBA; deploy Impact Weighting Factor (IWF) in asset/project financing and commercial real estate; frame ESG processes for public sector, social economy and large corporates; publish sustainability and Climate & Nature reports.

- Due diligence framework:
  - Governance and strategy integration: Half‑yearly/quarterly committees oversee duty of care across subsidiaries and operations; purchasing governed by a dedicated policy and sectoral exclusions; employee-related topics (psychosocial risks, equal opportunities, occupational health) included; mandatory ESG analysis for all new offers; IWF progressively rolled out to measure CIB transaction impacts.
  - Entity‑specific approaches: CNP Assurances’ due diligence by specialist sustainability officers with stakeholder input and CSR Committee oversight (covering suppliers, M&A, and investments). LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier apply the GREaT ESG methodology, exclusions, and shareholder engagement; Louvre Banque Privée uses sectoral exclusions and ESG selection rules.
  - Stakeholder engagement: Responsible purchasing, human rights commitments, and ESG/climate questionnaires in credit activities; shareholder engagement via LBP AM.
  - Identification and assessment of negative impacts: Use of Responsible Purchasing Charter, risk mapping, due diligence plan/policy, supplier assessments (own operations); IWF, exclusion policies, and Responsible Financing & Investment Charter (credit/investments). At CNP Assurances, engagement and exclusions plus ESG-based selection aim to prevent environmental (climate, biodiversity), ethical (anticorruption, AML/CTF), and social (human rights, anti‑discrimination) harms.

nodes.title: Due diligence procedures
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.6 Due diligence procedures
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group is implementing a structured process of due diligence to ensure that ESG issues are integrated into its activities.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s ESRS 2 disclosures on sustainable performance, covering ESG-linked remuneration, due diligence, cross-functional tools, and ESG risk management.

- ESG-linked remuneration:
  - Individual variable pay includes a significant ESG component, excluding financial results; ambition to raise non-financial weighting to 40% across banking and insurance by 2030.
  - Collective profit-sharing: 50% tied to non-financial indicators.

- Due diligence framework (Group, subsidiaries, and value chains):
  - Governance and strategic integration: dedicated committees (half-yearly/quarterly), purchasing policy and sectoral exclusions, mandatory ESG analysis for new offers, Impact Weighting Factor (IWF) rollout, and entity-specific procedures (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, La Financière de l’Échiquier, Louvre Banque Privée).
  - Stakeholder engagement: responsible purchasing, human rights and standards commitments, climate/ESG questionnaires in credit, shareholder engagement (LBP AM).
  - Identification and assessment of negative impacts: tools include responsible purchasing charters, risk mapping, due diligence plans, supplier assessments; financing and investment governed by IWF, exclusion policies, and Responsible Financing and Investment Charter; CNP applies ESG-based selection, exclusions, and engagement to prevent environmental, ethical, and social harms.
  - Corrective actions and follow-up: exclusion policies, engagement programs, responsible purchasing and supplier compliance frameworks; responsible purchasing policies at CNP Assurances and LBP AM.
  - Monitoring and communication: regular public reporting (Group and subsidiaries, SRI policies, SFRD statements); objective is full ESG integration with training and reporting.

- Cross-functional levers and tools (deployed across stages of due diligence):
  - Governance and policies: duty of care framework; multiple CSR/due diligence committees.
  - Product/service assessment: ESG checklist (credit), IWF, GREaT rating methodology, specific climate/sustainability questionnaires.
  - Risk mapping and assessment: human rights and environmental risk mapping; retail customer risk assessment.
  - Commitment and investment: ESG/responsible investment charters; M&A sustainability due diligence; exclusion policies (regulatory, standards-based, sectoral—e.g., coal, oil & gas, deforestation, biodiversity—, and GREaT-related); ESG-based selection; shareholder engagement/dialogue.
  - Purchasing: responsible purchasing policies/charters/manuals; supplier assessments (Provigis, Ellipro, IndueD, EcoVadis); Supplier Relations and Responsible Purchasing label.
  - Customer engagement: product suitability reviews and satisfaction surveys.
  - Communication and training: ESG/SFDR publications; duty of care e-learning.

- ESG risk management and internal control:
  - Integrated governance and risk framework with dedicated committees; ESG risks embedded in risk appetite and three lines of defense; regular internal control disclosures.
  - ESG risk identification via a Group-wide risk map, updated annually; criticality scored 1–4; ESG risk classified as “major”; uses existing and dedicated measurement systems.
  - Material ESG risks for CSRD: environmental (physical and transition climate risks; nature-related risks currently non-material), social/societal (employment, health & safety; customer protection; assessment failures), governance (internal governance failures).
  - Mitigation: sector policies, process adjustments, strengthened controls; links to decarbonization and employee action plans.
  - Oversight and reporting: Supervisory and Executive Boards integrate ESG into strategy and risk; regular briefings; monthly reporting to Executive Committee and Group Risk Management Committee.

nodes.title: Risk management and internal control
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.7 Risk management and internal control
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has set up a global governance and risk management system, for which additional information is available in Section 6.3 “Risk management framework” of the Universal Registration Document.
nodes.summary:
- Describes La Banque Postale Group’s global governance and risk management system for ESG, integrated into decision-making, risk appetite, and committee processes, and aligned with a three-lines-of-defence internal control model.
- Explains the ESG risk identification process, drawing on external environment, business portfolio, internal operations, strategic priorities, and stakeholder/NGO input.
- Details an annual Group-wide ESG risk mapping methodology that assesses criticality via combined impact and frequency on a 1–4 scale (minor to critical); ESG risk is currently rated “major,” using both existing (operational, compliance) and dedicated measurement systems.
- Links ESG risk mapping to the CSRD double materiality analysis and the identification of material impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs).
- Lists main ESG risk categories used in materiality analysis:
  - Environmental: physical and transition climate risks; nature-related physical and transition risks currently deemed non-material.
  - Social/societal: risks related to employment, health and safety; customer protection failure; assessment failures concerning customers and stakeholders.
  - Governance: failures in internal governance.
- Outlines mitigation measures: decarbonization levers and action plans; employee action plans and resources; sector-specific policies; process reviews/adjustments; and strengthened control and monitoring arrangements.
- States that risk-mapping results feed the risk monitoring system and management framework, triggering remedial plans for potential impacts.
- Confirms strong oversight by the Supervisory and Executive Boards, which integrate ESG into strategy, targets, and risk frameworks; they receive regular briefings, with monthly reports sent to the Executive Committee and the Group Risk Management Committee.

nodes.title: Risk management and internal control system
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.7.1 Risk management and internal control system
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has set up a global governance and risk management system, for which additional information is available in Section 6.3 “Risk management framework” of the Universal Registration Document.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale Group’s ESG-integrated risk management and internal control framework within the 2024 Universal Registration Document (ESRS 2; GOV_5_01–GOV_5_05).
- Governance and system design: A groupwide governance and risk management system embeds ESG into decision-making via dedicated committees and risk appetite; monitoring follows the three lines of defense model; internal control and risk framework detailed in referenced sections.
- ESG risk identification: Built on analyses of external environment, business portfolio, internal operations, and strategy, incorporating inputs from civil society and NGOs; consolidated in a Group ESG risk map updated annually.
- Risk assessment methodology: Common Group-wide methodology combining impact and frequency; criticality rated 1–4 (minor to critical); ESG risk currently qualified as “major”; leverages existing risk measurement systems and dedicated tools.
- Materiality linkage: ESG risks feed the CSRD double materiality analysis; material impacts, risks, and opportunities detailed elsewhere in the document.
- Main ESG risk categories:
  - Environmental: Physical and transition climate risks; nature-related physical and transition risks currently deemed non-material.
  - Social/societal: Risks related to employment, health and safety; customer protection failures; assessment failures concerning customers and stakeholders.
  - Governance: Failures in the Group’s internal governance.
- Mitigation and controls: Actions include sector policies, process reviews/adjustments, and strengthened controls/monitoring; specific action plans for decarbonization and employee resources referenced; mapping results feed ongoing risk monitoring and remedial planning.
- Oversight and reporting: Supervisory and Executive Boards integrate ESG into strategy, targets, and risk management; receive regular briefings; monthly reporting provided to the Executive Committee and Group Risk Management Committee.
- Cross-references: Sections 6.3, 4.6, 6.3.2, 6.8.3, 6.8.3.2, 2.1.3.2, 2.2.1.5, and 2.3.1.5 for detailed frameworks, mapping, and action plans.

nodes.title: Risks identified and risk mitigation strategy
nodes.heading: 2.1.2.7.2 Risks identified and risk mitigation strategy
nodes.start_phrase: The risks identified in the risk map have been included in La Banque Postale Group's double materiality analysis.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines La Banque Postale Group’s ESG-integrated risk management and internal control framework under ESRS 2, embedded in Group governance and decision-making, aligned with a three-lines-of-defence model, and covered by dedicated committees and reporting.
- Describes the process for identifying ESG risks: annual Group-wide ESG risk mapping informed by external environment, portfolio, operations, strategy, and civil society/NGO input; criticality assessed on a 1–4 scale; ESG risk deemed “major”; measurement leverages existing and dedicated systems.
- Summarizes key ESG risks used in the CSRD double materiality analysis:
  - Environmental: physical and transition climate risks; nature-related risks currently non-material.
  - Social/societal: employment/health/safety, customer protection, and stakeholder assessment failures.
  - Governance: internal governance failures.
- Explains mitigation approach: actions embedded in decarbonization and employee plans, sector policies, internal process reviews, and enhanced controls; outputs feed the risk monitoring system and remedial planning.
- Details governance oversight: Supervisory and Executive Boards integrate ESG into strategy, targets, and risk appetite; receive regular briefings; monthly reporting to the Executive Committee and Group Risk Management Committee.
- Presents the Group’s “just transition” strategy and business model: sustainable profitability via diversified bancassurance (retail, consumer finance, CNP Assurances, international), corporate and investment banking (public sector, social economy), and wealth/asset management; supported by mission-led DNA, accessible banking mandate, regional presence, partners, and strong financial profile; value creation for customers, regions, planet, employees, NGOs, and shareholders.
- Covers products and services: comprehensive, inclusive banking and insurance offerings; solutions for a sustainable economy (green financing, responsible savings); stewardship of the State’s accessible banking mission for vulnerable groups.
- Notes strategic portfolio moves: 2024 divestment of KissKissBankBank and Lendopolis to refocus on core banking while maintaining impact via partnerships; Lendopolis’ integration with Lendosphere to form a European leader in energy-transition crowdfunding.
- States responsible finance exclusions: no market-prohibited products, but strict stance on high-risk sectors; excludes fossil fuel financing and projects expanding air traffic (with safety/standards/efficiency exceptions); applies a Responsible Financing and Investment Charter excluding sensitive sectors and companies with serious or repeated ESG controversies.

nodes.title: A strategy for the just transition
nodes.heading: 2.1.3 A strategy for the just transition
nodes.start_phrase: The Group’s business model is based on sustainable profitability which supports the just transition.
nodes.summary: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance, ESRS 2) outlining its “just transition” strategy and business model. It details a sustainability-driven, diversified bancassurance model (retail via CNP Assurances and Consumer Finance, international bancassurance via CNP, corporate and investment banking for public sector/social economy/companies/financial institutions, and wealth/asset management through Louvre Banque Privée, LBP AM, Tocqueville Finance, La Financière de l’Échiquier). Strategic pillars include tailored customer solutions, positive-impact products, a learning culture, omnichannel digital experience, inclusive bancassurance leadership, and diversification for resilience. The Group’s resources (mission-led status, accessible banking mandate, backing of La Poste Group/Caisse des Dépôts, regional presence, people, partner network, solid/low-risk financial profile) enable value creation through support for the just transition, financial inclusion, employee development, regional financing, environmental action, NGO collaboration, and strengthened shareholder trust. The products/services section highlights comprehensive retail and business banking plus life/personal/P&C insurance, the State-entrusted accessible banking mission, and expanded inclusive/sustainable offerings (green financing, responsible savings). It also notes 2024 divestments of KissKissBankBank and Lendopolis to refocus on core banking while sustaining impact via partnerships (KKBB’s integration and sale to Ulule; Lendopolis’ transfer to Lendosphere creating a European leader in energy-transition crowdfunding). The responsible financing policy excludes fossil fuel financing and projects that increase air traffic (with safety/standards/efficiency exceptions) and applies a Responsible Financing and Investment Charter that restricts exposure to sensitive sectors and companies with serious or repeated ESG controversies.

nodes.title: Group business model and value chain
nodes.heading: 2.1.3.1 Group business model and value chain
nodes.start_phrase: The Group’s business model is based on sustainable profitability which supports the just transition.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines La Banque Postale Group’s ESRS 2-aligned sustainability reporting context and its strategy for a just transition.
- Describes a business model built on sustainable profitability across French and international bancassurance (notably via CNP Assurances), corporate and investment banking for public/social economy and institutions, and wealth/asset management (Louvre Banque Privée, LBP AM, Tocqueville Finance, La Financière de l’Échiquier).
- Strategic pillars: personalized customer solutions, positive-impact products, becoming a learning company, omnichannel digital experience, leading inclusive bancassurance for all, and diversification for resilience.
- Key resources: mission-led “sustainability DNA” (incl. accessible banking mission and ties to La Poste Group/Caisse des Dépôts), regional presence, employees, partner network, strong financial and low-risk profile.
- Value creation goals: enable customers’ just transition, banking/insurance inclusion, employee training/engagement, regional financing, environmental action, collaboration with charities/NGOs, and reinforcing shareholder confidence.
- Products/services: full bancassurance offering for retail and business clients; stewardship of the State’s accessible banking mission ensuring universal access to essential services; development of inclusive products and just transition solutions (green financing, responsible savings, offers tailored to individual and company projects).
- Portfolio actions: divestment of crowdfunding units KissKissBankBank and Lendopolis to refocus on core banking while maintaining sustainability impact via partnerships—KKBB integrated with Ulule; Lendopolis acquired by Lendosphere, forming a European leader in energy-transition crowdfunding.
- Risk and exclusions: no products outright prohibited by markets, but strict vigilance on high-sustainability-risk sectors; exclusions include fossil fuel financing and projects expanding air traffic capacity (with exceptions for safety, compliance, and energy-efficiency upgrades).
- Governance: a Responsible Financing and Investment Charter guides lending/investment, excluding sensitive sectors and companies with serious or repeated ESG controversies.

nodes.title: Business model
nodes.heading: 2.1.3.1.1 Business model
nodes.start_phrase: The Group’s business model is based on sustainable profitability which supports the just transition.
nodes.summary:
- Context: ESRS 2 sustainability reporting framework; strategy for a just transition.
- Business model: Sustainable profitability anchored in bancassurance (retail in France via CNP Assurances and Consumer Finance; international via CNP Assurances), corporate and investment banking serving public sector, social economy, companies and FIs, plus wealth and asset management (Louvre Banque Privée, LBP AM, Tocqueville Finance, La Financière de l’Échiquier).
- Strategic pillars: tailored customer solutions; positive-impact products; learning organization; digital/omnichannel experience; inclusive best-in-class bancassurance; diversification for resilience.
- Key resources: mission-led DNA including an accessible banking mandate; backing of La Poste Group and Caisse des Dépôts; regional footprint in France and abroad; employees; partner network; robust financial and low-risk profile.
- Value creation objectives: enable customer participation in the just transition; banking/insurance inclusion; employee training and engagement; regional financing; environmental action; collaboration with NGOs/charities; reinforce shareholder confidence.
- Products and services: comprehensive retail and business offerings spanning traditional banking and diversified insurance (life, personal, property and liability). Accessible banking mission guarantees essential services for vulnerable groups.
- Mission-led transformation: integration of social, environmental and regional targets; rollout of inclusive products, green financing, responsible savings, and solutions supporting a sustainable economy for individuals and companies.
- Portfolio update (2024): sale of KissKissBankBank and Lendopolis; KKBB continues cultural/social crowdfunding within Ulule; Lendopolis acquired by Lendosphere, creating a European leader in energy-transition crowdfunding; Group refocuses on core banking while sustaining positive impacts via partnerships.
- Responsible financing and exclusions: no products prohibited by market, but strict vigilance on high-sustainability-risk sectors. Excludes financing of fossil fuels and projects that increase air traffic (with exceptions for safety, compliance, and energy efficiency). A Responsible Financing and Investment Charter guides financing/investment and excludes sensitive sectors or companies with serious/repeated ESG controversies.

nodes.title: Products and services
nodes.heading: 2.1.3.1.2 Products and services
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group continues to strengthen its positioning as a committed bancassurance player, offering a comprehensive range of products and services tailored to the needs of its retail customers and to business customers.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (sustainable performance, ESRS 2), detailing its strategy for a just transition, business model, product offering, and responsible financing policies.

- Business model and value creation:
  - Growth drivers: French bancassurance (retail banking, CNP Assurances, consumer finance), international bancassurance via CNP Assurances, corporate and investment banking (public sector, social economy, corporates, financial institutions), and wealth/asset management (Louvre Banque Privée, LBP AM, Tocqueville Finance, La Financière de l’Échiquier).
  - Strategic priorities: tailored customer solutions, positive-impact products, becoming a learning company, digital/omnichannel experience, leadership in inclusive bancassurance, and diversification for resilience.
  - Key resources: mission-led “sustainability DNA,” accessible banking mandate, backing of La Poste Group/Caisse des Dépôts, regional presence, employees, partner network, and strong/low-risk financial profile.
  - Value outcomes: enabling customers’ just transition, financial inclusion in banking/insurance, employee training and engagement, regional financing, environmental action, collaboration with charities/NGOs, and strengthening shareholder trust.

- Products and services:
  - Comprehensive retail and business offerings: traditional banking plus life, personal, and property & liability insurance.
  - Accessible banking mission ensuring universal, non-discriminatory access for vulnerable groups.
  - Mission-led integration of social, environmental, and regional targets: inclusive products, green financing, responsible savings, and solutions for individuals’ and companies’ transition projects.
  - Portfolio streamlining: 2024 sale of KissKissBankBank (to Ulule) and Lendopolis (to Lendosphere), creating a European leader in energy-transition crowdfunding while refocusing on core banking and maintaining impact via partnerships.

- Prohibited/restricted activities and jurisdictions:
  - No products prohibited by market, but strict exclusions for high-sustainability-risk sectors.
  - Excludes financing of fossil fuels and projects increasing air traffic capacity (exceptions for safety, compliance, energy efficiency).
  - No operations in EU-designated non-cooperative tax jurisdictions; offers in such countries require Tax Department approval.
  - Exclusion list for sovereigns based on corruption, tax policy, and fundamental rights concerns.
  - Defence sector principles (effective 1 July 2024): excludes all weapons/equipment banned by international conventions/EU rules and related actors.
  - Deforestation policy (effective 1 January 2024): excludes operators/traders in coffee, cocoa, rubber, palm oil, soy, cattle, and timber unless they have a recognized no-deforestation policy, aligned with Caisse des Dépôts biodiversity policy.

- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter:
  - Purpose: embeds ESG considerations in lending and investment; complements sector policies and risk frameworks.
  - Two pillars:
    - Exclusions: sensitive sectors (e.g., tobacco; controversial/banned/unconventional weapons; pornography; gambling; pesticides; fur; animal testing). Sovereigns excluded if tax havens or weak on political/civil rights, workers’ rights, press freedom, and corruption.
    - Controversy management: aligns with UNGPs, ILO conventions, OECD Guidelines; pre-investment checks against an exclusion list overseen by a Controversies and Exclusion Committee (quarterly reviews); responses include supervision, engagement, or exclusion from the CIB portfolio if unresolved.
  - Implementation: dedicated internal procedures; Sustainability Department training and dissemination; Charter publicly available.
  - Scope: currently applies mainly to Corporate and Local Development Banking; not yet to French/foreign bancassurance or Wealth & Asset Management activities.

- Overall emphasis: integration of ESG into strategy and operations to support a just transition, financial inclusion, and regional development, coupled with robust exclusion and controversy management frameworks to mitigate financial, legal, and reputational risks.

nodes.title: Products and services - Introduction
nodes.heading: 2.1.3.1.2 Products and services
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group continues to strengthen its positioning as a committed bancassurance player, offering a comprehensive range of products and services tailored to the needs of its retail customers and to business customers.
nodes.summary: Overview of La Banque Postale Group’s bancassurance model and mission-led strategy: the Group provides traditional banking plus life, personal, and property/liability insurance to retail and business customers, and fulfills a State-entrusted accessible banking mission for vulnerable groups. It integrates social, environmental, and regional targets via inclusive products, green financing, and responsible savings. In 2024 it sold the business assets of crowdfunding platforms KissKissBankBank (subsequently taken over by Ulule) and Lendopolis (acquired 100% by Lendosphere to create a European energy-transition crowdfunding leader), refocusing on core banking while maintaining sustainability partnerships. The Group states no products are market-prohibited but applies strict exclusions and risk controls: no financing of fossil fuels or infrastructure that increases air traffic (except for safety, compliance, or energy-efficiency upgrades); a Responsible Financing and Investment Charter excluding sensitive sectors and companies with serious or repeated ESG controversies; prohibitions on operating in EU-listed non-cooperative tax jurisdictions with Tax Department approval required for offers; a country exclusion list for sovereign investments over corruption, tax, or basic rights concerns; clarified defence-sector rules effective 1 July 2024 excluding all weapons/equipment banned by international conventions or EU rules and related actors; and an anti-deforestation commitment effective 1 January 2024, aligned with Caisse des Dépôts, excluding financing/investment in coffee, cocoa, rubber, palm oil, soya, cattle, and timber operators/traders without a recognized no-deforestation policy.

nodes.title: La Banque Postale’s Financing and Investment Charter
nodes.heading:
La Banque Postale ’s Financing 
and Investment Charter
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale’s Responsible Financing and Investment Charter embodies the Bank’s commitment to sustainable and community-minded finance.
nodes.summary:
- Section context: Part of La Banque Postale’s sustainable performance and ESRS 2 sustainability reporting framework.
- Risk and compliance stance: Prohibits operations in EU-listed non-cooperative tax jurisdictions; offers there require Tax Department approval. Maintains a list of countries excluded from sovereign investments due to corruption, tax policy, or fundamental rights concerns. Clarifies defence-sector intervention principles and excludes all weapons/equipment banned by international conventions or EU rules.
- Deforestation and biodiversity: From 1 January 2024, a commitment strategy to combat deforestation; aligns with Caisse des Dépôts’ biodiversity policy. Excludes financing/investment in operators and traders in coffee, cocoa, rubber, palm oil, soya, cattle, and timber unless they have a recognized deforestation-prevention policy.
- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: Embeds ESG into lending/investment decisions via two pillars—exclusions and ESG controversy management.
  - Exclusions: Sensitive sectors (tobacco; controversial/banned/unconventional weapons; pornography; gambling; pesticides; fur; animal testing). Sovereign exclusions include tax havens or weak scores on political/civil liberties, workers’ rights, press freedom, and corruption.
  - Controversy management: Guided by UNGPs, ILO core conventions, and OECD Guidelines. A Controversies and Exclusion Committee updates a validated exclusion list quarterly; sources include public info, data providers, and counterparties. Procedure allows supervision, engagement, or exclusion if issues persist.
  - Implementation and scope: Governed by internal procedures; Sustainability Department ensures dissemination and understanding. Applies primarily to Corporate and Local Development Banking; not yet to bancassurance (France/abroad) or Wealth and Asset Management.
- Customer segments and propositions:
  - Public sector and social economy: Financing to local authorities and public hospitals via SFIL/CAFFIL for infrastructure and medical equipment; Hippocad supports local social action.
  - Corporates: Supports SMEs to large listed firms with tailored financing for productive investment, tech/ecological/social innovation, and energy transition; focus on climate-exposed sectors and strategic industries.
  - Financial institutions: Provides investment activities, structured financing, securities lending/borrowing, hedging, and cash management.
  - Retail customers: Serves 10.1 million active customers with nationwide accessibility (17,000 outlets, incl. 7,000 post offices); 647,000 new customers in 2024; 26% growth in complementary product sales.
  - Policyholders: Integration of CNP Assurances creates an integrated bancassurer offering life, retirement, personal risk, and protection, serving over 30 million personal risk/protection and 14 million savings/retirement policyholders in Europe and Latin America.

nodes.title: Breakdown of own workers and income
nodes.heading: 2.1.3.1.4 Breakdown of own workers and income
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group is not considered to be a company active in the fossil fuel sector, given its financing, investment and insurance business, in accordance with the list defined by the regulations.

- Context and scope: Excerpts from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document under “Sustainable performance” and ESRS 2, covering breakdowns of income and workforce, sectoral exclusions, and sustainability strategy/targets.
- Sectoral exclusions and zero revenues: The Group is not active in fossil fuels, chemical production, controversial/prohibited weapons, or tobacco growing. It reports zero revenues from these sectors (including coal, oil, gas, and tobacco cultivation) and applies fossil fuel exclusion policies outlined in its Responsible Financing and Investment Charter.
- Income definition and amount: Total income (aligned with the French Monetary and Financial Code definition of net turnover) aggregates interest, fees/commissions, gains on financial instruments, reinsurance items, and other operating income; reported at €41,100 million.
- Workforce breakdown: 14,512 own workers, with 12,204 in France, 670 in Europe (excl. France), and 1,638 in the Rest of the World.
- References to climate risk and reporting: Additional details on climate transition risk indicators appear elsewhere in the URD; disclosures reference ESRS 2 and specific SBM metrics.
- Mission, purpose, and governance: As a mission-led company, La Banque Postale articulates a purpose centered on social inclusion, regional development, and planetary boundaries. CNP Assurances (part of the Group) embeds its company purpose in its Articles of Association, with stakeholder commitments and monitoring indicators; it is positioned as a major green investor within the Caisse des Dépôts ecosystem.
- Sustainability targets and integration: By 2025, targets include 80% of new offers classified as sustainable via an ESG checklist and assessment of 87% of the Bank’s technical reserves using the Impact Weighting Factor (IWF).
- ESG in product innovation: ESG criteria are integrated into product design across Retail, Corporate, and Local Development Banking using common tools (ESG checklist; green/social/sustainable bond framework).
- Examples of “just transition” offerings: 
  - Financing for social home ownership and energy renovation (e.g., PAS loans, zero-interest eco-loan, Avance Rénovation, impact real estate loans) and green personal loans.
  - Community finance and solidarity products (SIS; LBP AM SRI Human Rights and Actions Solidaire funds).
  - SRI-labelled and ESG-screened savings solutions; transition-focused funds (e.g., Tocqueville Environnement SRI) and green bond issues.
  - Free services supporting customers’ carbon footprint tracking (Carbo) and youth financial inclusion (Youth Pass).

nodes.title: Sustainability strategy and targets
nodes.heading: 2.1.3.1.5 Sustainability strategy and targets
nodes.start_phrase: As a mission-led company, La Banque Postale is committed to meeting social, environmental and regional challenges.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and framework: Part of La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document on sustainable performance and ESRS 2 reporting, referencing exclusion principles in the Responsible Financing and Investment Charter and a glossary of CSR terms.
- Mission-led purpose: La Banque Postale’s company purpose centers on just transition, inclusion, and planetary boundaries; CNP Assurances’ purpose emphasizes responsible insurance/investment and an inclusive, sustainable society, embedded in its Articles of Association.
