The proprietary GREaT methodology—covering Governance, Resources (natural and human), Energy transition, and Territorial development—assesses issuers on topics including product/service quality and safety, data privacy, consumer relationships, access to essential services, and human rights. It is applied to all asset classes, assigns SRI scores to roughly 12,000 companies, and feeds quantitative selection thresholds audited for SRI certification. A GREaT Committee oversees engagement and exclusion policies and makes exclusion decisions.

The text also positions impact finance as a core strategic pillar addressed across the Group’s double materiality analysis. It references monitoring indicators and links them to climate action (E1), regional and community commitments (S3), and consumer/end-user interests (S4). Impact finance IROs span:
- Negative impacts: environmental and social harms from financed activities; potential customer detriment from inadequate insurance.
- Positive impacts: sustainable/positive-impact financing; improved access to bancassurance for all customers including vulnerable groups; enhanced working conditions in the downstream value chain.
- Opportunities: growth in sustainable finance markets and new business openings.
- Risks: portfolio exposure to physical and transition climate risks.
The section emphasizes exemplary management of financing and investments, proactive mitigation of environmental and social impacts, voluntary positive-impact actions, market development, and business model resilience.

nodes.title: Material IROs related to impact finance
nodes.heading: 2.1.6.3 Material IROs related to impact finance
nodes.start_phrase: The theme of impact finance is one of the pillars of La Banque Postale Group’s strategy, and is therefore present across all scopes of the double materiality analysis.
nodes.summary:
- The excerpt is from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance section) and aligns with ESRS 2 on sustainability reporting preparation.
- It identifies impact finance as a core strategic pillar embedded across the Group’s double materiality analysis, covering financing of environmental solutions, the social economy, and support for vulnerable customers.
- It references specific material impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs) tied to impact finance, with details elsewhere in the report (Section 2.1.3.2).
- The IROs span:
  - Governance and management: exemplary management of financing and investments; awareness and limitation of environmental and social impacts.
  - Negative impacts: potential environmental/social harm from financed activities; risks to customers from inadequate insurance coverage.
  - Positive impacts: intentional investments for environmental and social benefits; improved access to bancassurance (including for vulnerable groups) and regional coverage; sustainable/positive-impact financing; promoting favorable working conditions in the downstream value chain.
  - Opportunities: opening new markets and business lines, particularly in sustainable finance.
  - Risks/resilience: portfolio exposure to physical and transition climate risks; building business model resilience.
- It introduces monitoring indicators for the Group’s impact finance commitments, with measurement and disclosure linked to:
  - E1: Combating and adapting to climate change (Section 2.2.1)
  - S3: Commitment to regions and communities affected by activities (Section 2.3.3)
  - S4: Acting in the interests of consumers and end-users (Section 2.3.4).
- Overall, the passage sets the scope, material topics, and performance monitoring framework for impact finance within La Banque Postale’s CSR reporting.

nodes.title: Monitoring indicators for impact finance commitments
nodes.heading: 2.1.6.4 Monitoring indicators for impact finance commitments
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group is committed to a broad approach to impact finance.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on impact finance as a strategic pillar, embedded across La Banque Postale Group’s double materiality analysis, covering financing of environmental solutions, the social economy, and support for vulnerable customers.
- Mapping of impact finance to material IROs, spanning:
  - Positive impacts: voluntary actions and investments with environmental/social benefits; sustainable/positive impact financing; access to bancassurance (including vulnerable groups) and regional coverage.
  - Negative impacts: environmental/social impacts of financed activities; potential negative customer impacts from inadequate insurance.
  - Risks and opportunities: exposure to physical and transition risks; opportunities in sustainable finance; resilience of the business model; exemplary management of financing and investments; downstream value-chain working conditions.
- Monitoring indicators for impact finance commitments, with references to climate action (E1), regional and community commitments (S3), and consumer/end-user interests (S4).
- Detailed definitions of assets managed with ESG filters/labels:
  - SFDR classifications (Articles 6, 8, 9) and scope application.
  - LBP AM “responsible technical reserves”: SRI/Greenfin-certified or equivalent (SRI V2) portfolios; other ESG-filtered assets (e.g., SFDR 8) with defined exclusions and lower selectivity.
  - Exclusions of marketed-but-not-managed assets from reporting.
  - Louvre Banque Privée methodology: cumulative sector exclusions, standards-based exclusions via Sustainalytics, internal critical review; use of SRI-certified or ≥3 Morningstar Globes funds; allowance for certain non-rateable strategies capped at 5% and categorized SFDR 8; no direct holdings in bonds/real estate/forestry; handling of unlisted assets via LBP AM for “Green Industry Law” profiles.
  - CNP Assurances “other ESG filters”: subsidiary-specific but group-consistent protocols, complemented by exclusion and engagement policies and NZAOA commitments; eligible asset classes include listed equities, bonds, real estate, woodland, private equity/infrastructure, and listed equity funds.
- Reported outstandings (2022–2024):
  - LBP AM & Louvre Banque Privée: growth in total assets; mix across SFDR Articles 6/8/9 and non-SFDR; rising Article 8 and 9 volumes.
  - CNP Assurances, LBP AM & Louvre Banque Privée: total outstandings increase; stable total responsible finance assets; breakdown between SRI/Greenfin-compliant and other ESG-filtered assets.
- Environmental information on climate change (E1):
  - Material IROs and link to strategy/business model; reference to detailed climate IRO assessment.
  - Climate risk types (physical and transition) per materiality analysis.
  - Resilience analysis and stress testing:
    - Internal framework using NGFS scenarios aligned with ACPR/ECB exercises; short-term (1–3 years) projections on retail/non-retail portfolios with plans to extend beyond 10 years.
    - Sensitivity analyses for market, liquidity, and operational risk; integration into ICAAP and risk management (risk mapping, materiality matrix).
    - Physical risk scenarios: floods for real estate, drought for corporates; operational risk scenario of a 100-year Seine flood to calibrate insurance coverage.
    - Findings: overall performance aligned with eurozone bank averages; limited exposure and low concentration to carbon-intensive sectors.
  - CNP Assurances ACPR climate stress test (France scope, end-2022 data): assessed sensitivity to high-rate environments; demonstrated resilience due to portfolio decarbonization, coal exposure reduction, and increased green investments.
- Cross-references to glossary and other URD sections for terminology and methodological details.

nodes.title: Type of climate risk
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.1.1 Type of climate risk
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group’s various climate-related physical and transition risks are presented in Section 2.1.3.2 “Description of material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs)”.
nodes.summary:
- ESG fund eligibility and limits at Louvre Banque Privée: in rare cases, funds not rateable by Morningstar globes (e.g., Global Macro, Long/Short strategies) can be included if their ESG process is detailed and validated by the UCI Referencing Committee; such funds are capped at 5% of a management profile’s technical reserves and must be SFDR Article 8.

nodes.title: Resilience analysis
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.1.2 Resilience analysis
nodes.start_phrase: An internal stress test framework has been developed by La Banque Postale to measure the impacts of climate risk on its business model and study its resilience based on the scenarios of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) used in the exercises of the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) and the European Central Bank (ECB).
nodes.summary:
- ESG integration in asset selection and management:
  - Louvre Banque Privée may include, in exceptional cases, funds not rateable by Morningstar “globes” (e.g., Global Macro, Long/Short strategies) if their ESG process is validated by the UCI Referencing Committee; capped at 5% of a management profile’s technical reserves and must be SFDR Article 8.
  - Louvre Banque Privée does not directly hold bonds, real estate, or forestry assets and generally does not manage unlisted assets; “Green Industry Law” profiles may include some unlisted assets, selected by LBP AM.
  - CNP Assurances defines “technical reserves with other ESG filters” via subsidiary-specific protocols reviewed for Group consistency, supplemented by exclusions, shareholder engagement, and NZAOA commitments; eligible assets include listed equities/bonds, real estate, woodland, private equity/infrastructure funds, and listed equity funds.

- Climate risk materiality, stress testing, and resilience:
  - Group-wide climate risk assessment follows NGFS scenarios as used by ACPR/ECB, with 1–3 year projections (constant assets) for Retail and Non-Retail portfolios, expanding to >10 years from 2024.
  - Additional sensitivity analyses cover market, liquidity, and operational risks; results feed ICAAP, increase capital coverage for climate risks, and inform risk mapping/materiality.
  - Physical risk scenarios include floods for real estate, droughts for corporates, and a 100-year Seine flood for operational risk and insurance calibration.
  - Portfolio exposure to most carbon-intensive sectors is limited, with low concentration; overall performance aligns with eurozone banks.
  - CNP Assurances participated in ACPR climate stress tests (data end-2022), showing resilience aided by lower portfolio carbon footprint, reduced coal exposure, and higher green investments; assessed sensitivity to high-rate environments.

- Transition plan and Paris Agreement alignment:
  - Commitment to net-zero emissions by 2040 (10 years ahead of Paris Agreement), contingent on aligned action by governments and companies.
  - In 2025, publication of a Group transition plan (La Banque Postale, CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée) detailing 5-year actions, integrating climate targets with financial planning, governance, monitoring, and dedicated financing.
  - Methodological anchors: SBTi (commitment since 2017; co-development and early validation in 2021 for operations and CIB) and NZBA; subsidiaries are members of NZAOA (CNP) and NZAMI (LBP AM).
  - Ongoing implementation: property portfolio steering tools (residential/commercial) and development of corporate counterparty tools; operational targets integrated into La Poste Group’s SBTi-validated target (March 2024).
  - Sectoral policies in coal, oil, and gas aligned to 1.5°C, grounded in IPCC SR15, IEA Net Zero by 2050, and CRREM 1.5°C.
  - Subsidiaries deploy Paris-aligned strategies adapted to their business specificities.

nodes.title: Presentation of the transition plan
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.2.1 Presentation of the transition plan
nodes.start_phrase: In 2021, through its Chairman of the Executive Board, La Banque Postale made an ambitious commitment to achieve net zero emissions by 2040, i.e. ten years ahead of the targets set by the Paris Agreement, conditional upon consistent measures from governments and companies.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and purpose: Extract from La Banque Postale Group’s Universal Registration Document detailing its climate strategy, transition plan, governance, and mitigation/adaptation policies within the “Sustainable performance – Environmental information” section.
- Climate strategy foundation: Scenario analyses quantify stressed impacts and internal capital adequacy and define low-carbon pathways to align portfolios with the Paris Agreement; climate risks are embedded in the strategy and business model.
- Net-zero commitment and transition plan:
  - Net-zero emissions by 2040 (announced 2021), ahead of Paris Agreement timelines, contingent on broader policy consistency.
  - Group-wide transition plan published in 2025 covering La Banque Postale, CNP Assurances, LBP AM, and Louvre Banque Privée; five-year actions aligned with financial planning horizons; requires transformation across governance, monitoring, and financing.
  - Plan integrates long-term targets into commercial and operational strategies and mobilizes all business lines.
- Methodologies and alliances:
  - Pathways built using SBTi and NZBA frameworks; LBP on NZBA Steering Group since 2021.
  - Early SBTi involvement (since 2017), co-developing finance-sector methodology; one of the first banks with SBTi-validated pathways (operational and CIB) in 2021.
  - 2023 progress: rollout of steering tools for real estate (residential/commercial) and corporate counterparties; operational targets integrated into La Poste Group’s SBTi-validated target (March 2024).
- Sector policies and scientific alignment: Stringent coal, oil, and gas risk policies aligned with a 1.5°C trajectory using IPCC SR15, IEA NZE 2050, and CRREM 1.5°C; strategy designed to be climate-resilient.
- Subsidiary targets and approaches:
  - CNP Assurances: Paris-aligned GHG reduction targets; ~28% of the investment portfolio under an aligned target by end-2024; approach follows Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance recommendations with continuous improvement.
  - LBP AM: “Net Zero” alignment for 80% of AUM by 2030 and 100% by 2040 (Net Zero Asset Managers Initiative member).
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Uses “implied temperature rise” scoring (SBTi/CDP data) to assess and aggregate portfolio alignment (1.5°C to >3°C).
- Market benchmarks: Group and subsidiaries are not excluded from Paris Agreement-aligned benchmarks, such as the EU Paris-Aligned Benchmark (EU PAB).
- Embedding in strategy and finance:
  - Each business line has a roadmap aligning commercial targets with climate targets; divisional delivery with Executive Committee oversight.
  - Transition projects integrated into strategic and budget reviews, strengthening integrated financial and non-financial planning.
  - Governance: Plan led by the Sustainability Department; validated at each stage by the Executive Committee; Supervisory Board informed; Mission Committee contributed and approved final content. Subsidiary approvals via respective boards/committees (CNP Board; LBP AM approvals in 2025; LBP Privée Executive Board in 2024).
- Monitoring and reporting: Annual public progress reporting; plan review every 3–5 years to reflect regulatory and strategic changes; mechanisms in place to assess progress and adjust actions.
- Mitigation, adaptation, and efficiency policies:
  - Mitigation through sector-specific policies (coal, oil & gas, aeronautical) and decarbonization pathways for high-emitting sectors (real estate, automotive transport, air transport, cement).
  - Adaptation: Caisse des Dépôts Group adopted an adaptation policy in 2024; LBP Group to develop an aligned adaptation policy starting 2025.
  - Operational energy efficiency addressed via building management commitments.

nodes.title: Incorporating the transition plan into the Group’s overall strategy and financial forecasts
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.2.2 Incorporating the transition plan into the Group’s overall strategy and financial forecasts
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has included its decarbonization target s in its overall target s.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale Group’s sustainable performance and environmental strategy, aligned with the Paris Agreement.
- CNP Assurances: emission-reduction targets aligned with the Net‑Zero Asset Owner Alliance; about 28% of its investment portfolio covered by Paris-aligned targets at end‑2024; iterative improvement due to data gaps.

- Louvre Banque Privée: portfolio managed using an “implied temperature rise” metric based on SBTi and CDP data, targeting alignment down to 1.5°C.
- Group notes compatibility with Paris-aligned financial benchmarks such as the EU Paris-Aligned Benchmark (PAB).
- Transition plan integration: decarbonization targets embedded in overall Group strategy and financial planning; each business line has a roadmap aligning commercial and climate objectives; execution monitored by the Executive Committee; projects incorporated into strategic and budget reviews to track costs and value.
- Governance of the transition plan: led by the Sustainability Department; validated by the Executive Committee; Supervisory Board informed; Mission Committee approved final content. Entity approvals include CNP Assurances’ Board, LBP AM approvals planned for 2025, and Louvre Banque Privée’s plan adopted in 2024 with joint publication in 2025.
- Monitoring and reporting: annual progress disclosed in the sustainability report; plan reviewed every 3–5 years to reflect regulatory and strategic changes; management mechanisms set to track progress and adjust actions.
- Climate policies:
  - Mitigation: GHG reduction across activities; sector policies (coal, oil & gas, aeronautics) and decarbonization pathways for high‑emitting sectors (real estate, automotive transport, air transport, cement).
  - Adaptation: alignment with Caisse des Dépôts’ 2024 adaptation policy; LBP Group to formalize an aligned adaptation policy starting in 2025.
  - Energy efficiency: operational commitments, particularly in building management.

Subsidiary governance: CNP Assurances’ plan approved/monitored by its Board; LBP AM’s plan to be approved in 2025 by its Sustainable Finance Committee and Supervisory Board; Louvre Banque Privée’s plan adopted in 2024, to be jointly published with La Banque Postale in 2025.
- Monitoring and review: annual progress reporting in the sustainability report; management mechanisms to assess progress and adjust; full plan review every 3–5 years to reflect regulatory and strategic changes.
- Climate policies:
  - Mitigation: GHG reduction across activities; sector policies (coal, oil & gas, aeronautics); decarbonization targets/pathways for high-emitting sectors (real estate, automotive transport, air transport, cement).

nodes.title: Climate change mitigation and adaptation policies
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.3 Climate change mitigation and adaptation policies
nodes.start_phrase: Through its climate policies, La Banque Postale Group aims to address the following sustainability issues:
nodes.summary:
- Focus of the excerpt: La Banque Postale Group’s climate strategy and governance, integration of transition plans into overall strategy and finance, and detailed climate mitigation/adaptation policies across the Group and key subsidiaries (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée).
- Investment alignment and targets:
  - CNP Assurances: Paris Agreement–aligned decarbonization targets; ~28% of the investment portfolio covered by Paris-aligned targets at end-2024; targets based on Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance (NZAOA) recommendations; iterative improvement due to data gaps.
  - LBP AM: Commitment to “Net Zero” alignment for 80% of AUM by 2030 and 100% by 2040.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Uses “implied temperature” metric (SBTi and CDP data) to assess portfolio alignment from 1.5°C to >3°C scenarios; portfolio temperature is a weighted average of holdings.
  - Group inclusion in Paris-aligned benchmarks (e.g., EU PAB), which aggregate issuers compatible with a 1.5°C pathway by 2050.
- Transition plan integration and governance:
  - Decarbonization targets embedded in Group strategic objectives; each business line created a roadmap aligning commercial and climate targets.
  - Execution managed short-to-medium term within divisions; overall monitoring by the Executive Committee; progressive incorporation of transition projects into strategic and budget reviews with tracking of execution, costs, and value creation; strengthens integrated financial and non-financial planning.
  - Construction led by the Sustainability Department; iterative validation by the Executive Committee; Supervisory Board kept informed; Mission Committee contributed and approved final content.
  - Subsidiary governance: CNP Assurances’ plan approved/monitored by its Board; LBP AM’s plan slated for approval in 2025 by the Sustainable Finance Committee and Supervisory Board; Louvre Banque Privée’s plan adopted in 2024, to be co-published with La Banque Postale’s in 2025.
- Monitoring and review:
  - Annual public progress reporting in the sustainability report; formal management mechanisms to assess progress and allow adjustments; full plan review every 3–5 years to reflect regulatory and strategic developments.
- Climate policies (mitigation, adaptation, energy efficiency):
  - Mitigation: Reduction of GHG emissions across activities, with sector policies for coal, oil and gas, and aeronautics; decarbonization targets/pathways for carbon-intensive sectors (real estate, automotive transport, air transport, cement), focused on Corporate and Investment Banking.
  - Adaptation: Caisse des Dépôts Group adopted an adaptation policy in 2024; La Banque Postale Group to develop an aligned adaptation policy starting 2025.
  - Operational energy efficiency: Commitments around buildings, renewable energy use, and reductions in transport- and purchase-related emissions (with further detail referenced in Section 2.2.1.5).
- Group climate framework for financing and investment:
  - Application of the parent Group’s climate policy: strict framework for high-emission sectors, progressive alignment to a 1.5°C pathway, and financing supportive of environmental transition.
  - La Banque Postale’s additional instruments: sector-specific policies, principles of intervention, and a Responsible Financing and Investment Charter.
- Sector-specific policies and exclusions (banking scope):
  - Part of the “net zero emissions by 2040” ambition; apply to financing and investments in coal, oil and gas, and aeronautics, primarily within Corporate Banking and Local Development; bancassurance and Wealth & Asset Management currently excluded (with separate policies to be detailed elsewhere).
  - Coal policy: Complete exit by 2030; conditional financing for companies publicly committed to exit coal before 2030 with science-based, Paris-aligned transition plans; financing allowed for renewable energy projects; renewable subsidiaries of coal companies not excluded.
  - Complementary measures: Exclusion policy for environmental controversies, responsible mobility, building energy performance, responsible digital, responsible purchasing, and aeronautics intervention principles; distinct focus on own operations versus Corporate & Investment Banking.

nodes.title: Risk Management Policy – Coal sector
nodes.heading: Risk Management Policy – Coal sector
nodes.start_phrase: This policy establishes the principles to be applied in order to fulfil its commitment to completely exit the coal sector by 2030.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and intent: The section outlines La Banque Postale’s environmental and climate strategy within its universal registration document, referencing a glossary for CSR terms and linking to detailed decarbonization levers and action plans.
- Group alignment: As part of Caisse des Dépôts and La Poste, the bank applies the Group Climate Policy across financing and investments to set strict rules for high-emission activities, progressively align portfolios with a 1.5°C pathway, and channel financing toward environmental transformation.
- Net zero by 2040 sector policies (banking scope): 
  - Coal: Commitment to a complete coal exit by 2030; financing only for companies publicly committed to exit coal before 2030 with science-based, Paris-aligned transition plans; financing allowed for renewable projects and renewable subsidiaries.
  - Oil & gas: Commitment to a total exit by 2030; exclusion and gradual divestment from companies, including those on GOGEL, unless they have a credible public exit strategy before 2040; exceptions only for health/safety or regulatory compliance; no collaboration with entities opposing the energy transition.
  - Aeronautics: Financing limited to newest aircraft and companies with 1.5°C-aligned strategies from 2025; support for SAF and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except specific French law provision), with support for modernization that advances energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.
  - Note: Policies apply to Corporate Banking and Local Development; bancassurance and Wealth & Asset Management are out of scope here and have separate policies.
- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: Embeds decarbonization in corporate and investment banking; imposes exclusions for fossil fuel activities and environmental law violators; controversy assessment procedures in place.
- Operational commitments: Additional responsible commitments span mobility, building energy performance, digital, and purchasing.
- Market initiatives: Active participation in UNEP FI Principles for Responsible Banking since 2019, aligning strategy with SDGs and the Paris Agreement; PRB reporting referenced.
- Subsidiary focus (CNP Assurances): 
  - Frameworks: Compliant with Article 29 of the Energy-Climate Law and SFDR; aligned with UN Global Compact and PRI.
  - Targets: Member of the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance (carbon neutrality in the investment portfolio by 2050).
  - Levers: Portfolio Paris alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and public policy advocacy.
  - Policies: Coal phase-out (zero exposure by 2030 EU/OECD; 2040 elsewhere); extended oil and gas investment restrictions (2021–2022); due diligence policy (2024) organized around exclusion, engagement, and ESG-based selection; governance and oversight by Investment Department and asset management committees.

nodes.title: Risk Management Policy – Oil and Gas sectors
nodes.heading: Risk Management Policy – Oil and Gas sectors
nodes.start_phrase: This policy establishes the principles to be applied to achieve a total exit commitment from these sectors by 2030 in order to support its climate commitments.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of La Banque Postale’s environmental and sustainable finance commitments within its 2024 Universal Registration Document.
- Oil and Gas Risk Management Policy: commitment to fully exit oil and gas by 2030; exclusion of companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries; conditional engagement only with firms having credible public exit strategies before 2040; limited exceptions for health/safety/regulatory financing; no collaboration with companies obstructing the energy transition.
- Aeronautics sector principles: financing limited to newest aircraft and companies aligned with a 1.5°C pathway from 2025; support for SAF and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except in France if permitted by Climate and Resilience law); support for modernization projects that advance energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.
- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: integrates decarbonization into corporate and investment banking; excludes fossil fuel activities and companies breaching environmental laws; controversy assessment procedures for environmental issues; cross-reference to detailed charter.
- Participation in market initiatives: alignment with UNEP FI Principles for Responsible Banking, SDGs, and Paris Agreement; reference to PRB reporting section.
- Subsidiary commitments (CNP Assurances): adherence to LEC Article 29, SFDR, UN Global Compact, PRI; member of Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance targeting portfolio net zero by 2050; three levers—portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and advocacy for supportive public policies; 2024-updated due diligence policy with pillars of exclusions, engagement, and ESG-based selection; coal phase-out by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (rest of world); extended oil and gas investment restrictions (2021–2022); governance and oversight by the Investment Department and asset management committees.

nodes.title: The Bank’s principles of intervention in the aeronautics sector
nodes.heading: The Bank's principles of intervention in the aeronautics sector
nodes.start_phrase: In line with its climate commitments, the principles establish the rules to be applied in order to participate in and encourage the decarbonisation of the aeronautics sector.
nodes.summary:
- Sets a Risk Management Policy for Oil & Gas with a full exit by 2030: exclusion and gradual divestment from companies, including those on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries; maintains ties only if firms have a public, credible pre-2040 exit strategy; allows financing solely for health/safety or regulatory needs; rejects collaboration with companies obstructing the energy transition.
- Defines climate-aligned principles for the aeronautics sector: financing limited to newest aircraft and, from 2025, companies on a 1.5°C pathway; supports SAF and electric aircraft projects; stops financing new airports (except where allowed by France’s Climate and Resilience law); backs upgrades to existing airports that advance energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.
- Outlines the Responsible Financing and Investment Charter guiding Corporate and Investment Banking: exclusions for fossil fuel activities and environmental law violators; controversy assessment procedures; integrates decarbonization into financing and lending decisions.
- Highlights participation in market initiatives, notably UNEP FI’s Principles for Responsible Banking since 2019, aligning strategy with the SDGs and the Paris Agreement, with PRB reporting referenced in the URD.
- Details subsidiary policies, chiefly CNP Assurances: climate strategy aligned with Article 29 LEC and SFDR; adheres to the UN Global Compact and PRI; member of the Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance targeting net-zero by 2050; three levers—portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and policy advocacy; a 2024-updated due diligence policy centered on exclusions, engagement, and ESG-based selection; coal phase-out to zero by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (elsewhere); extended oil and gas investment restrictions in 2021–2022; governance and monitoring handled by the Investment Department and asset management committees.

nodes.title: Responsible Financing and Investment Charter
nodes.heading: Responsible Financing and Investment Charter
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale is well aware of the need to incorporate decarbonisation matters into its Corporate and Investment Banking activities, and also works with other sectors.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Environmental information within La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, outlining sustainable performance policies, risk management, and responsible financing to meet climate goals.

- Oil and gas risk management policy:
  - Commitment to fully exit oil and gas by 2030.
  - Exclusion of companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries, with phased divestment.
  - Continued engagement only with firms having a credible, public exit strategy before 2040.
  - Exceptions limited to financing for health/safety or regulatory compliance.
  - No collaboration with companies opposing the energy transition.

- Aeronautics sector principles:
  - Financing restricted to newest aircraft and companies with strategies aligned to a 1.5°C pathway from 2025.
  - Support for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and electric aircraft projects.
  - No financing of new airports (except in France where permitted by the Climate and Resilience law).
  - Support for modernization of existing infrastructure that advances energy transition, biodiversity, and environmental performance.

- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter:
  - Integrates decarbonization into corporate and investment banking.
  - Exclusions for fossil fuel activities and companies violating environmental laws.
  - Procedure to assess companies involved in serious or repeated environmental controversies.
  - Provides guidance for financing and lending to business clients.

- External initiatives:
  - Active participation in the UN’s Principles for Responsible Banking (UNEP FI), aligning strategy with the SDGs and the Paris Agreement; PRB reporting referenced in the document.

- Subsidiary policies (CNP Assurances):
  - Climate policy aligned with Article 29 of the Energy-Climate Law, SFDR, UN Global Compact, and PRI.
  - Member of the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance; commitment to net-zero investment portfolio by 2050.
  - Three levers: portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure; shareholder engagement; advocacy for pro-transition public policies.
  - 2024 due diligence policy centered on exclusion, engagement, and ESG-based selection.
  - Coal phase-out: zero exposure by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (rest of world); extended oil and gas investment restrictions (2021–2022).
  - Oversight by the Investment Department and asset management committees.

nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines La Banque Postale’s environmental risk and responsible finance framework. It details a policy to fully exit oil and gas by 2030, excluding companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (and their subsidiaries) from financial services unless they have a credible plan to leave the sector before 2040, with limited exceptions for health, safety, or regulatory needs, and a refusal to work with actors obstructing the energy transition. It sets sector rules for aeronautics: financing only newest aircraft and, from 2025, companies aligned with a 1.5°C pathway; support for SAF and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except where allowed by French law), while backing modernization that advances energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance. The Responsible Financing and Investment Charter guides corporate and investment banking, imposing exclusions on fossil fuel operators and environmental law violators and establishing a review process for serious environmental controversies. The Bank participates in global initiatives like UNEP FI’s Principles for Responsible Banking, aligning strategy with the SDGs and the Paris Agreement. Subsidiary commitments, notably CNP Assurances, include adherence to LEC Article 29, SFDR, the UN Global Compact, and PRI; membership in the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance targeting net-zero portfolios by 2050; and a three-pronged approach of portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and advocacy for pro-transition public policies. nodes.title: Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
nodes.heading: Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
nodes.start_phrase: In addition, La Banque Postale’s subsidiaries have established climate change mitigation policies for their activities.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines La Banque Postale’s environmental risk management, sector policies, responsible financing framework, subsidiary commitments, and science-based decarbonization targets.

- Oil and gas risk policy: commitment to fully exit the oil and gas sectors by 2030; exclusion of companies on the Global Oil and Gas Exit List (GOGEL) and their subsidiaries, with gradual divestment; continued relationships only with firms having a public, credible pre-2040 exit strategy; allowance for financing strictly needed for health/safety or regulatory compliance; no collaboration with companies obstructing the energy transition.

- Aeronautics sector principles: financing restricted to newest aircraft and companies aligned with a 1.5°C pathway from 2025; support for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and electric aircraft; no financing of new airports (except possible cases in France per the Climate and Resilience law); support for modernization of existing infrastructure when it advances the energy transition, biodiversity, or environmental performance.

- Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: embeds decarbonization in corporate and investment banking; excludes fossil fuel companies and those violating environmental laws; controversy assessment process for serious/repeated environmental issues.

- Industry initiatives: active participation in market frameworks; PRB (UNEP FI) signatory since 2019, aligning strategy with SDGs and the Paris Agreement; PRB reporting referenced in the document.

- Subsidiaries’ policies and governance:
  - CNP Assurances: climate strategy aligned with LEC Article 29 and SFDR; UN-convened Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance member (2050 portfolio net zero); three levers—portfolio alignment measurement and disclosure, shareholder engagement, and advocacy for supportive public policies; 2024 due diligence policy built on exclusion, engagement, and ESG integration; coal exit by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (rest of world); extended exclusions to oil and gas (2021–2022); climate risk mitigation via reinsurance for excess mortality (including pandemics and heat waves).
  - LBP AM: exclusion policy covering thermal coal and oil & gas (updated 2023), validated by the Sustainable Finance Committee; oversight by ESG and GREaT committees; applies to all open-ended funds; harmonization in progress with La Financière de l’Échiquier (voting, engagement, coal already aligned; oil & gas combining underway); engagement policy to improve portfolio climate performance, with weekly ESG committee monitoring; Governance Committee oversees voting policy.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: integrates sustainability risks under SFDR and Energy-Climate Act Article 29; ESG Charter sets targets; operational responsibility lies with the Director of Discretionary Management and the Chief Sustainability Officer; Executive Board approves annual sustainability roadmap; aims to balance ESG integration with diversification and risk control; key ESG documents publicly available.

- Climate targets and performance trajectory (operational scope):
  - Net zero ambition by 2040, using science-based trajectories.
  - 100% renewable electricity by 2030.
  - Reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 43.6% over 2021–2030 (vehicle fleet and buildings; excludes Banking Advice Line, CNP Assurances, and La Poste Network buildings), aligned to a 1.5°C scenario using the Absolute Contraction Approach.
  - Reduce partial Scope 3 emissions (categories 1 partial, 3, 6, 7) by 25%.
  - Expected absolute reductions by 2030: Scope 1 −2,219 tCO2e; Scope 2 (market-based) −736 tCO2e; Scope 3 (partial) −7,757 tCO2e.
  - Targets aligned with SBTi pathway validated in March 2024 for La Poste SA and implemented for La Banque Postale SA.

nodes.title: Presentation of decarbonization targets
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.4.1 Presentation of decarbonization targets
nodes.start_phrase: To monitor and achieve its reduction targets, and in particular the achievement of its “zero net emissions” ambition by 2040, La Banque Postale has developed science-based trajectories.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s sustainable performance and environmental strategy, with emphasis on climate risk management, portfolio decarbonization, governance, methodologies, and progress against targets.

- Climate risk and exclusion policies:
  - CNP Assurances implements global reinsurance to mitigate excess mortality risks (pandemics, heat waves).
  - LBP AM applies and regularly updates an exclusion policy (thermal coal; oil and gas), validated by the Sustainable Finance Committee, overseen by ESG and GREaT committees; applies to all open-ended funds and published online.
  - Integration of La Financière de l’Échiquier into LBP AM: oil and gas policies being combined; voting, engagement, and coal policies harmonized.
  - LBP AM’s engagement policy promotes climate and ESG integration in investee strategies, with campaign monitoring and voting policy governance.
  - Louvre Banque Privée integrates sustainability risks per SFDR and Article 29 LEC, with an ESG charter, defined responsibilities, annual roadmap approval, and public disclosures.

- Operational decarbonization targets (SBTi-aligned, validated March 2024 within La Poste SA scope):
  - 100% renewable electricity by 2030.
  - Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions: -43.6% (2021–2030), excluding CNP Assurances, Banking Advice Line, and La Poste Network buildings.
  - Scope 3 (partial: categories 1 partial, 3, 6, 7): -25% (2021–2030).
  - Targeted absolute reductions by 2030: Scope 1 (-2,219 tCO2e), Scope 2 (-736 tCO2e), Scope 3 partial (-7,757 tCO2e).

- Financed portfolio targets and frameworks:
  - Dual approach using SBTi and NZBA.
  - Real estate and corporate portfolios:
    - Home loans (retail): -73.7% kgCO2e/m² (2022–2035), equating to -53% by 2030 (CRREM 1.5°C; PCAF); new target filed with SBTi in 2024.
    - Commercial real estate: -65% kgCO2e/m² (2022–2030).
    - Large corporate equity and bonds: portfolio “temperature” from +3.14°C (2019) to 2.2°C (2025) for Scopes 1–2.
    - Large corporate medium/long-term loans: 3.14°C (2019) to 2.3°C (2025) for Scopes 1–2.
  - NZBA sectoral targets (Scope 3 Category 15 intensity):
    - Automotive: -7% gCO2e/vehicle.km (2020–2030).
    - Aviation: -56% gCO2e/passenger.km (2020–2030).
    - Cement: -30% kgCO2e/tonne (2020–2030).
    - No exposure to coal; power generation financing limited to renewables; oil & gas policy aligned with a 1.5°C pathway from 2030.
  - Acknowledged trade-off: decarbonization of real estate portfolios may conflict with affordability and inclusion goals (e.g., lending to low-income households and social housing).

- Financed emissions and coverage (as of 30 June 2024):
  - Total measurable Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions: 10,920 ktCO2e; 95% from corporate portfolios, 5% from retail residential real estate.
  - €71bn of exposures covered by SBTi pathways (79% residential real estate; 11% commercial real estate; 7% large corporate equity/bonds and MLT loans; 3% asset/project financing in renewables).
  - Of €106bn eligible for Scope 3 calculation, 67% managed by low‑carbon pathways.

- Subsidiary targets:
  - CNP Assurances:
    - Operations: -50% Scopes 1–2 (2019–2030; location-based).
    - Investment portfolio: net zero by 2050 (NZ AOA), 1.5°C alignment with asset-class targets; coal exit by 2030 (EU/OECD) and 2040 (RoW).
    - By 2029: -53% Scopes 1–2 for directly held equities/corporate bonds/infrastructure; -32% for directly owned real estate; -17% carbon intensity for electricity producers by end‑2024.
  - LBP AM (including LFDE): NZAMi commitment; 1.5°C IPCC P2 alignment; milestones—80% of technical reserves aligned by 2030, 100% by 2040, economy-wide neutrality by 2050; SBTi-based validation share methodology.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: implied temperature pathway targeting 1.5°C alignment by 2040 (LEC Article 29-compliant).

- Methodological framework:
  - Use of SBTi, NZBA, PCAF, CRREM 1.5°C, and IPCC SR15 temperature scoring (ROTS).
  - Current strategy based on IPCC SSP1‑1.9 (Paris 1.5°C), with disclosure of any future baseline adjustments.
  - Revised real estate pathways filed with SBTi at end‑2024; broader methodological review planned in 2025.

- Progress against operational targets (selected metrics):
  - Scope 2 decreased 23% from 2023 to 2024, driven by energy efficiency, building management systems, renovations, and renewable electricity sourcing.
  - Scope 1 slightly increased in 2024 due to vehicle fleet; new fleet policy being rolled out.
  - Scope 3 (partial) down 4.9% in 2024 vs 2023.

- Governance and disclosure:
  - Clear committee oversight (Sustainable Finance Committee, ESG Committee, GREaT, Governance Committee).
  - Annual approval of sustainability roadmaps; broad public disclosure of ESG charters, Article 29 reports, SFDR documentation, and adverse impact statements.

nodes.title: Detail of decarbonization targets
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.4.2 Detail of decarbonization targets
nodes.start_phrase: Additional information on GHG emissions and the actions implemented to achieve the targets is available in Sections 2.2.1.5 “Decarbonisation levers and action plans” and 2.2.1.7 "Group greenhouse gas emissions".
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s environmental strategy and performance within its 2024 Universal Registration Document, covering net-zero commitments, methodology, operational and financed emissions targets, progress, and decarbonisation levers.
- Net-zero and alignment initiatives:
  - LBP AM joined the Net Zero Asset Managers initiative (NZAMi) in 2021; decarbonisation trajectory set for LBP AM and Tocqueville Finance (open-ended and dedicated funds, all eligible asset classes), extended in 2023 to La Financière de l’Échiquier.
  - Milestones: 80% of technical reserves aligned with a Paris-compatible carbon pathway by 2030; 100% by 2040; economy-wide carbon neutrality by 2050.
  - Five-year review cycle under NZAMi; methodology anchored in SBTi for Financial Institutions, tracking the share of technical reserves invested in SBTi-validated companies.
  - Louvre Banque Privée uses an “implied temperature rise” approach targeting 1.5°C alignment by 2040, per Article 29 of France’s Energy-Climate law.
- Methodology and scenarios:
  - Targets set using the IPCC SSP1-1.9 (1.5°C-aligned) scenario; assumes a 2020 peak of global emissions and lower financial impact; baseline choices reflect data availability and relevance; any future baseline changes will be disclosed.
- Operational emissions targets and performance (SBTi scope, excluding Banking Advice Line and CNP Assurances):
  - 2021 baselines and 2030 targets: Scope 1: 5,089 tCO2e to 2,870 (-43.6%); Scope 2: 1,689 to 953 (-43.6%); partial Scope 3: 31,026 to 23,270 (-25%). Average annual cuts: S1/S2 -4.84%, S3 -2.78%.
  - 2024 progress vs 2023: Scope 2 down 23% (exceeds 2030 trajectory) due to building energy efficiency (BMS, renovations) and renewable electricity; Scope 1 slightly up from vehicle fleet, with a new policy being rolled out; example of footprint reduction via site consolidation in Orléans.
- Financed emissions targets (sector intensity and portfolio temperature):
  - Sector intensity targets/pathways:
    - Residential real estate (retail): 2022 baseline 28 kgCO2e/m²; 2024 at 28.5; 2030 target 13.16 (-53%). New 2035 SBTi submission targets -73.7% over 2022–2035 with -53% by 2030.
    - Commercial real estate: 2022 baseline 32.6; 2024 at 29.6; 2030 target 11.41 (-65%).
    - Automotive: 2020 baseline 111 gCO2e/vehicle-km; 2024 at 173; 2030 target 103.23 (-7%).
    - Aviation: 2020 baseline 143 gCO2e/passenger-km; 2024 at 103; 2030 target 62.92 (-56%).
    - Cement: 2020 baseline 511 kgCO2e/tonne; 2024 at 375; 2030 target 357.7 (-30%).
  - Pathways: Real estate and corporate portfolios aligned to SBTi; automotive, aviation, cement aligned to NZBA using IEA NZ2050 scenarios. Data primarily from counterparties’ annual reports; sectoral proxies used as needed; intensities for some issuers above sector averages; 2024 car and airline portfolio intensities increased vs 2023 but remain aligned with decarbonisation trajectories.
  - Portfolio temperature alignment:
    - Large corporate equities and bonds (customer Scopes 1&2): improved from 3.1°C (2019) to 1.6°C (2024), outperforming the 2025 target of 2.19°C.
    - Medium/long-term loans to large corporates (customer Scopes 1&2): 3.1°C (2019) to 2.4°C (2024), on track to meet 2.32°C by end-2025.
- Data and coverage developments:
  - Enhanced methodology and precision in calculating real estate intensities through broader collection of energy performance assessments; amount of technical reserves analyzed rose 15.4% (30 Jun 2024 vs 31 Dec 2023) due to better data processing; challenging real estate market limited shifts toward better energy ratings.
- Renewable energy commitments and targets:
  - 100% renewable electricity for major sites since 2015; green electricity share rose again in 2024; target remains 100% by 2030 (92.5% in 2024).
  - Mission-led financing goal: €5.6bn in renewable energy project financing by 2025; €5.039bn originated in 2024; energy financing limited to renewables.
- Decarbonisation levers and action plans:
  - Actions span own operations and Corporate & Investment Banking; detailed Transition Plan to be published in 2025.
  - Operational levers include buildings, vehicles, digital footprint, business travel and commuting; Sustainability Department oversees implementation.
  - Buildings: rollout of BMS; energy renovations (LEDs, replacing gas boilers with more efficient tech); renewable electricity with guarantees of origin; collaboration with La Poste Immobilier; 16 energy audits at key sites; measures continue through 2026.
  - 2030 buildings abatement target: reduce 1,732 tCO2e from 2021 level (3,972 tCO2e), via renovations and BMS/impact fund (-1,212), efficient use (-173), and decarbonising residual consumption (-346).
- Key quantitative snapshots:
  - Renewable electricity supply: 95.2% (2022), 92% (2023), 92.5% (2024), 100% target (2030).
  - Renewable energy financing originations: €4,586m (2023), €5,039m (2024), €5,600m target (2025).

nodes.title: Decarbonisation levers and action plans
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5 Decarbonisation levers and action plans
nodes.start_phrase: To achieve its decarbonisation targets, La Banque Postale and its subsidiaries, including CNP Assurances, LBP AM and Louvre Banque Privée, are implementing a decarbonisation strategy based on various levers, both for their own operations and for their Corporate and Investment Banking activities.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of La Banque Postale’s environmental performance and targets within its CSR/Universal Registration Document, focusing on portfolio alignment, renewable energy, and decarbonisation actions.
- Portfolio temperature alignment: 2024 temperature for large corporate equities and bonds (Scopes 1 & 2) is already below the 2025 target; large corporate medium/long-term loans (Scopes 1 & 2) are on track to reach 2.32°C by end-2025.
- Renewable energy commitments: 100% renewable electricity usage for all major sites since 2015; share of green electricity increased again in 2024; KPI shows 92.5% in 2024 with a 100% target by 2030 (measured on SBTi scope, excluding CNP Assurances and the Banking Advice Line).
- Energy financing strategy: La Banque Postale finances only renewable energy projects; mission-led target of €5.6 billion in renewable energy financing by 2025, with €4,586 million in 2023 and €5,039 million in 2024.
- Decarbonisation strategy and governance: Group-wide levers across own operations and Corporate & Investment Banking, covering subsidiaries (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée); detailed Transition Plan to be published in 2025.
- Operational scope priorities: reducing emissions from buildings, vehicle fleet, digital footprint, and business travel/commuting, led by the Sustainability Department with implementation by relevant functions.
- Buildings decarbonisation actions: deployment of Technical Building Management Systems (BMS), energy renovations (e.g., LED installations, replacement of energy-intensive equipment), renewable electricity supply, HVAC optimization with La Poste Immobilier, and systematic pursuit of energy performance in maintenance (e.g., replacing gas boilers with more efficient alternatives); 16 energy audits completed on major sites; actions continue through 2026.

nodes.title: Operational scope
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.1 Operational scope
nodes.start_phrase: Reducing the carbon footprint of operational activities is based on targeted actions for buildings, vehicles, the digital footprint, and business travel and commuting.
nodes.summary:
- Portfolio alignment and temperature targets: 2024 portfolio temperature for large corporate equities and bonds (Scopes 1 & 2) is already below the 2025 target; large corporate medium/long‑term loans (Scopes 1 & 2) are on track to reach 2.32°C by end‑2025.

- Renewable energy commitments:
  - Operations: 100% renewable electricity for major sites since 2015; share of green electricity rose again in 2024; on an SBTi pathway (excluding CNP Assurances and the Banking Advice Line); target 100% renewable electricity by 2030 (2024: 92.5%).
  - Financing: Mission-led target of €5.6bn in renewable energy project financing by 2025, with progress of €4.586bn in 2023 and €5.039bn in 2024; only finances renewable energy projects.

- Decarbonisation strategy and governance: Group-wide levers across operations and Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB), implemented by La Banque Postale and subsidiaries (CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée); actions driven by the Sustainability Department; full Transition Plan to be published in 2025.

- Operational scope action plans and 2030 targets (vs 2021 baseline):
  - Buildings (target: –1,732 tCO2e from 3,972 tCO2e): energy audits, BMS rollout, energy renovation (LEDs, replacing energy‑intensive equipment), efficient use, and decarbonising residual consumption; 98% renewable electricity under La Poste Immobilier contract; actions continue through 2026; Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund mobilised.
  - Vehicles (target: –1,223 tCO2e from 2,806 tCO2e): full transition of internal fleet to electric/plug‑in hybrids by 2030; eco‑driving training; potential fixed compensatory allowance for company vehicles; deployment in subsidiaries.
  - Travel and commuting (target: –6,566 tCO2e from 26,264 tCO2e; 17% modal shift, 16,224 SOV trips avoided): prioritize public transport (incl. park‑and‑ride in soft mobility pass), active modes (bike purchase/rental and repair support), car‑sharing and car‑free days, remote meetings, and train over air; “soft mobility pass” since 2023 (50% public transport reimbursement + up to €220/year sustainable mobility package); teleworking policy (2 fixed days/week + 10 floating days/year) with measured GHG savings (~6 tCO2e/year per 2023 survey insight).
  - Digital: “Responsible digital by design” with ESG criteria embedded in IT procurement; responsible design of solutions; reduction of workstation and infrastructure footprint (incl. data centre cooling); 30% hardware reuse, ending hard‑drive destruction; ongoing awareness and full digital footprint measurement across IT and related building infrastructure.
  - Responsible purchasing and suppliers: RFAR-certified approach to mitigate environmental impacts; enhanced supplier carbon footprint measurement focused on top 50 emitters; contributions of digital and responsible purchasing to overall targets not yet allocated.

- Corporate & Investment Banking decarbonisation:
  - Sector policies: strict exclusions for coal, oil, and gas with divestment commitments by 2030.
  - Green/impact financing: expansion of green and impact loans (e.g., interest‑free energy renovation loans, impact real estate loans); Group connection to Caisse des Dépôts’ €100bn commitment to France’s environmental transition (2023–2028).
  - Stewardship: active shareholder engagement and voting by LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier to align investees with Net Zero pathways.
  - ESG integration: systematic E, S & G criteria in investment decisions using tools like LBP AM’s GREaT methodology; alignment with decarbonisation objectives; further details to come in the 2025 Transition Plan.

nodes.title: Corporate and Investment Banking
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.2 Corporate and Investment Banking
nodes.start_phrase: The climate and sustainability commitments of the Corporate and Investment Banking portfolios are based on:
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document covering Sustainable performance and Environmental information, focused on the Group’s transition plan and decarbonisation actions across business lines and operations.
- Operational scope levers: Formalised responsible purchasing under RFAR certification to reduce environmental impacts; enhanced supplier carbon-footprint measurement targeting the 50 highest-emitting suppliers; ongoing work to better manage the operational footprint; contributions from digital and responsible purchasing not yet quantified.
- Corporate & Investment Banking: Strict sectoral exclusion/divestment policies for coal, oil and gas by 2030; expansion of green and impact financing (e.g., energy-renovation loans, impact real estate loans); active shareholder engagement via LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier; systematic ESG integration using LBP AM’s GREaT methodology; actions aligned with the Group Transition Plan (published 2025).
- Retail Banking 2030 plan: 
  - Internal systems: qualify consumer loans; calculate carbon footprints for consumer and very small business loans; deploy decision-support tools; explore virtual cards and process dematerialisation.
  - Customer offers: finance sustainable consumption (energy renovations, low-emission vehicles); promote responsible savings with ESG-based segmentation and emissions disclosure; launch impact passbook; expand housing renovation support with partnerships and potential offers for collective housing; dedicated solutions for professionals (impact account, Bpifrance green loans, advisory).
  - Governance/tools: carbon footprint measurement for residential property; use of Impact Weighting Factor in mortgage granting; sustainability-preference questionnaires; portfolio allocation/management rules.
- Corporate & Local Development Banking 2030 plan:
  - Monitoring: calculate financed and facilitated emissions; industrialise data tools (e.g., Impact Weighting Factor); assess company and national transition plans.
  - Portfolio steering: transition-linked granting/pricing criteria; track green bond impact; optimise/rotate low-carbon energy loan portfolios to free capital for new green assets.
  - Offers: support commercial property renovation; tailored ESG services and coordination (green loan structuring); impact factoring; impact banking and e-payments (citizen term account); PV leasing for the public sector.
  - Enablers: staff training needs review; sectoral policies and responsible financing charters; carbon footprint measurement for key portfolios.
- Private Banking (Louvre Banque Privée) 2030 plan:
  - Asset management: consider quantitative constraints on alignment to progressively exclude non-aligned issuers; extend exclusions to conventional fossil fuels; mandates meet SFDR Article 8 and monitor negative impact metrics; active issuer dialogue; sectoral disengagement policies; SRI “citizen” range.
  - Residential real estate: automate retrieval of energy performance data (EPD/DPE) and CO2 by class; integrate energy efficiency into pricing; align mortgage policy with the 2021 Climate & Resilience law for rental properties (e.g., class G renovation commitments).
- Asset Management (LBP AM) 2030 plan: Define and regularly review Net Zero alignment targets (80% of total assets by 2030 toward 100%); align voting/engagement with Net Zero; continue fossil energy policy updates; embed decarbonisation objectives in SRI segmentation and day-to-day management using research tools; transparent reporting.
- Insurance (CNP Assurances) 2030 plan:
  - Investments: implement exclusions (coal, oil, gas); strengthen financed-emissions coverage and ESG integration across asset classes; include transition-plan analysis in engagement; pursue green investments (bonds, certified buildings, forests, green infrastructure); set a new green investment target by 2026 after reaching €30bn in 2025; prior green (2019) and sustainable (2023) bond issues.
  - Insurance business: integrate climate into strategy and incentives; expand sustainable unit-linked products; progressively green Euro funds; improve customer non-financial disclosures; sustainable retirement savings offer.
- Support functions: All corporate functions (governance, HR, finance, sustainability, risk, data/IT, compliance, legal, public affairs, reporting, communications) to develop their own transition plans and provide training/awareness to embed sustainability in practices.
- Measurement approach: Quantifying GHG reductions beyond operational scope remains difficult due to data gaps and sector variability; impacts are currently assessed qualitatively with annual management to adjust actions; the transition plan will be updated within three years as data and methodologies improve.

nodes.title: Support functions
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.3 Support functions
nodes.start_phrase: All of La Banque Postale Group’s support functions will be called on to support the decarbonisation efforts implemented by each activity, including the following functions: governance, human resources, finance, sustai nability, risks, data and information technology, compliance, legal, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, reporting and communications.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document on sustainable performance, environmental information, and insurance.
- Role of support functions: All support areas (governance, HR, finance, sustainability, risk, data/IT, compliance, legal, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, reporting, communications) are mobilized to back decarbonization and must create their own transition plans; awareness and training are used to embed sustainable behaviors.
- Measuring decarbonization: Quantifying GHG reductions beyond operational scope is challenging due to data gaps and sector variability; current impact assessment is largely qualitative, with projects to improve measurement; annual management reviews guide course correction; the transition plan will be updated within three years as data/methods improve.
- Investment activities (near-term actions): Update exclusion criteria per evolving climate scenarios; expand financed-emissions coverage; deepen ESG integration across asset classes; continue property-specific decarbonization work plans; factor companies’ transition plans into shareholder engagement; set a new green investment target by 2026 after meeting €30bn outstanding by 2025.
- Insurance business (near-term actions): Broaden sustainable unit-linked offerings; progressively increase sustainability of legacy Euro funds; enhance non-financial (sustainability) disclosures to customers on their investments.
- CNP Assurances 2030 action plan – investments: Enforce exclusion policies for coal, oil, and gas; apply active ownership (voting and dialogue) to drive transition; select investments using ESG criteria across listed/unlisted equity, bonds, infrastructure, real estate, and forests; scale green investments (green bonds, certified buildings, forests, green infrastructure); noted green bond (2019) and sustainable bond (2023) issuances to finance transition.
- CNP Assurances 2030 action plan – insurance: Embed climate in business strategy (market positioning, incentives); provide ongoing sustainability information at subscription and annually; offer sustainable retirement savings built on ESG-driven pillars.
- Reporting references: Includes tagged indicators/citations (e.g., E1_1_03, E1_3_01, E1_MDR_A_01_12, E1_3_03, E1_3_04, E1_4_23) indicating alignment with standardized sustainability reporting frameworks.

nodes.title: Contributions to decarbonisation actions
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.4 Contributions to decarbonisation actions
nodes.start_phrase: As part of the transition plan, the precise quantification of actions and associated GHG reductions remains a significant challenge beyond the operational scope.
nodes.summary:
- Mobilization of support functions for decarbonization: governance, HR, finance, sustainability, risk, data/IT, compliance, legal, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, reporting, and communications each to develop their own transition plans, supported by awareness and training initiatives.
- Decarbonization actions and measurement: current impact assessment beyond the operational scope is primarily qualitative due to data gaps and sector variability; annual monitoring used to adjust actions; the transition plan will be updated within three years as data and methodologies improve.
- Planned actions in investment and insurance:
  - Investments: update exclusion criteria in line with climate scenarios; expand financed emissions coverage; deepen ESG integration across asset classes; continue property-specific work plans; embed transition-plan analysis in shareholder engagement for high-sustainability sectors; set a new green investment target by 2026 after achieving €30bn by 2025.
  - Insurance: broaden sustainable unit-linked offerings; enhance sustainability of legacy Euro funds; improve non-financial information shared with customers.
- CNP Assurances 2030 action plan:
  - Investments: exclusion policies for coal, oil, gas; active shareholder engagement (voting, dialogue); ESG-based selection across listed/unlisted, real assets; green investments (green bonds, forests, certified buildings, green infrastructure); green bond (2019) and sustainable bond (2023) issuances to fund transition.
  - Insurance business: integrate climate change into strategy and incentives; provide sustainability information at subscription and annually; offer sustainable retirement savings based on ESG pillars.
- Financial resources and budgeting:
  - 2025–2029 transition projects phased into annual budgets; 71% of 2025 strategic projects already budgeted.
  - Dependencies include stable ESG data supply, vehicle fleet electrification, and cost-bearing capacity; no current warnings on capacity.
  - Carbon Budget oversight within La Poste Group for operational decarbonization.
  - 2025 plan: 2,188 tCO₂e reduction for €7.2m net CapEx/OpEx (€10.7m gross, including €3.1m for CNP Assurances; €3.5m costs avoided via space optimization). Allocation: 69% buildings (energy efficiency, CNP IT server outsourcing), 31% vehicles (fleet greening). In 2024, €3.4m for 139 vehicles and €5.8m for buildings.
- Consideration of locked-in (irreducible) emissions:
  - Operational: future emissions tied to IT servers and building depreciation are not a material transition risk (<1% of Group footprint) at Group level; CNP Assurances estimates ~2,691 tCO₂e/year locked-in for its scope.
  - Financed portfolios: not yet quantifiable due to pending CSRD data from portfolio companies and uncertainty in loan lifetimes/prepayments.
  - No significant CapEx in coal, oil, or gas activities (reported as zero).

nodes.title: Financial resources related to the transition plan
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.5 Financial resources related to the transition plan
nodes.start_phrase: The transition plan provides for projects for all of the Bank’s business lines between 2025 and 2029.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR/environmental), focusing on transition plan financing and treatment of irreducible (locked-in) emissions.
- Transition plan budgeting (2025–2029):
  - Annual budgeting with gradual integration of projects; as of October 2024, 71% of 2025 strategic projects are already budgeted.
  - Execution depends on stable ESG data supply, electrification of the vehicle fleet, and ability to bear costs; no current warnings on these capacities.
  - Annual budget exercises will assess dependence on financial/human resources.
- Carbon Budget monitoring:
  - Decarbonisation of own operations tracked via La Poste Group’s annual Carbon Budget tool (validated June 13, 2024).
- 2025 decarbonisation investment and impact:
  - Targeted reduction: 2,188 tCO₂e in 2025 (full GHG benefits materialize in later years).
  - Total net CapEx/OpEx: €7.2m for the Group; gross spend €10.7m (including €3.1m for CNP Assurances) offset by €3.5m in avoided expenses (space freed at La Banque Postale).
  - Allocation: 69% to buildings (energy efficiency at LBP; outsourcing CNP Assurances’ IT servers), 31% to vehicles (greening service/company fleets).
  - Real estate CapEx based on a multi-year estimate by La Poste Immobilier (Nov 2024), refined in Q1 2025.
- 2024 spend (LBP scope):
  - €3.4m for vehicles (orders for 139 vehicles) and €5.8m for buildings.
- Consideration of irreducible (locked-in) emissions:
  - Concept applied to identify future emissions tied to assets/products.
  - Operational scope: future emissions from IT servers and building depreciation exist but represent <1% of Group footprint; not treated as a 2030–2050 transition risk and not quantified at Group level.
  - CNP Assurances estimate: ~2,691 tCO₂e/year from servers and building depreciation.
  - Financed portfolios: locked-in emissions not yet quantifiable due to (1) lack of portfolio companies’ locked-in data (expected from 2025 CSRD disclosures) and (2) uncertain asset/loan lifetimes and prepayment behavior.
- Fossil-related CapEx:
  - No significant CapEx in coal, oil, or gas (all reported as €0).

nodes.title: Consideration of irreducible emissions
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.6 Consideration of irreducible emissions
nodes.start_phrase: The strategic and investment choices made today can lock in the pathway of a company’s GHG emissions for years to come.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale Group’s environmental transition planning, financing, and regulatory alignment (2025–2029), with emphasis on 2025 budgets, decarbonisation levers, locked-in emissions, and EU Green Taxonomy metrics.
- Transition plan financing and execution:
  - Annual integration of projects; for 2025, 71% of strategic projects already budgeted.
  - Key dependencies: stable ESG data supply, vehicle fleet electrification, and cost absorption; no identified warnings on capacity.
  - Annual budgeting will assess dependency of actions on available resources (financial, human, etc.).
  - Monitoring via La Poste Group’s annual Carbon Budget, validated by the Board on 13 June 2024.
- 2025 decarbonisation budget and impacts (operational scope):
  - Targeted reduction: 2,188 tCO₂e in 2025; full benefits accrue in future years.
  - Net CapEx/OpEx: €7.2m; gross spend €10.7m (incl. €3.1m for CNP Assurances); €3.5m in avoided expenses (e.g., freed-up m² at La Banque Postale).
  - Allocation: 69% to buildings (energy efficiency at La Banque Postale, outsourcing CNP Assurances’ IT servers); 31% to vehicles (fleet greening).
  - Real estate CapEx based on a multi-year estimate (Nov 2024) refined in Q1 2025 by La Poste Immobilier.
  - 2024 indicative spend: €3.4m for vehicles (139 vehicles ordered) and €5.8m for buildings.
- Consideration of irreducible/locked-in emissions:
  - Operational scope assets (IT servers, building depreciation) generate future emissions but represent <1% of Group footprint; not treated as a transition risk to 2030–2050 and not quantified at Group level.
  - CNP Assurances: estimated locked-in emissions ≈2,691 tCO₂e/year (servers and buildings).
  - Financed portfolios: locked-in emissions not yet quantifiable due to:
    - Need for counterparties’ own locked-in emission data (expected via CSRD from 2025).
    - Uncertain asset lives and loan prepayment dynamics preventing robust loan-level lock-in assessments.
  - No significant CapEx in economic activities related to coal, oil, or gas (all reported as €0).
- Link to the European Green Taxonomy:
  - Transition plan CapEx/OpEx for banking activity not directly captured by EU 2021/2178 KPIs; effects materialize through portfolio exposures.
  - Methodology aligns with regulation: assessment via counterparties’ turnover/CapEx alignment for general financing and project analysis for specialized financing.
  - At 31 Dec 2024: Green Asset Ratio (GAR, consolidated prudential scope) = 5.7% (€10.3bn) based on turnover.
    - Total assets: €321.3bn; covered assets (denominator): €180.1bn.
    - Assets analyzed for eligibility: €148.0bn; eligible assets: €92.5bn.
    - GAR contribution breakdown highlights: Real estate households 4.9 pts; unallocated exposures 0.8 pt.
  - Data limitations constrain taxonomy alignment assessment; enhanced data collection is underway per the transition plan.
  - Further detail provided in Section 2.2.6 “European Green Taxonomy.”

nodes.title: Link with the European Green Taxonomy
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.7 Link with the European Green Taxonomy
nodes.start_phrase: In the context of the banking activity, the CapEx and OpEx related to the action plans of the Bank’s transition plan are not directly affected by “the key performance indicators provided for by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178”.
nodes.summary:
- Link with the European Green Taxonomy:
  - The Bank’s transition plan CapEx/OpEx are not directly covered by KPI rules under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178; impacts are instead reflected through portfolio exposures.
  - La Banque Postale calculates and publishes its Green Asset Ratio (GAR) and related taxonomy-alignment metrics, using pillars such as counterparties’ turnover and CapEx alignment for general financing and project-level analysis for specialized financing.
  - At 31 Dec 2024, regulatory GAR (prudential scope) is 5.7% (€10.3bn) based on turnover, with key contributors including Real Estate Households (4.9 pts) and 0.8 pt unallocated.
  - Scope and methodology highlights: total assets €321.3bn; covered assets €180.1bn (excluding sovereigns, central banks, trading book); assets analyzed for eligibility €148.0bn; eligible assets €92.5bn. Covered assets further exclude companies not subject to NFRD and derivatives in the banking book. Ongoing data collection aims to address current data limitations on taxonomy alignment.

- Climate change adaptation:
  - Operational adaptation work underway with EcoAct to assess site adaptability and inform a geographically tailored adaptation plan; no standalone adaptation policy yet—work aligned with Caisse des Dépôts and set to begin in 2025.
  - CNP Assurances is executing adaptation plans to mitigate physical climate risks: reducing exposure across sovereigns, corporates, real estate, and forests; integrating climate risk into reinsurance strategy with close monitoring of treaty changes; and reinforcing resilience via regularly updated business continuity plans.

- Energy consumption and mix (Group, buildings and vehicles):
  - Reporting distinguishes fossil (natural gas, non-renewable electricity, fuel oil, propane, petrol, diesel, district heating—classified as fossil in 2024 due to unavailable source split) and renewable (purchased/produced renewable electricity, firewood, steam, cooling).
  - 2024 totals: total energy 188,360 MWh; fossil 90,125 MWh (48%); renewable 98,235 MWh (52%).
    - Of renewables: renewable fuels 2,393 MWh; purchased/acquired renewable electricity, heat, steam, cooling 95,400 MWh; self-generated non-fuel renewable 442 MWh.
  - Renewable energy production managed at Group level: 1,086 MWh total in 2024, from solar on Lemnys D and Nantes sites and 821 MWh from CNP Assurances (partly fed back to the grid).

nodes.title: Actions for climate change adaptation
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.5.8 Actions for climate change adaptation
nodes.start_phrase: Regarding climate change adaptation, in the operational scope, La Banque Postale is currently working with EcoAct to establish the degree of adaptability of its sites.
nodes.summary:
- Climate change adaptation: La Banque Postale is working with EcoAct to assess the adaptability of its sites and build a geography-based adaptation plan to strengthen climate resilience by understanding vulnerabilities to climate hazards and regional interactions. A dedicated adaptation policy for La Banque Postale is not yet in place; work coordinated with Caisse des Dépôts will begin in 2025.
- CNP Assurances’ adaptation measures: Reduces exposure to physical climate risks in investments (states, companies, buildings, forests), integrates climate risks through reinsurance coverage management and close monitoring of treaty changes, and updates its business continuity plan to enhance resilience to extreme events.
- Energy consumption and mix (2024): Reporting covers buildings and vehicles across La Banque Postale Group. Fossil sources include natural gas, non-renewable electricity, fuel oil, propane, petrol, diesel, and district heating (classified as fossil due to group methodology and lack of source breakdown in 2024). Renewable sources include purchased/produced renewable electricity, firewood, steam, and cooling. Renewables account for 52% of the energy mix; fossil fuels 48%. Key figures: total energy consumption 188,360 MWh; fossil 90,125 MWh; renewable 98,235 MWh (of which 2,393 MWh renewable fuels; 95,400 MWh purchased renewable electricity/heat/steam/cooling; 442 MWh self-generated non-fuel renewable).
- Renewable energy production (2024): Managed at group level, including solar at Lemnys D and Nantes and 821 MWh from CNP Assurances; some output is fed back to the grid. Total renewable energy produced: 1,086 MWh.

nodes.title: Total energy consumption
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.6.1 Total energy consumption
nodes.start_phrase: Energy consumption is reported for La Banque Postale Group and includes consumption from buildings and vehicles.
nodes.summary:
- Climate change adaptation:

  - Reporting covers buildings and vehicles across La Banque Postale Group.
  - Fossil energy includes natural gas, non-renewable electricity, fuel oil, propane, petrol, diesel, and district heating (counted as fossil due to methodology constraints); nuclear consumption is not material.
  - Renewable energy includes purchased/produced renewable electricity, firewood, steam, and cooling.
