nodes.title: Energy production
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.6.2 Energy production
nodes.start_phrase: Renewable energy production is now managed at La Banque Postale Group level.
nodes.summary:
- Climate change adaptation: La Banque Postale is working with EcoAct to assess site adaptability and build a Group adaptation plan that accounts for geographic vulnerabilities and regional climate interactions. A dedicated adaptation policy is not yet in place; work aligned with Caisse des Dépôts will start in 2025. CNP Assurances has adaptation plans to manage physical climate risks by reducing portfolio exposure (States, companies, buildings, forests), integrating climate risks via reinsurance management and close monitoring, and strengthening internal resilience through regular business continuity plan updates.

- Energy consumption and mix (operational scope: buildings and vehicles): Fossil sources include natural gas, non-renewable electricity, fuel oil, propane, petrol, diesel, and district heating (counted as fossil due to lack of source breakdown). Renewables include purchased/produced renewable electricity, firewood, steam, and cooling. 2024 totals: 188,360 MWh total energy; 90,125 MWh from fossil (48%); 98,235 MWh from renewables (52%), comprising 95,400 MWh purchased/acquired renewable electricity/heat/steam/cooling, 2,393 MWh renewable fuels, and 442 MWh self-generated non-fuel renewables.

- Renewable energy production: Managed at Group level; 1,086 MWh produced in 2024 from solar at Lemnys D and Nantes sites and 821 MWh by CNP Assurances, part of which was fed into the grid.

- Greenhouse gas emissions: The Group measures emissions across the full value chain. Operational targets follow the SBTi scope (excluding CNP Assurances and LCB and only partially including Scope 3), and financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15) targets are defined by intensity/temperature and detailed elsewhere. Methodologies differ by entity; for CNP Assurances, only counterparties’ Scopes 1–2 are included in the table, with an additional estimate of 82 MtCO2e for counterparties’ upstream/downstream Scope 3. In 2024, the Group expanded its operational Scope 3 perimeter for the first time, improving transparency but limiting year-on-year comparability.
  - 2024 emissions: Scope 1: 17,544 tCO2e (–11% vs 2023: 19,699); Scope 2 market-based: 1,865 tCO2e (–50% vs 2023: 3,705); Scope 2 location-based: 5,219 tCO2e.
  - Total Scope 3: 62,945,457 tCO2e, including purchased goods and services (227,595), capital goods (84,824), fuel/energy-related activities (2,036), waste (1,637), business travel (2,442), employee commuting (29,218), and investments (62,597,706).
  - Investments breakdown: banking 10.92 million tCO2e, insurance 18.918 million tCO2e, wealth and asset management 32.759 million tCO2e.
  - Total GHG emissions: 62,968,220 tCO2e (location-based) and 62,964,867 tCO2e (market-based).
  - Notes include uncertainty levels by data type and methodology.

nodes.title: Greenhouse gas emissions by scope
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.7.1 Greenhouse gas emissions by scope
nodes.start_phrase: In order to manage its low-carbon pathway, La Banque Postale Group measures the GHG emissions relating to all of its activities across its entire value chain.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and perimeter: La Banque Postale Group presents its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the full value chain to manage its low‑carbon pathway, with results shown for the entire Group (not limited to the SBTi operational target scope).
- Targets context: Operational SBTi targets (excluding CNP Assurances and LCB and only partly Scope 3) and financed emissions targets (intensity/portfolio temperature) are referenced but not detailed here; see Section 2.2.1.4.2.
- 2024 scope expansion and comparability: Operational Scope 3 coverage was broadened in 2024 (purchased goods/services across all groups, capital goods, upstream energy, plus first-time calculations for waste and business travel), improving transparency but limiting year‑on‑year comparability.
- Entities covered for financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15): La Banque Postale SA, CNP Assurances, Louvre Banque Privée, LBP AM and La Financière de l’Échiquier; methodologies are entity‑specific and detailed in the methodological section.
- Key 2024 GHG results by scope:
  - Scope 1: 17,544 tCO2e (‑11% vs 2023: 19,699).
  - Scope 2: 5,219 tCO2e (location‑based); 1,865 tCO2e (market‑based, ‑50% vs 2023: 3,705).
  - Scope 3 total: 62,945,457 tCO2e, including:
    - Cat. 1 Purchased goods/services: 227,595 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 2 Capital goods: 84,824 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 3 Fuel/energy‑related (upstream): 2,036 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 5 Waste: 1,637 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 6 Business travel: 2,442 tCO2e.
    - Cat. 7 Employee commuting: 29,218 tCO2e (stable vs 2023).
    - Cat. 15 Investments: 62,597,706 tCO2e, of which banking 10.92 Mt, insurance 18.919 Mt, wealth and asset management 32.759 Mt.
  - Total Group GHG: 62,968,220 tCO2e (location‑based) and 62,964,867 tCO2e (market‑based).
- CNP Assurances specificities: Only counterparties’ Scopes 1 and 2 included in the table; for information, additional financed Scope 3 upstream/downstream for listed equities, corporate bonds and infrastructure is estimated at 82 MtCO2e.
- Emissions intensity metrics:
  - Total GHG intensity: 1,532 tCO2e per €m of Group income (both location‑ and market‑based).
  - Financed emissions intensity (per covered exposures): banking 132; insurance 399; asset management 396; not calculated for Wealth Management due to portfolio size.
- Methodology and reporting scope: Environmental reporting includes consolidated subsidiaries and those under operational control; subsidiary 115K excluded (immaterial). Emission factors are supplied by La Poste Group based on ADEME references and updated annually; CNP reports Scopes 1–2 directly in tCO2e using ADEME factors.
- Uncertainty approach: Qualitative levels (low/medium/strong) tied to data type and extrapolation; strong uncertainty for monetary factors and indirect sources (e.g., Scope 3 Cat. 15). ADEME factor uncertainties are not directly applied except for monetary factors.
- Cross‑references: Detailed methodologies in Section 2.2.1.7.3; decarbonisation targets in Section 2.2.1.4.2; glossary of CSR terms on page 808.

nodes.title: GHG emissions intensity
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.7.2 GHG emissions intensity
nodes.start_phrase: The GHG emissions intensity is calculated on the basis of the total GHG emissions presented above, divided by La Banque Postale Group's total income(1).
nodes.summary:
- Section focus: Sustainable performance and environmental information from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, centered on GHG emissions intensity and methodology.
- Definition of GHG emissions intensity: total Group GHG emissions divided by total income; highlights that financed emissions are the dominant component, requiring a specific financed-emissions intensity metric.
- Portfolio-specific intensity approaches:
  - Banking portfolio: intensity includes counterparties’ Scopes 1, 2, and 3; residential real estate exposures use Scopes 1 and 2 only.
  - Insurance portfolio: intensity includes Scope 3 upstream and downstream financed emissions for comparability (notably 82 million tCO2e for listed equities, listed corporate bonds, and infrastructure).
  - Asset Management: includes counterparties’ Scopes 1, 2, and 3; Wealth Management excluded due to small size.
- 2024 scope and boundary updates:
  - Environmental reporting covers consolidated subsidiaries and non-consolidated entities under operational control; consolidation rules detailed elsewhere.
  - Subsidiary 115K excluded in 2024 due to very small size and office move; no material impact on comparability.
  - Major expansion of Scope 3 coverage with La Poste Group:
    - Category 1 (purchased goods and services) extended to all purchase groups.
    - Category 2 (capital goods) added.
    - Category 3 (upstream energy-related emissions) added.
    - Categories 5 (waste) and 6 (business travel) calculated for the first time.
  - Scope 3 Category 15 (investment emissions) consolidates data from CNP Assurances, LBP AM, Louvre Banque Privée (including La Financière de l’Échiquier), and La Banque Postale SA.
  - These methodological changes limit year-on-year comparability for the affected categories.
- Methodology and emission factors:
  - Emissions calculated using La Poste Group emission factors based on ADEME benchmarks; updated annually and applied consistently across entities.
  - Exception: CNP Assurances reports its own tCO2e figures using ADEME factors.
- 2024 GHG emissions intensity results:
  - Total GHG intensity per income: 1,532 tCO2e/€m (both location-based and market-based).
  - Financed emissions intensity per covered exposures:
    - Banking scope (Scopes 1–3): 132 tCO2e/€m.
    - Insurance scope (Scopes 1–3): 399 tCO2e/€m.
    - Asset management scope (Scopes 1–3): 396 tCO2e/€m.

nodes.title: Methodological information
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.7.3 Methodological information
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group’s environmental reporting scope for the calculation of GHG emissions includes subsidiaries consolidated in the Group’s financial statements and non-consolidated subsidiaries over which La Banque Postale has operational control.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale Group’s 2024 environmental reporting on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, intensity metrics, methodologies, Scope 1–3 coverage (including financed emissions), data sources, limitations, and climate-related projects.

- GHG emissions intensity:
  - Overall intensity calculated as total Group GHG emissions divided by total income; financed emissions dominate the footprint.
  - Portfolio-specific intensities provided to complement the Group-level metric:
    - Banking (financed emissions, Scopes 1–3 for counterparties; Scopes 1–2 only for residential real estate): 132 (per covered exposure).
    - Insurance (financed emissions incl. counterparty Scope 3 for comparability): 399.
    - Asset management (financed emissions incl. counterparty Scopes 1–3): 396.
  - Gross emissions intensity relative to income: 1,532 tCO2e/€m (identical location- and market-based).

- Reporting scope and 2024 methodological updates:
  - Environmental scope includes consolidated subsidiaries and non-consolidated entities under operational control; minor entity (115K) excluded without affecting comparability.
  - 2024 expansion of operational Scope 3 with La Poste Group:
    - Category 1 (purchases) extended to all spend groups; inclusion of Category 2 (capital goods) and upstream energy in Category 3; Categories 5 (waste) and 6 (business travel) now calculated.
    - These changes break comparability with prior year for affected categories.
  - Emission factors primarily from ADEME via La Poste Group; updated annually; CNP Assurances reports Scopes 1–2 directly.

- Scope 1 and 2 specifics:
  - Scope 1: company fleet fuel, building thermal energy (gas, fuel oil, propane, wood) and, new in 2024, refrigerant leaks.
  - Scope 2: electricity and district heating; both market- and location-based methods applied. Renewable electricity backed by guarantees of origin; supplier-specific factors used market-based.
  - Data gaps addressed via surface area extrapolation for select French service entities (Django, Lyon Financial Centre, Poitiers Financial Centre).
  - Contractual instruments coverage:
    - 87% of Scope 2 emissions covered by renewable electricity contracts.
    - 100% via bundled energy with attributes; 0% via non-pooled instruments.

- Scope 3 coverage, exclusions, and methods:
  - Included: Categories 1 (purchases), 2 (capital goods), 3 (fuel- and energy-related activities), 5 (waste), 6 (business travel), 7 (employee commuting), and 15 (investments).
  - Excluded/not yet reported: 4 (upstream transport/distribution—work in progress for cash transport), 8 (upstream leased assets—none reallocated), 9 (customer travel—unable to calculate 2024), 11 (use of products—method alignment ongoing), 12 (end-of-life of sold products—work ongoing, with bank card LCA noted), 10/13/14 (not applicable).
  - Methods rely on monetary emission factors (ADEME), allocation keys, extrapolations; lower reliability vs. primary data. Only 2% of operational Scope 3 uses primary data (fuel/energy-related activities, waste, business travel).
  - Employee commuting based on a 2023 mobility survey; ADEME factors applied with modal shift assumptions.
  - Data collection aligns with sustainability reporting period; no significant events affecting financed emissions; timing notes provided where reporting dates differ.

- Financed emissions (Scope 3 Category 15):
  - La Banque Postale SA scope includes residential real estate (home loans), commercial real estate, and corporate portfolios; excludes retail technical reserves (non-real estate), equities, and sovereign exposures.
  - Coverage at 30 June 2024: 26% of total technical reserves (€83bn).
  - Methods aligned with PCAF, SFDR, and Pillar III; financed share typically based on revenue (enterprise value preferred but harder to obtain).
  - Corporate emissions data prioritized from reported sources; otherwise estimated by Bloomberg/Sustainalytics; if unavailable, PCAF sector factors applied. Real estate emissions based on EPC/energy data.
  - Scope 3 of counterparties dominates financed emissions and carries higher uncertainty (e.g., for Large Corporates, ~82% of financed emissions are counterparty Scope 3).
  - Subsidiary methodologies:
    - CNP Assurances: covers equities, corporate bonds, sovereigns (domestic/Scope 1), real estate, and direct infrastructure; uses S&P Trucost and reported data; ~€331bn (80%) in scope, €254bn (60%) with data; estimates Scope 3 financed emissions for listed equities/bonds/infrastructure at ~82.3 MtCO2e; acknowledges double counting and disclosure gaps.
    - LBP AM: uses MSCI (and Carbon4Finance for LFDE); asset eligibility 74% (LBP AM) and 92% (LFDE); calculates carbon intensity/footprint incl. Scopes 1–3; data as of 31 Dec 2023.
    - Louvre Banque Privée: direct securities via Sustainalytics; UCITS via SFDR PAI published by managers at end-2024.
  - Financed emissions for LBP SA updated semi-annually; figures as of 30 June 2024.

- Biogenic emissions:
  - Not quantified for Scopes 1–3 in 2024.

- GHG reduction/offset projects:
  - Value chain: no carbon absorption projects; internal “Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund” supports emission-reduction initiatives (buildings, mobility). CNP Assurances’ forests absorbed 483,653 tCO2 in 2024 (not used for offsetting).
  - Outside value chain: since 2015, participation in La Poste Group’s “Climate + Regions” supporting French Low Carbon Label projects (mainly forestry). At La Banque Postale, 20 projects (10 certified; 2 already generating credits); also supports methodology development (e.g., hedges). Estimated sequestration: 11,455 tCO2e over project lifetimes; average cost €29/t; no reduction projects included in this portfolio.

nodes.title: Value chain projects
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.8.1 Value chain projects
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale does not support carbon absorption projects in its value chain or own operations.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document detailing CSR environmental information and sustainable performance.
- Portfolio carbon footprint methodologies:
  - Sovereign bonds: Uses UNFCCC national emissions and World Bank GDP (PPP); applies to all sovereign holdings; methodology aligned with NZAOA and PCAF, allocating national emissions by the investment’s share of GDP (PPP).
  - Real estate: Scope 1 and 2 estimated prioritizing actual consumption, EPC, location, and asset type; estimates follow PCAF when needed.
- Financed emissions data and coverage:
  - LBP AM: MSCI data; LFDE: Carbon4Finance; asset coverage for calculations is 74% (LBP AM) and 92% (LFDE); carbon intensity and footprint calculated for Scopes 1–3; data as of 31/12/2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Direct securities via Sustainalytics (primarily company-reported data, estimates if missing); UCITS via SFDR negative impact indicators provided directly by asset managers without restatement.
- Primary data use: 2% of operational Scope 3 emissions calculated with primary data (fuel- and energy-related activities, waste, business travel). Financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15) rely on external providers.
- Biogenic emissions: Not quantified for Scopes 1–3 in FY2024.
- GHG mitigation and carbon credit-related initiatives:
  - Within value chain: No support for absorption projects; supports internal reduction projects through the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund (building energy efficiency and mobility).
  - CNP Assurances forestry: Monitors annual absorption; 483,653 tCO2 gross absorbed in 2024; forests managed for services/timber, not offsets.
  - Outside value chain: “Climate + Regions” program (since 2015) with La Poste Group supports sequestration and adaptation projects in France; contributed to France’s Low Carbon Label with CNPF; 25 certified projects supported as of 01/06/2024, mainly forestry.
    - At La Banque Postale level: 20-project portfolio, 10 certified (two have generated verified credits/reductions); non-certified items include methodology development (hedges recognized; Aleppo pine silviculture not recognized).
    - Estimated lifetime sequestration: 11,455 tCO2e; average cost €29/t; portfolio contains no carbon reduction projects.

nodes.title: Projects outside the value chain
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.8.2 Projects outside the value chain
nodes.start_phrase: Since 2015, La Banque Postale has voluntarily built a “Climate + Regions” programme with two other entities of La Poste Group (the Mail Services, Parcels and Digital Services business units).
nodes.summary:
- Overview of La Banque Postale Group’s GHG accounting and environmental performance, including financed and operational emissions, data sources, and carbon credit projects and governance.
- Financed emissions methodologies:
  - Sovereign portfolio: Calculated per NZAOA/PCAF using UNFCCC domestic emissions and World Bank GDP (PPP); covers all sovereign bonds (direct and indirect).
  - Real estate portfolio: Scope 1–2 estimated from actual energy use/EPC/location/asset type, prioritizing primary data; estimates aligned with PCAF when needed.
  - Listed assets: LBP AM uses MSCI; La Financière de l’Échiquier uses Carbon4Finance; calculation coverage 74% (LBP AM) and 92% (LFDE); Scope 1–3 intensity/footprint calculated; data as of 31 Dec 2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Direct securities data from Sustainalytics (reported or estimated); UCITS data from SFDR negative impact indicators provided by management companies without restatement.
- Data quality and scope:
  - Operational Scope 3 primary data share is 2% (fuel- and energy-related activities, waste, business travel).
  - Financed emissions (Scope 3 Cat. 15) rely on multiple external data providers.
  - Biogenic CO2 emissions for Scopes 1–3 not quantified for 2024.
- Value-chain climate actions:
  - LBP does not support absorption projects in its own value chain; funds internal reduction projects via the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund (e.g., building energy efficiency, mobility).
  - CNP Assurances’ woodland assets absorbed 483,653 tCO2 in 2024; tracked for value, not used for offsetting.
- Outside value-chain carbon contributions:
  - Since 2015, “Climate + Regions” program (with La Poste Group) supports French sequestration/adaptation projects and helped catalyze the Low Carbon Label; La Poste Group leads in supporting low-carbon certified projects.
  - LBP portfolio: 20 projects, 10 certified; two have already generated credits; also supported methodology development (“Hedges” recognized; “Sylviculture du Pin d’Alep” not recognized). Estimated sequestration 11,455 tCO2e over project lifetimes at ~€29/t; portfolio comprises absorption (no reduction) projects.
  - CNP Assurances’ VCS-certified Serragem project (Brazil): replaces Amazonian firewood with biomass waste for ceramics; 9,469 tCO2e contributed in 2024; 585,959 tCO2e avoided over 11 years with 309,408 tCO2e expected over the next nine; delivers environmental and social co-benefits; not used to meet LBP’s own GHG reduction targets.
- Project selection and standards:
  - ESG panel across La Poste Group reviews projects with specialized partners (EcoAct, CNPF, Société Forestière, Carbone Farmers, CDC Biodiversité).
  - Assessment criteria include sequestration potential/certification (Low Carbon Label, Gold Standard), biodiversity and socio-economic co-benefits, carbon price, and value split.
- Credit issuance/cancellation:
  - Low Carbon Label credits are ex-post and cancelled upon DGEC recognition after N+5 external audits.
  - In 2024, LBP’s first Low Carbon Label forestry projects (1,334 tCO2e) received recognition; Serragem reduces 9,469 tCO2e per year.
- Net-zero pathway:
  - Alignment with La Poste Group’s NZE 2040 strategy; scenarios under analysis; conclusions expected Q1 2025 with a 2025 decision.
- Carbon credits summary:
  - Cancelled in 2024: 10,803 tCO2e total; 12.35% absorption, 87.65% reduction; 12.35% Low Carbon Label, 87.65% VCS; 12.35% in EU; 12.35% aligned with Paris Agreement Article 6 expectations; 2023 data not available.
  - Expected cancellations until 2026: 10,121 tCO2e.

nodes.title: Project qualification
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.8.3 Project qualification
nodes.start_phrase: Each project selected in La Banque Postale's portfolio must be presented to a selection panel bringing together the ESG experts from each contributing La Poste Group entity.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale’s sustainable performance and environmental actions, with emphasis on carbon credits, project governance, and internal carbon pricing.
- Highlights CNP Assurances’ Serragem project (launched 2007) that replaces Amazonian firewood with biomass waste (açaí kernels, sawdust) for ceramic kilns in Pará, Brazil; 2024 voluntary contribution of 9,469 tCO2e; 585,959 tCO2e avoided over 11 years and a further 309,408 tCO2e expected over the next nine years; delivers local jobs, markets, environmental actions, and social initiatives; not counted toward La Banque Postale’s GHG reduction targets; certified under the Verified Carbon Standard.
- Describes project selection by an ESG panel across La Poste Group entities, with partner presentations (EcoAct, CNPF, Société Forestière, Carbone Farmers, CDC Biodiversité) and multi-criteria assessment (carbon potential/certifications, biodiversity benefits, socio-economic co-benefits, price per tonne, revenue split).
- Explains absorption projects (natural CO2 sequestration such as afforestation, post-dieback reforestation, Arboreal City) and Low Carbon Label rules: ex-post credit cancellation upon DGEC-issued Emissions Reductions after N+5 third-party audits.
- 2024 base year milestones: first Low Carbon Label pilot forestry projects in France recognized for 1,334 tCO2e; Serragem delivers 9,469 tCO2e/year reductions; future cancellations tied to pending N+5 audits for absorption projects.
- Carbon credits canceled in 2024: total 10,803 tCO2e; 12.35% absorption vs. 87.65% reduction; 12.35% Low Carbon Label; 87.65% Verified Carbon Standard; 12.35% in the EU; 12.35% aligned with Article 6 expectations. Expected cancellations until 2026: 10,121 tCO2e.
- Net zero alignment: La Banque Postale follows La Poste Group’s NZE strategy, with scenario analysis underway toward NZE by 2040; represented on the NZE Steering Committee; conclusions due Q1 2025 with a 2025 decision.
- Internal carbon pricing mechanism (since 2015) aims to anticipate market carbon price dynamics and drive decarbonization; scope refresh planned in 2025 to fully cover the operational footprint.
- Framework built around the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund; CNP Assurances established a similar carbon and biodiversity fund in 2022.
- Dual funding dimensions: internal (building renovations/energy optimization, internal calls for projects, KPI tracking for avoided tCO2e, cost savings, ROI) and external (carbon sequestration and biodiversity projects in France and abroad, tracking tCO2e sequestered, species saved, area preserved; annual reporting to the Executive Committee).
- Results and funding: over €3 million allocated across ten editions; 103 internal projects funded avoiding over 7,529 tCO2e (e.g., energy retrofits, awareness campaigns, e-bikes/scooters, solar thermal/PV, green roofs, carpooling hub); external partnerships with CDC Biodiversité and WWF to develop national carbon sinks.
- Internal carbon price set at €60/tCO2e, informed by CDP, Institut Montaigne, and the Blanchard-Tirole Commission (≈€65/tCO2e benchmark); annual fund budgets calculated as GHG emissions multiplied by the internal price.
- Budget inputs: banking scope uses year N-2 emissions (Scopes 1 and 2: 5,278 and 1,876 tCO2e; Scope 3 operational: 31,819 tCO2e) due to project lead times; insurance scope uses year N emissions (Scopes 1 and 2: 1,495 and 276 tCO2e; Scope 3 travel/commuting: 6,525 tCO2e).

nodes.title: Internal carbon price
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.9 Internal carbon price
nodes.start_phrase: Since 2015, La Banque Postale has structured an internal carbon pricing mechanism with a dual ambition:
nodes.summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale’s internal carbon pricing mechanism, launched in 2015, designed to both anticipate market carbon price impacts for climate risk management and drive decarbonization targets, with scope expansion work planned for 2025.
- Central role of the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund (and CNP Assurances’ analogous fund since 2022) to monetize the Group’s carbon footprint and finance:
  - Internal projects: building renovation/energy optimization and internal calls for projects, with annual monitoring of environmental/economic gains and ROI (tCO2e avoided, euros saved).
  - External projects: carbon sequestration in France and abroad and biodiversity conservation, tracking tCO2e sequestered, species saved, and area preserved; results reported annually to the Executive Committee.
- Outcomes and resourcing:
  - Over €3 million allocated across the first ten editions; 103 internal projects financed, avoiding more than 7,529 tCO2e; examples include energy retrofits, awareness campaigns, e-mobility fleets, solar installations, green roofs, and carpooling hubs.
  - External partnerships with CDC Biodiversité and WWF to develop innovative national carbon sinks.
- Internal carbon price set at €60/tCO2e, aligned with recommendations (CDP, Institut Montaigne, Blanchard‑Tirole Commission ~€65/tCO2e for EU finance).
- Annual fund budgets derived from GHG emissions × internal carbon price:
  - Banking scope uses year N‑2 emissions: SBTi Scope 1 = 5,278 tCO2e; Scope 2 = 1,876 tCO2e; operational Scope 3 = 31,819 tCO2e.
  - Insurance scope uses year N: Scope 1 = 1,495 tCO2e; Scope 2 = 276 tCO2e; Scope 3 (business travel and commuting) = 6,525 tCO2e.
- Coverage via internal carbon pricing: 100% of Scope 1 and Scope 2; 35% of partial operational Scope 3.
- Anticipated financial effects of climate-related risks: reporting timing determined; detailed metrics disclosed under Pillar III elsewhere in the document (exposures to acute/chronic physical risks and real estate energy efficiency distribution).
- Operational GHG management indicators and trends:
  - Buildings CO2 (tCO2e): 18,421 (2022), 13,821 (2023), 13,071 (2024) – continuing decrease.
  - Vehicle emissions: 6,158 (2022), 5,540 (2023), 6,338 (2024) – +14% from 2023 to 2024 due to phased vehicle policy rollout and improved fleet estimation.
  - IT and data centers: 10,544 (2022), 9,651 (2023), 9,069 (2024) – 6% decrease from 2023 to 2024 via data center optimization, equipment life extension/reuse, responsible purchasing (EPEAT), and employee awareness/training.
  - Transition to the “Aguaro” measurement tool in 2024 improved precision, reliability, and traceability of carbon data.
- Alignment with SBTi and mission-led commitments:
  - Monitoring of low‑carbon pathway indicators within the operational scope supports climate action, stakeholder accountability, and credibility.
  - SBTi Scope 1 & 2 emissions: 6,389 tCO2e (2023), 6,260 tCO2e (2024), with a 2030 target of 3,823 tCO2e.
- Governance: annual indicator reviews and impact reporting to the Executive Committee to assess system relevance and progress toward reduction targets.

nodes.title: Anticipated financial effects of climate-related risks
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.10 Anticipated financial effects of climate-related risks
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has chosen to determine the reporting deadline for this information.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (with CSR glossary reference).  
- Climate-related financial effects: The Group sets its reporting timeline but points readers to existing Pillar III disclosures for:
  - Assets exposed to physical risk (model 5) and indicators of potential climate change physical risk (Section 6.8.8).
  - Location of assets with significant physical risk and physical risk measurement approach (Section 6.8.4.2 and 6.8.4.2.1).
  - Real estate assets by energy efficiency class and transition risk indicators (model 2) for loans collateralised by property (Section 6.8.7.2).
- Additional entity-specific indicators:
  - GHG emissions management across buildings, vehicles, and digital/IT.
    - Vehicles: +14% emissions from 2023 to 2024, linked to gradual vehicle policy rollout and improved fleet estimation.
    - IT and data centres: −6% from 2023 to 2024, driven by data centre optimisation (cooling, temperature regulation, space management), equipment life extension and reuse, responsible purchasing (EPEAT), and employee awareness/training.
    - Transition from “Green Argile” to “Aguaro” tool in 2024 improved precision, reliability, and traceability of carbon data.
  - Alignment with mission-led company status and SBTi: monitoring low‑carbon pathway indicators within operational scope to support climate action, stakeholder responsibility, and credibility.
  - Impact financing: tracking indicators that reflect commitments and actions to finance environmental solutions, aligned with La Banque Postale’s mission-led metrics and CNP’s company purpose.
- Key operational GHG metrics (tCO2e):
  - Buildings: 18,421 (2022) → 13,821 (2023) → 13,071 (2024).
  - Vehicles: 6,158 (2022) → 5,540 (2023) → 6,338 (2024).
  - IT equipment and data centres: 10,544 (2022) → 9,651 (2023) → 9,069 (2024).
- SBTi Scope 1 & 2 trajectory (tCO2e): 6,389 (2023) → 6,260 (2024) vs 2030 target of 3,823.

nodes.title: GHG emissions management indicators
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.11.1 GHG emissions management indicators
nodes.start_phrase: To manage its low-carbon pathway in its operational scope, La Banque Postale specifically monitors emissions related to buildings, vehicles and digital technology.
nodes.summary:
- Focuses on environmental information within La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, specifically the anticipated financial effects of climate-related risks and entity-specific performance indicators.
- States that disclosures on climate-related financial risks follow Pillar III reporting, with cross-references to:
  - Assets exposed to physical risk (acute and chronic) and related indicators (Section 6.8.8).
  - Geographic location of assets with significant physical risk and measurement approach (Sections 6.8.4.2 and 6.8.4.2.1).
  - Energy efficiency of real estate collateral as a transition-risk indicator (Section 6.8.7.2).
- Presents GHG emissions management indicators for the operational scope (buildings, vehicles, digital/IT):
  - Vehicle fleet emissions rose 14% from 2023 to 2024 due to phased vehicle policy implementation and improved fleet estimation.
  - IT and data centre emissions fell 6% from 2023 to 2024 through data centre optimization (cooling, temperature, space), equipment life extension and reuse (including donations to SSE), responsible purchasing (EPEAT-certified equipment, CSR criteria), and staff awareness/training.
  - Adoption of the “Aguaro” measurement tool in 2024 improved precision, reliability, and traceability of carbon data.
- Connects these indicators to the company’s mission-led status and SBTi-aligned low-carbon pathway, emphasizing credibility, stakeholder responsibility, and contribution to climate action.
- Includes trend data:
  - Buildings CO2 emissions down from 18,421 tCO2e (2022) to 13,071 (2024).
  - Vehicle emissions: 6,158 (2022), 5,540 (2023), 6,338 (2024).
  - IT/data centres: 10,544 (2022), 9,651 (2023), 9,069 (2024).
  - SBTi Scope 1 & 2 emissions: 6,389 (2023) to 6,260 (2024), with a 2030 target of 3,823 tCO2e.
- Notes management indicators for impact financing, reflecting the Group’s commitments to fund environmental solutions, monitored under La Banque Postale’s mission-led framework and CNP’s company purpose.

nodes.title: Management indicators related to impact financing
nodes.heading: 2.2.1.11.2 Management indicators related to impact financing
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group’s commitments and actions to finance environmental solutions are reflected in indicators monitored as part of La Banque Postale’s status as a mission-led company, and in CNP’s company purpose.
nodes.summary:
- Climate-related risk disclosure: Key data (exposures to physical risk, location of high-risk assets, and real estate energy efficiency) is reported under Pillar III and referenced to specific sections of the Universal Registration Document.
- Operational GHG management focus: Buildings, vehicle fleet, and digital (IT/data centers).
- 2023–2024 emissions trends: Vehicle emissions up 14% (policy rollout and better fleet estimation); IT/data center emissions down 6% (data center optimization, equipment life extension/donations, responsible purchasing favoring EPEAT, staff training).
- Measurement enhancement: Migration from Green Argile to Aguaro tool in 2024 improved carbon data precision, reliability, and traceability.
- SBTi-aligned pathway and mission-led status: Scope 1 & 2 emissions at 6,260 tCO2e in 2024 vs 3,823 tCO2e target for 2030; operational emissions in 2024—buildings 13,071 tCO2e, vehicles 6,338 tCO2e, IT 9,069 tCO2e.
- Renewable energy financing: Target €5.6bn in commitments by 2025; 2024 annual production lower due to strong market competition; strategic diversification into batteries, hydrogen, and grid balancing with strict selectivity.
- Impact measurement: Proprietary Impact Weighting Factor (IWF) covered 73% of activities in 2024; target ≥87% by end-2025.
- CNP Assurances investments: Impact investments reached €1.7bn by end-2024 (exceeding 2025 pledge of €1bn); green investments €29.4bn (CNP SA and subsidiaries), tracking to ≥€30bn by end-2025.
- Green loans to local authorities: EU Taxonomy-aligned since 2022; outstanding €1.5bn as of 31 Dec 2024, already beyond the 2025 target.
- Key impact finance metrics: Renewables deployed production €5,039m (2024; target €5,600m in 2025); annual production €453m (2024); renewables commitments €2,621m (2024); green loan annual production €1,563m (2024).
- Biodiversity materiality: Not material for own operations; material via financed activities in sectors exerting significant pressure on nature (e.g., soil degradation/deforestation, pollution, ecosystem pressures, GHGs).
- Biodiversity transition approach: Integrating climate–nature linkages; supporting sector transformations (agriculture, chemicals, mining); participation in “Roquelaure Entreprises et Biodiversité”; initial qualitative TNFD-based scenario analysis for 2030/2050; 2024 Climate & Nature report focused on Corporate & Investment Banking; plan to adopt a combined climate–nature transition plan by 2028.
- Policy alignment: Roadmap guided by the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and a double materiality lens (financial dependence on natural capital and corporate impacts on nature).

nodes.title: Material IROs related to biodiversity and ecosystems
nodes.heading: 2.2.2.1 Material IROs related to biodiversity and ecosystems
nodes.start_phrase: The double materiality analysis shows that biodiversity is not material for La Banque Postale for its own operations and service activities.
nodes.summary:
- Section focus: Preserving biodiversity and ecosystems within La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Environmental information).
- Materiality: Biodiversity is not material for the Bank’s own operations/services; it is material through financed activities that pressure nature (e.g., soil degradation, pollution, ecosystem stress, GHG emissions). Soil degradation includes land degradation, desertification, and soil sealing, potentially driven by deforestation.
- Transition plan approach: Financial institutions must integrate climate–nature interlinkages, addressing synergies/trade-offs and transforming operations, value chains, and portfolios to align financial flows with climate goals and biodiversity preservation.
- Sector engagement: La Banque Postale supports transformative initiatives in high-impact sectors (agriculture, chemicals, mining) and participates in market initiatives such as “Roquelaure Entreprises et Biodiversité” aligned with France’s national biodiversity strategy.
- Scenario analysis: Initial qualitative TNFD-aligned scenarios for 2030 and 2050 assess biodiversity and ecosystem risks/opportunities, reflecting the absence of agreed quantitative nature scenarios.
- Governance and reporting: The 2024 Climate and Nature report details integration of nature into risk management and decision-making, initially for Corporate and Investment Banking, with plans to extend across the Group.
- Target timeline: Commitment to adopt an integrated climate-and-nature transition plan by no later than 2028.
- Policy alignment: Roadmap aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, using a double materiality lens—financial materiality (dependency on natural capital) and impact materiality (corporate impacts on nature).

nodes.title: Transition plan
nodes.heading: 2.2.2.2 Transition plan
nodes.start_phrase: The consensus is confirmed on the need for financial institutions to recognise the link between climate and nature, taking into account the potential synergies and trade-offs between these two topics.
nodes.summary:
- Focus area: Preserving biodiversity and ecosystems within La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR/Environmental section).
- Materiality: Biodiversity is not material for the bank’s own operations and services; it is material through financed activities in sectors that pressure nature (e.g., soil degradation, pollution, ecosystem stress, GHG emissions; soil degradation includes land degradation, desertification, soil sealing, and can stem from deforestation).
- Transition plan: Emphasizes integrating climate and nature, moving beyond decarbonization to transform operations, value chains, and portfolios; aims to align financial flows with climate imperatives and biodiversity preservation via a holistic approach. The bank supports transformative initiatives in high-impact sectors (agriculture, chemicals, mining) and participates in market initiatives such as “Roquelaure Entreprises et Biodiversité” tied to France’s national biodiversity strategy.
- Scenario analysis: Conducted an initial, qualitative TNFD-aligned scenario analysis of biodiversity and ecosystem risks/opportunities for 2030 and 2050, reflecting the current absence of agreed quantified nature scenarios.
- Reporting and scope: The 2024 Climate and Nature report details integration of nature into risk management and decision-making, initially covering Corporate and Investment Banking, with plans to extend to other Group entities.
- Targets: Commitment to adopt an integrated climate-and-nature transition plan by no later than 2028 to ensure consistency and target alignment.
- Policies and frameworks: Alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework using a double materiality approach—financial materiality (dependence on natural capital/ecosystem services) and impact materiality (company impacts on nature).

nodes.title: Policies related to biodiversity and ecosystems
nodes.heading: 2.2.2.3 Policies related to biodiversity and ecosystems
nodes.start_phrase: Fully aware of the major challenges and guidelines of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), La Banque Postale Group is calling up all the action levers at its disposal to align its roadmap with this agreement, based on a “double materiality” approach:
nodes.summary:
- Scope and materiality: Biodiversity is not deemed material for La Banque Postale’s own operations and services, but is material through financed activities in sectors that pressure nature (e.g., soil degradation, pollution, ecosystem stress, GHGs; soil degradation includes land degradation, desertification, soil sealing, and can result from deforestation).

- Transition plan and strategy: The bank recognizes climate–nature interdependence and plans a combined climate and nature transition plan by 2028, targeting transformation of operations, value chains, and portfolios, and aligning financial flows with climate and biodiversity goals. It supports sectoral transitions (agriculture, chemicals, mining) and participates in market initiatives such as “Roquelaure Entreprises et Biodiversité” tied to France’s national biodiversity strategy.

- Risk and scenario analysis: An initial qualitative TNFD-aligned scenario analysis (2030/2050) identifies biodiversity and ecosystem risks and opportunities; qualitative approach used due to lack of agreed quantified nature scenarios. The 2024 Climate and Nature report details integration of nature into risk management and decision-making, starting with Corporate and Investment Banking and to be extended group-wide.

- Policy alignment and governance: The Group aligns with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and Caisse des Dépôts’ biodiversity policy built on four pillars: measuring footprint and risks; reducing negative impacts; increasing positive impacts; and contributing to research, training, and awareness. It also participates in the Group’s Water policy for freshwater-related biodiversity.

- Internal policies and exclusions:
  - Deforestation and ecosystem conversion: 2023 intervention principles for high-risk sectors, applicable to Large Corporates financing/investment; implementation overseen by the Group Risk Management Committee.
  - Responsible Financing and Investment Charter: Restricts financing/investment in companies with ≥20% revenue from agricultural pesticides (herbicides, fungicides, insecticides).

- Subsidiary actions:
  - CNP Assurances: Engaged with the Institute for Sustainable Finance on deforestation, member of Nature Action 100; Sustainability Department oversees climate and biodiversity; Climate Risk Committee expanded to include biodiversity; due diligence includes biodiversity.
  - LBP AM: Signatory of the Finance for Biodiversity Pledge; biodiversity policy addresses 18/23 KMGBF targets with commitments, exclusions, and advocacy; annual updates, time-bound exclusion lists, and quarterly reporting.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: Biodiversity strategy under LEC Article 29; excludes harmful sectors (e.g., unconventional pesticides, fossil fuels); integrates biodiversity controversies; monitors Principal Adverse Impacts (PAIs) into risk ratings affecting exclusions and SFDR classification; overseen by Directors of Discretionary Management and Sustainability.

nodes.title: La Banque Postale’s policies and commitments
nodes.heading: La Banque Postale’s policies and commitments
nodes.start_phrase: In December 2023, La Banque Postale developed intervention principles for companies in sectors at risk of deforestation and ecosystem conversion.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale Group’s biodiversity strategy within its CSR and environmental commitments.
- Alignment with Caisse des Dépôts’ 2022 biodiversity policy structured around four pillars: measuring footprint and risks; reducing direct/indirect negative impacts; increasing positive impacts; and contributing to research, training, and awareness.
- Specific attention to aquatic ecosystems through participation in Caisse des Dépôts Group’s Water policy.
- Introduction (Dec 2023) of intervention principles for clients in deforestation and ecosystem-conversion risk sectors, applying to Large Corporates’ financing and investment; oversight by the Group Risk Management Committee, which includes the Executive Board Chair.
- Application of the Responsible Financing and Investment Charter, including a restrictive policy on financing/investing in companies with ≥20% revenue from agricultural pesticides.
- Subsidiaries’ aligned actions:
  - CNP Assurances: engagement with the Institute for Sustainable Finance on deforestation; member of Nature Action 100; Sustainability Department leads climate/biodiversity; Climate Risk Committee expanded to biodiversity; integration of climate and biodiversity risks across investment, insurance, and operations; due diligence incorporates biodiversity.
  - LBP AM: signatory of the Finance for Biodiversity Pledge; biodiversity policy guided by material pressures; meets 18/23 Kunming-Montreal GBF targets via engagement, exclusions, and advocacy; annual policy updates, scheduled exclusion list reviews, and quarterly reporting to internal committees.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: biodiversity strategy under Article 29 of the Energy-Climate Law; exclusions for sectors harmful to biodiversity (e.g., unconventional pesticides, fossil fuels); assessment of biodiversity-related controversies with potential exclusions; integration of Principal Adverse Impacts into risk ratings influencing exclusion and SFDR metrics; implementation led by the Directors of Discretionary Management and Sustainability.
- Cross-references provided for further details on exclusion and due diligence policies, and a glossary for CSR terms.

nodes.title: Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
nodes.heading: Policies and commitments of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the Group approach, La Banque Postale’s subsidiaries have rolled out policies in line with their specific business.
nodes.summary:
- The Group aligns its biodiversity approach with Caisse des Dépôts’ 2022 policy built on four pillars: measuring footprint and risks; reducing direct/indirect negative impacts; increasing positive impacts; and contributing to research, training, and awareness. It also participates in the Group’s freshwater (water) policy.
- In 2023, La Banque Postale set intervention principles for companies in sectors at risk of deforestation/ecosystem conversion, applying to Large Corporates financing and investment within Corporate and Local Development Banking; implementation overseen by the Group Risk Management Committee.
- A Responsible Financing and Investment Charter guides business lending and financing, including a restrictive policy toward companies deriving ≥20% of revenue from agricultural pesticides.
- Subsidiary policies:
  - CNP Assurances: engages via the Institute for Sustainable Finance on deforestation; joined Nature Action 100 (2023); manages climate/biodiversity at Group level via the Sustainability Department and an expanded Climate Risk Committee; integrates climate and biodiversity risks across investments, insurance, and operations; due diligence covers biodiversity.
  - LBP AM: signatory to the Finance for Biodiversity Pledge; biodiversity policy addresses 18 of 23 Kunming-Montreal GBF targets with concrete actions on engagement, exclusion, and advocacy; policy updated annually with predefined exclusion list timelines and quarterly reporting.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: biodiversity strategy for discretionary management (per France’s Energy-Climate Law, Article 29); excludes harmful sectors (e.g., unconventional pesticides, fossil fuels); applies controversy-based exclusions; monitors PAIs and integrates them into risk ratings; responsibility lies with the Directors of Discretionary Management and Sustainability.
- Deforestation focus:
  - Uses FORESTIQ databases to flag customers at high risk of deforestation, ecosystem conversion, or related human rights violations.
  - Engagement strategy aligned with the EU Regulation on deforestation-free products (RDUE/EUDR), requiring zero deforestation, compliance with producer-country law, and a due diligence statement.
  - Scope covers coffee, cocoa, rubber, oil palm, soy, cattle, wood and certain derivatives; all EU operators/traders are in scope.
  - La Banque Postale will not lend to or invest in operators/traders of these commodities without a recognized deforestation-prevention policy.
  - Potentially exposed customers undergo an in-depth risk and commitment assessment by the Sustainability Department; an internal procedure defines roles, responsibilities, and process steps across corporate banking and markets teams.
  - CNP Assurances excludes new investments in companies operating/trading in the listed commodities without a recognized anti-deforestation policy.
  - LBP AM applies cross-cutting exclusions for high-risk agricultural producers/traders lacking sufficient prevention measures, with a risk-based focus on upstream value-chain actors.

nodes.title: Addressing deforestation, a major focus of the Group’s biodiversity policy

- Strict financing and investment stance: no lending or investing in operators/traders lacking a recognized deforestation-prevention policy; in-depth sustainability risk and commitment assessments for exposed clients; formal internal procedures defining roles, responsibilities, and steps.
- Group-wide alignment: CNP Assurances excludes new investments in companies in listed commodities without credible anti-deforestation policies; LBP AM excludes high-risk producers/traders lacking adequate prevention, focusing on upstream value chain links.
- Acknowledgement of no current sustainable land management/agriculture policy, with plans to develop one.
- Biodiversity action plans: measurement of impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities across the value chain; development of a science-based roadmap to reduce ecosystem impacts and restore biodiversity.
- Early adoption of TNFD (Sept 2023) and integration with CSRD impact analysis.
- Mapping of targeted biodiversity impacts across Group policies (CDC, La Banque Postale, LBP AM, CNP), addressing pressures such as land-use change, overexploitation, climate change, pollution, invasive species, pesticide impacts, species status, and ecosystem condition.

nodes.title: Measuring the impacts and dependencies of the financed activities on biodiversity (La Banque Postale)
nodes.heading: Measuring the impacts and dependencies of the financed activities on biodiversity (La Banque Postale)
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale measures the impacts, dependencies, risks and opportunities of its activity in relation to nature throughout its value chain to understand its relationship with living things.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale’s biodiversity and ecosystems action plans within its Sustainable Performance/Environmental Information, acknowledging it currently has no dedicated sustainable land or agriculture policy but plans to develop one.
- Frameworks and approach: Early adopter of TNFD (Sept 2023); applies the TNFD LEAP process (Locate, Evaluate, Assess, Prepare) and the Global Biodiversity Score (GBS) from CDC Biodiversité to measure impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities across the value chain as a basis for a science-based roadmap to protect and restore biodiversity.
- Portfolio coverage and methods: Conducted an in-depth nature-related analysis on 39% of its financing portfolio (residential and commercial real estate, commercial, corporates, public sector and social economy). Combined “Locate” and “Evaluate” phases with sector-specific qualitative grids for priority sectors: real estate; food and beverage manufacturing; transport and warehousing; energy production and distribution; health and pharmaceuticals.
- Key findings on impacts and risks:
  - Corporate and public/social portfolios’ impacts mainly occur upstream in financed companies’ supply chains.
  - Terrestrial impacts largely from land use and climate change; freshwater impacts from pollution and wetland conversion.
  - High-impact activities in sensitive areas face elevated transition risk; nature-based activities in degraded areas face significant physical risk.
  - Identified top contributing companies to inform potential engagement policies.
- Dependencies on ecosystem services:
  - 62% of the Corporate portfolio technical reserves finance activities critically dependent on at least one ecosystem service; most exposed sectors: real estate, telecommunications, construction.
  - Most common dependencies: water-related services (surface and groundwater); highest dependency: soil stabilisation and erosion control.
- Measurement limitations and next steps:
  - Current exclusions: retail banking direct reserves (ex-real estate), equity securities, sovereign exposures (sovereign bonds, Banque de France technical reserves, centralized passbook savings) due to limited methodologies/data.
  - Measurements rely mainly on financial data; plans to enhance accuracy with physical, pressure-specific indicators (including climate change) for better management.
- Policies and governance landscape:
  - Group references include CDC Biodiversity and Water policies, Group Deforestation & Ecosystem Conversion policy, La Banque Postale’s Financing & Investment Charter, LBP AM Biodiversity policy, and CNP Assurances due diligence on principal adverse impacts.
  - Targeted material negative impacts and biodiversity erosion vectors include: land-use change, overexploitation, climate change, pollution, invasive species, species status, ecosystem condition (e.g., land degradation, desertification, soil sealing), and ecosystem services (e.g., pesticides).
- Financing biodiversity outcomes (Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund):
  - Supports biodiversity credits measurement and generation with CDC Biodiversité at the Cros du Mouton site (Var); funded two voluntary restoration/rewilding units in 2024 (€99,600 excl. tax).
  - Backs WWF France Nature Impact (payments for ecosystem services) to preserve, restore, and sustainably manage high-biodiversity forests in mainland France.
  - Ensures decarbonisation projects deliver biodiversity co-benefits (species diversity in reforestation, protection of water points, agroforestry and reforestation practices).
- Subsidiary actions (CNP Assurances):
  - Integrates biodiversity into ESG filters for listed equities and bonds, assessing disruption of fragile areas, biodiversity programs, land use, resource controversies, water dependency and discharge treatment.
  - “Green Works” charter for real estate mandates biodiversity protection in construction and operations: ecosystem respect, low-impact materials, waste and water reduction, plant- and biodiversity-promoting technical solutions, circular economy (reuse), and ecosystem services in buildings/green spaces.
  - Applies sustainable management principles to 54,986 hectares of owned forests via Société Forestière de la Caisse des Dépôts.

nodes.title: Actions of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
nodes.heading: Actions of La Banque Postale Group subsidiaries
nodes.start_phrase: CNP Assurances includes biodiversity in the ESG filters of listed equities and bonds.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and approach: La Banque Postale analyzed nature-related impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities on 39% of its financing portfolio using the TNFD LEAP framework and the Global Biodiversity Score (GBS). Sector-specific qualitative grids complemented quantitative footprints for five priority sectors: real estate; food and beverage manufacturing; transport and warehousing; energy production and distribution; health and pharmaceuticals.

- Key findings and risk assessment:
  - Impacts in corporate and public/social economy portfolios are mainly in upstream value chains (supplier purchases).
  - Terrestrial impacts are driven by land use and climate change; freshwater impacts by pollution and wetland conversion.
  - High-impact activities in sensitive areas face elevated transition risks; nature-based activities in degraded areas face significant physical risks.
  - Dependencies: 62% of Corporate portfolio technical reserves finance activities critically dependent on at least one ecosystem service (notably real estate, telecoms, construction). Widespread dependency on water-related services; highest on soil stabilization and erosion control.
  - Identification of main company contributors informs engagement policies.

- Measurement limits and data needs:
  - Exclusions due to methodology/data gaps: retail banking direct reserves (excluding real estate), equity securities, sovereign exposures (sovereign bonds, Banque de France technical reserves, centralized passbook savings).
  - Current measurements rely largely on financial data; plan to add physical, pressure-specific indicators (including climate) tailored to LBP’s financing.

- Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund:
  - Finances biodiversity protection/restoration and decarbonization projects with biodiversity co-benefits.
  - 2024 actions: support for biodiversity credit generation/measurement with CDC Biodiversité at Cros du Mouton (Var); purchase of two voluntary restoration/rewilding units (€99,600 excl. tax).
  - Supports WWF France’s Nature Impact (payments for ecosystem services) for high-biodiversity forests in mainland France; promotes species diversity, water point preservation, agroforestry, and reforestation.

- Subsidiary actions:
  - CNP Assurances:
    - Integrates biodiversity in ESG filters for listed equities/bonds, addressing land use, fragile area disruption, resource controversies, water dependency/discharges.
    - “Green Works” charter for real estate to protect ecosystems, favor low-impact materials, reduce waste/water use, and promote biodiversity/circularity; sustainable management of 54,986 ha of forests.
    - Shareholder engagement embeds biodiversity; 2024: topic in 31% of direct dialogues (five companies).
    - Measures portfolio dependency on ecosystem services via BIA-GBS (covers 98% of directly held equities/bonds).
    - Participates in the 2024 “biodiversity marketplace initiative” with 11 institutional investors to advance methodologies and biodiversity goals.
  - LBP AM:
    - Conducts engagements on sustainable proteins, water, deforestation, pesticides, pollution; monitors portfolio biodiversity footprint.
    - SRI Analysis and Research team (10 people) and specialized data providers; launched a cross-sector Biodiversity rating in 2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée:
    - Since 2024, measures biodiversity footprint with BIA-GBS; redesigning methodology to integrate UCITS.
    - Uses footprint to pinpoint pressures and main contributors and to guide company dialogues; invested in data and expanded ESG team (five officers).
    - Since Jan 1, 2023, all mandates must include biodiversity considerations.

- Internal awareness and practices:
  - Group-wide biodiversity e-learning available since February 2022.
  - No reliance on biodiversity offsets; focus on impact reduction and preservation via the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund.
  - Nature-based solutions: investment in WWF France’s Nature Impact for forest preservation/restoration; local/indigenous knowledge not yet integrated.

- Targets and progress:
  - CNP Assurances: commit to measure biodiversity across entire forest portfolio by end-2025 (92% inventoried via IBP method by end-2024); allocate 3% of woodland to older/natural growth areas by end-2025.
  - LBP will consider quantified impact-reduction targets following 2023–2024 assessments, contingent on improved measurement accuracy, methodologies, and higher-quality data.

nodes.title: Employee awareness
nodes.heading: Employee awareness
nodes.start_phrase: The Group is raising its teams’ awareness of biodiversity issues, primarily by way of a biodiversity e-learning module which has been available to all employees since February 2022.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Environmental information) focusing on biodiversity strategy, actions, measurement, engagement, and targets across Group entities.

- Shareholder engagement and policy integration:
  - CNP Assurances has embedded biodiversity into its shareholder engagement, holding direct dialogues with companies (31% of 2024 conversations) to drive ambitious biodiversity action and disclosure of biodiversity-related risks.
  - It participates with 10 other institutional investors in a 2024 “biodiversity marketplace initiative” to develop robust methodologies for integrating biodiversity into financial management and to support international biodiversity goals.
  - LBP AM runs engagement campaigns on sustainable proteins, water, deforestation, pesticide use, and pollution; it aims to raise awareness, promote best practices, and monitors portfolio biodiversity footprints.

- Measurement, tools, and data:
  - CNP Assurances assesses portfolio company dependencies on ecosystem services using BIA-GBS, covering 98% of its directly held equity and bond portfolios.
  - LBP AM’s 10-person SRI Analysis and Research team, supported by specialized data providers, developed a cross-sector Biodiversity rating in 2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée began measuring its biodiversity footprint with BIA-GBS in 2024, is redesigning its methodology to include UCITS, and uses results to identify main pressures and contributors and to initiate company dialogues. It has expanded ESG resources (five ESG officers) and subscribed to dedicated data services.
  - Since January 1, 2023, all Louvre Banque Privée management mandates incorporate biodiversity considerations in investment policies.

- Internal awareness and capacity building:
  - Group-wide biodiversity e-learning module available to all employees since February 2022.

- Offsets, nature-based solutions, and local knowledge:
  - La Banque Postale does not use biodiversity offsets; it prioritizes reducing its environmental footprint and preserving biodiversity, including financing projects via the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund.
  - It invests in WWF France’s Nature Impact initiative, a nature-based solution fund for protecting, restoring, and sustainably managing forests in mainland France to deliver biodiversity protection and carbon sequestration.
  - Local and indigenous knowledge has not yet been integrated into its biodiversity actions.

- Targets and results:
  - CNP Assurances SA and its French subsidiaries target full biodiversity measurement of their forest portfolio by end-2025 (92% inventoried by end-2024 using the IBP method) and commit to allocate 3% of woodland to older and natural growth areas by end-2025.
  - Following 2023–2024 assessments of impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities, La Banque Postale will work toward quantified biodiversity impact-reduction targets, contingent on improved measurement accuracy, target-setting methodologies, and higher-quality data.

- Reference: A glossary of CSR terms is available (page 808).

nodes.title: Targets and results related to biodiversity and ecosystems
nodes.heading: 2.2.2.5 Targets and results related to biodiversity and ecosystems
nodes.start_phrase: Concerning the sustainable management of forests, CNP Assurances SA and its French subsidiaries have undertaken to measure the biodiversity of their entire forest portfolio by the end of 2025 (92% of the surface area of the portfolio has been inventoried using the IBP method, developed by the National Forest Ownership Centre (Centre national de la propriété forestière – CNPF) at the end of 2024).
nodes.summary:
- Focus of the excerpt: how La Banque Postale Group and its asset management entities integrate biodiversity and pollution considerations into strategy, stewardship, measurement, targets, and reporting within the 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Environmental information).

- Stewardship and market initiatives
  - CNP Assurances has embedded biodiversity into its shareholder engagement, discussing the topic with five companies in 2024 (31% of direct dialogues), encouraging ambitious corporate actions and disclosure on biodiversity risks.
  - CNP Assurances measures portfolio companies’ dependencies on ecosystem services using the BIA-GBS methodology, covering 98% of directly held equity and bond portfolios; participates with 10 other institutional investors in the 2024 “biodiversity marketplace initiative” to advance methodologies and investor practices.
  - LBP AM runs collaborative engagement on sustainable proteins, water, deforestation, pesticides, and pollution; monitors portfolio biodiversity footprint; uses a 10-person SRI research team and specialized data providers; launched a cross-sector Biodiversity rating in 2023.
  - Louvre Banque Privée began measuring its biodiversity footprint in 2024 with BIA-GBS, is redesigning methodology to integrate UCITS, and will use results to identify main pressures/contributors and engage companies on action plans. It has increased data resources and expanded its discretionary management ESG team to five officers. Since 1 Jan 2023, all management mandates include biodiversity considerations.

- Internal awareness, offsets, and nature-based solutions
  - Group-wide employee awareness via a biodiversity e-learning module available since February 2022.
  - No use of biodiversity offsets; the Group prioritizes footprint reduction and biodiversity preservation, notably via the Climate and Biodiversity Impact Fund.
  - Investment in WWF France’s Nature Impact initiative (a Nature-based Solution) targeting forest preservation, restoration, and sustainable management in mainland France.
  - Local and indigenous knowledge has not yet been integrated into biodiversity actions.

- Targets and progress on forests and impact-setting
  - CNP Assurances SA and French subsidiaries: measure biodiversity across the entire forest portfolio by end-2025 (92% of the area inventoried with the CNPF IBP method by end-2024) and allocate 3% of woodland to older/natural growth by end-2025.
  - Following 2023–2024 assessment of impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities, La Banque Postale plans to set quantified impact-reduction targets as methodologies, data quality, and measurement accuracy improve.

- Biodiversity footprint indicators
  - La Banque Postale (four portfolios, 39% of financing portfolio) uses Global Biodiversity Score (MSA.sq.km):
    - Cumulative static impacts at 31/12/2023: 4,180 MSA.sq.km (land), 65 MSA.sq.km (aquatic).
    - Periodic (dynamic) change in 2023: +55 MSA.sq.km for land.
  - CNP Assurances (BIA-GBS™, end-2024) covers 99% of directly held equity and corporate bonds (100% relative to provider coverage). Footprint per € thousand invested (MSA.sq.m):
    - Aquatic: static 3.51; dynamic 0.05.
    - Land: static 48.65; dynamic 2.85.
  - LBP AM: at end-2023, 70% of assets (convertible, corporate and sovereign bonds, equities) covered by a biodiversity footprint of 58 MSA.PPB per € billion invested.

- Pollution management (material in financed activities, not in own operations)
  - Pollution recognized as one of five major biodiversity pressures (IPBES) and addressed within biodiversity policies.
  - Responsible Financing and Investment Charter excludes companies deriving >20% of revenue from pesticide manufacture/sales.
  - CNP Assurances’ 2021–2025 sustainable forest management charter: herbicides/fungicides prohibited; insecticides limited to health emergencies, with training and methodologies to support this.
  - Pollution factors included in ESG ratings for listed assets.
  - LBP AM actions: pesticides exclusion; engagement with pig farms and fertilizer producers on soil pollution/chemical use; engagement with salmon/shrimp farmers on aquaculture nutrient deposits; commitments on plastics circularity; GREaT rating model covers pollution.
  - Under CSRD and TNFD, La Banque Postale conducted deeper analyses with GBS to map dependencies on 21 ecosystem services and assess land and freshwater biodiversity impacts across IPBES pressures, including pollution.

- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document on sustainable performance and environmental information, focusing on biodiversity footprint measurement and pollution management.

- Action plans and assessments:

nodes.heading: 2.2.3.1 Pollution prevention and reduction policies
nodes.start_phrase: Pollution is one of the five major types of pressure on ecosystems and biodiversity identified by IPBES.

- Pollution is addressed within broader biodiversity preservation efforts and through the Responsible Financing and Investment Charter, including exclusions of companies deriving over 20% of revenue from pesticide manufacture or sales.

nodes.title: Action plans related to the prevention and reduction of pollution
nodes.heading: 2.2.3.2 Action plans related to the prevention and reduction of pollution
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the double materiality analysis carried out as part of the CSRD, as part of the TNFD, La Banque Postale SA has also conducted a more in-depth study of the impacts and dependencies related to biodiversity using the Global Biodiversity Score (GBS), a tool developed by CDC Biodiversité.
nodes.summary:
- Measurement of biodiversity footprint across investment and financing portfolios:
  - La Banque Postale: Assesses 39% of its financing portfolio using the Global Biodiversity Score (GBS) in MSA.sq.km; cumulative static impacts at 31/12/2023 are 4,180 MSA.sq.km (land) and 65 MSA.sq.km (aquatic); 2023 shows a +55 MSA.sq.km change for land.
  - CNP Assurances: Uses BIA-GBS™, covering 99% of directly held equities and corporate bonds (effectively 100% per data provider). Footprint per €1,000 invested—Aquatic: static 3.51 MSA.sq.m; dynamic 0.05 MSA.sq.m. Land: static 48.65 MSA.sq.m; dynamic 2.85 MSA.sq.m.
  - LBP AM: 70% of assets (convertible, corporate and sovereign bonds, equities) covered; footprint measured at 58 MSA.PPB per € billion invested.

- Pollution materiality and governance:
  - Pollution deemed non-material for own operations but material in financed activities; addressed via responsible financing and investment policies.
  - Exclusion of companies with >20% revenue from manufacturing/selling agricultural pesticides.
  - Forestry management charter (CNP Assurances) bans herbicides/fungicides and limits insecticides to health emergencies; training and methodologies to meet targets.
  - Pollution considerations integrated into ESG ratings and LBP AM’s GREaT rating model.

- Policies, action plans, and engagements to prevent/reduce pollution:
  - TNFD-aligned portfolio analysis using GBS to assess dependencies on ecosystem services and impacts across IPBES pressures (including pollution); findings published in the 2023 Climate and Nature Report and to inform a Nature Transition plan.
  - CNP Assurances applies ESG filters (Pollution/Waste) and a “Green Works” Charter for real estate to limit construction-phase pollution, select low-impact materials, reduce waste, and manage asbestos/lead.
  - LBP AM implements a pesticides exclusion policy and active engagements:
    - Agriculture: engage pig farming and fertilizer producers on soil pollution and chemical use; require plans to reduce pesticide use by 2030 (aligned with Kunming-Montreal Target 7 and EU Farm to Fork), phase out highly hazardous pesticides by 2030, disclose pesticide-free product shares, consumer communication, and transparent influence policies.
    - Aquaculture: engage salmon/shrimp farmers on sustainable practices and nutrient-related pollution.
    - Plastics/circularity: commitments sought from agri-food companies.
    - Water: require regular impact analyses, site- and substance-specific reduction targets, disclosure of indicators, remediation plans for incidents, and mapping/protection plans for activities near critical freshwater/sensitive aquatic ecosystems.
  - Louvre Banque Privée: improves management of SFDR PAI indicators and integrates pollution into issuer/asset manager engagement.

- Targets and next steps:
  - Following 2023–2024 impact/dependency/risk assessments, pollution impact-reduction targets will be progressively set, contingent on improved measurement accuracy, methodologies, and higher-quality data.

nodes.title: targets and results related to the prevention and reduction of pollution
nodes.heading: 2.2.3.3 targets and results related to the prevention and reduction of pollution
nodes.start_phrase: Following the exercise to measure impacts, dependencies, risks and opportunities conducted in 2023-2024, impact reduction targets will be gradually established.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: La Banque Postale Group’s CSR environmental measures on pollution prevention and water/marine resources, primarily across financed activities and real estate.
- ESG integration on pollution: CNP Assurances applies ESG filters to listed equities/bonds, including “Pollution/Waste” criteria (air/soil pollution, toxic emissions, e-waste, packaging).
- Real estate “Green Works” Charter: ecosystem protection during construction, low-impact materials, waste reduction, control of odours/VOCs, and compliance on asbestos/lead; measures to limit site-adjacent pollution.
- Soil pollution expectations (LBP AM): 
  - Pesticide use/production reduction plans by 2030 aligned with Kunming-Montreal Target 7 and EU Farm to Fork.
  - Phase-out of highly hazardous pesticides by 2030.
  - Reporting on pesticide-free production, clear consumer information, awareness actions.
  - Publication of an influence policy on plant protection products with transparent advocacy practices.
- Water pollution expectations (LBP AM for financed companies): 
  - Regular assessment of impacts on local surface/groundwater.
  - Action plans with site- and substance-specific discharge/pollution reduction targets, prioritizing high water-stress sites.
  - Publication of monitoring indicators.
  - Remediation/restoration/rewilding plans after incidents.
  - Mapping and protection plans for activities near critical freshwater/sensitive aquatic biodiversity ecosystems.
- Louvre Banque Privée: strengthens quantitative management of SFDR PAI indicators to identify high-impact entities and integrates pollution into engagement.
- Targets/results on pollution: Following 2023–2024 impact/dependency/risk/opportunity assessments, impact-reduction targets will be phased in as measurement accuracy, methodologies, and data quality improve.
- Water and marine resources policy (2024): Adoption of Caisse des Dépôts water policy addressing scarcity, water quality/infrastructure, flooding/soil sealing; aims to support:
  - 10% national water consumption reduction by 2030.
  - Preservation of 100% of drinking water catchments by 2027 (EU Water Framework Directive).
  - Three pillars: understand impacts/risks; adopt water-saving; preserve water quality/infrastructure. Implementation begins 2025 under GRMC oversight.
- Water-related commitments:
  - By end-2025: water footprint/dependency assessment.
  - By end-2027: initial estimate of aquatic pollution from operations and financed/invested entities; assessment of portfolio exposure to drought/water stress (France, overseas, and relevant international).
- Financing portfolio measures on water:
  - By end-2025: integrate water-saving target and local water-stress levels into ESG analysis.
  - In high-stress areas: require alignment with best-practice water consumption to avoid worsening scarcity.
  - Deploy financing tools for efficient water management; loans to sanitation services/water agencies to improve water quality.
  - Exclude financing/investment in companies with >20% revenue from pesticide manufacture/sales.
- Oceans: no dedicated policy yet; to be developed with Caisse des Dépôts in 2025 ahead of the UN Ocean Conference (UNOC) in Nice.

nodes.title: Preserving water and marine resources [E3]
nodes.heading: 2.2.4 Preserving water and marine resources [E3]
nodes.start_phrase: The “Water” topic is not included in the scope of La Banque Postale’s own operations.
nodes.summary:
- Context and scope: In La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR, Environmental information 2.2.4), water is addressed primarily through financed activities (downstream value chain), not the Bank’s own operations.
- Policy framework: In 2024, the Group adopted Caisse des Dépôts’ water policy, targeting three challenges—scarcity of water resources, water quality and related infrastructure, and flooding/soil sealing—aiming to support France’s 10% water-use reduction by 2030 and preserve 100% of drinking water catchments by 2027 in line with the EU Water Framework Directive.
- Governance and rollout: The Group Risk Management Committee oversees implementation; the policy is structured around commitments, targets, and indicators, with first actions starting in 2025.
- Pillar 1—Understand impacts and risks: Commitments include producing a water footprint/dependency assessment by end-2025; estimating aquatic pollution from operations and financed entities by end-2027; and assessing portfolio exposure to drought/water stress (France, overseas territories, and relevant international exposures) by end-2027.
- Pillar 2—Water saving (sobriety): Support stakeholders in reducing consumption and modernizing water/sanitation networks; deploy financing tools for efficient water management. For financing portfolios: integrate water-saving targets and local water stress into ESG analysis by end-2025; ensure projects in high-stress areas align with best sector practices to avoid worsening shortages; expand dedicated water-efficiency financing.
- Pillar 3—Preserve water quality and infrastructure: Reduce ecosystem impacts, prioritize nature-based solutions, and support rewilding/restoration. Targets include combating aquatic pollution, ensuring proper water cycle functioning, and protecting wetlands. Portfolio rules: exclude financing/investment in companies with over 20% of revenue from pesticide manufacture/sales; provide loans that improve water quality via public sanitation services or water agencies.
- Marine/oceans policy: No specific sustainable oceans and seas policy yet; development planned with Caisse des Dépôts in 2025, ahead of the UN Ocean Conference (UNOC) in Nice, June 2025.
