nodes.title: Employee skills policy
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.2 Employee skills policy
nodes.start_phrase: The policies presented in this paragraph aim to reinforce the positive impacts and opportunities of upskilling employees.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: CSR social information detailing La Banque Postale Group’s employee-related policies on quality of work life and working conditions (QWLWC), skills development, and remuneration, aimed at enhancing positive impacts (well‑being, upskilling) and mitigating risks (health, work conditions, pay deterioration).

- QWLWC policy:
  - Objectives: workload regulation; protection of physical and mental health; work–life balance; reducing information overload; fostering good work relationships across the employee lifecycle.
  - Approach: multidisciplinary primary risk prevention; data-driven analysis with indicators; broad stakeholder involvement; test-and-learn continuous improvement; monitoring of actions and progress.
  - Governance and compliance: aligned with French Labour Code and sectoral collective agreements; QWLWC agreement signed 11 Sept 2023 by three representative unions; provisions published on intranet; annual commission oversees implementation.
  - Group scope: CNP Assurances has a QWLWC agreement emphasizing engagement and well‑being, and sets international diversity and inclusion governance across subsidiaries.

- Employee skills policy:
  - Purpose: support the Group’s Strategic Plan through upskilling and continuous learning across the employee journey (onboarding, transformation support, new offerings).
  - Coverage: continuous, regulatory, and mandatory trainings (EU/national banking standards, GDPR, RGAA).
  - Process: skills development plan co-built by business lines and HR, validated and shared across the Group.
  - HR missions and principles: recruit and onboard, assess skills, manage careers, promote development and potential; four pillars—co‑constructed career management, cross-entity mobility within La Banque Postale/La Poste ecosystem, talent acquisition, and managerial development.

- Remuneration policy:
  - Governance: approved by Executive and Supervisory Boards; implemented by the HR Director.
  - Principles and targets: recognition of performance, fairness, transparency; fair pay based on expertise, tenure, experience with market benchmarking and internal equity; gender pay equality; recognition of long-term individual and collective performance; alignment of behaviors with long-term Group goals; support for internal mobility and career advancement to build long-term commitment.

nodes.title: Employee Remuneration policy
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.3 Employee Remuneration policy
nodes.start_phrase: Remuneration policies aim to prevent and mitigate the negative impacts of the Group regarding a potential deterioration in remuneration levels, the number of jobs or the type of contract for employees.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: The excerpt outlines La Banque Postale Group’s social policies aimed at enhancing quality of life at work, safeguarding health and safety, developing employee skills, ensuring fair remuneration, and promoting diversity and inclusion across the Group and its subsidiaries.

- Quality of Work Life and Working Conditions (QWLWC):
  - Implemented by HR for La Banque Postale’s Economic and Social Unit (UES); aligned with French Labour Code and sector agreements.
  - Objectives: global QWLWC approach covering work content (workload regulation), prevention and health (physical/mental), work relations and work-life balance, and tackling information overload.
  - Method: multidisciplinary primary risk prevention—indicator-based analysis, co-building with stakeholders, broad involvement, continuous improvement, action monitoring.
  - Focus on good work relationships throughout careers; onboarding as a cultural alignment lever.
  - 2023 QWLWC agreement signed with three representative unions; published on intranet; annual commission monitors implementation.
  - CNP Assurances has a parallel QWLWC agreement and international D&I governance.

- Employee Skills Policy:
  - Training policy supports the Strategic Plan via skills development plans for all Group employees.
  - Covers onboarding, support during transformations, continuous learning, and mandatory/regulatory training (e.g., banking standards, GDPR, RGAA).
  - Skills plan co-built with business lines and HR; validated and shared across departments.
  - HR core missions: recruitment/onboarding, skills assessment, career path management, professional development, potential development.
  - Four HR principles: co-constructed career management; cross-entity mobility (La Banque Postale, financial services, La Poste Network, La Poste Group); talent recruitment; managerial development.

- Remuneration Policy:
  - Approved by Executive and Supervisory Boards; implemented by HR; based on performance recognition, fairness, transparency.
  - Aims: fair pay reflecting expertise, tenure, market and internal equity; gender pay equality; recognition of long-term individual/collective performance; alignment with long-term goals; career development to foster commitment.
  - Published on intranet; compliant with labor law and collective agreements.
  - Subsidiaries tailor policies to local/sector regulations.
  - CNP Assurances’ policy aligns with strategic, financial and non-financial objectives, ensures fairness and gender equality; each subsidiary drafts its own policy with HR oversight.
  - Louvre Banque Privée has remuneration and professional equality agreements.

- Health and Safety:
  - 2024 prevention plan validated by the Health, Safety and Working Conditions Commission (HSWCC):
    - Continue/adapt occupational risk assessments specific to La Banque Postale.
    - Analyze lost-time accidents using the “5 Whys” method.
    - Implement workstation adjustments recommended by occupational health.
    - Raise awareness of road safety risks.
  - QWLWC collective agreement integrated into UES development strategy; complements prior agreements (diversity, remote work).
  - Subsidiary measures: CNP’s QWLWC agreement; Louvre Banque Privée safety booklet; Louvre Banque Privée Immobilier Conseil DUERP.
  - Strengthened prevention via multidisciplinary impact assessments for transformation projects; three national HSWC committees held in 2023 plus monitoring of the “Réussir Ensemble” agreement.

- Diversity and Inclusion (D&I):
  - Policy renewed every three years via social agreement; implemented by HR for all UES employees; shared internally and externally.
  - Five pillars: Disability (RQTH recruitment and recognition), Generations (youth entry, older worker retention, intergenerational diversity), Parity (gender equality and governance parity, anti-sexism), LGBT+ inclusion, Social/Ethnic origins (fairness across the employee lifecycle).
  - Built with experts, charities, HR, and employees.
  - Covers all legally defined discrimination grounds (26 to date), including sex, gender, age, and disability.

nodes.title: Health and safety policies
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.4 Health and safety policies
nodes.start_phrase: The policies presented below aim to prevent and mitigate negative impacts on working conditions that could harm the physical or mental health of employees.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information).
- Remuneration policy:
  - Published on the intranet, accessible to all employees, and strictly compliant with applicable regulations, labor law, collective bargaining, and company agreements.
  - Group-wide guiding principles applied by subsidiaries, adapted to local/sectoral rules.
  - CNP Assurances’ policy aims to attract, retain, motivate, and recognize employees, aligned with strategic, financial, and non-financial objectives; implemented by management/HR and deployed by managers; ensures fairness, gender equality, and adequate wages.
  - Louvre Banque Privée has its own remuneration policy and a professional equality agreement to prevent negative impacts on employees.
- Health and safety:
  - Policies aim to prevent/mitigate risks to physical and mental health and ensure employee safety.
  - 2024 prevention plan (HR/HSWCC) focuses on: continuing LBP-specific risk assessments; analyzing lost-time accidents with the “5 Whys”; workstation adjustments via occupational health; road safety awareness.
  - A Quality of Work Life and Working Conditions (QWLWC) agreement signed for La Banque Postale UES, integrating into corporate strategy and complementing prior agreements (diversity, equality, remote work). Other subsidiaries maintain their own QWLWC/safety frameworks (e.g., CNP’s QWLWC agreement, Louvre Banque Privée’s safety booklet, DUERP for Louvre Banque Privée Immobilier Conseil).
  - Strengthened workplace prevention processes via multidisciplinary assessments of transformation projects, proactive change-risk management, and prevention plans; three national HSWC committees held in 2023 alongside “Réussir Ensemble” agreement monitoring.
- Diversity and inclusion:
  - Policy redefined every three years via a social agreement, implemented by HR and applicable across La Banque Postale UES.
  - Built with experts, charities, HR, and employees; communicated internally and externally.
  - Five pillars: disability (hiring and recognition), generations (youth entry and senior retention), parity (gender equality and balanced governance), LGBT+ inclusion, and social/ethnic origins (fairness across the employee lifecycle).
  - Covers all legally recognized discrimination grounds (26), including sex, gender, age, and disability.

nodes.title: Diversity and inclusion policies and commitments
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.5 Diversity and inclusion policies and commitments
nodes.start_phrase: The policies presented in this paragraph respond to the positive and negative impacts and risks related to diversity and inclusion.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information), with references to CSR glossary and indicators.
- Remuneration policies: Group-wide, compliant with regulations, labor law, and collective agreements; published on the intranet and accessible to all employees. Subsidiaries set policies aligned with Group principles and local rules. CNP Assurances’ policy is tied to strategic goals and performance (financial and non-financial), implemented by management and HR, promoting fairness and gender equality. Louvre Banque Privée has a remuneration policy and a professional equality agreement.
- Health and safety (QWLWC) policies: Annual prevention plan validated by the HSWCC focusing on occupational risk assessment, “5 Whys” analysis of lost-time accidents, workstation adjustments, and road safety awareness. A QWLWC agreement was signed for La Banque Postale UES; other subsidiaries have their own instruments (CNP Assurances QWLWC agreement; Louvre Banque Privée safety booklet; Louvre Banque Privée Immobilier Conseil DUERP). Strengthened change management via multidisciplinary impact assessments and prevention plans; national HSWC committees held in 2023 alongside monitoring of the “Réussir Ensemble” agreement.
- Diversity and inclusion commitments: A triannual Diversity & Inclusion policy led by HR for La Banque Postale UES, covering all 26 legal discrimination grounds and built with experts, NGOs, and employees. Five pillars: disability, generations, gender parity, LGBT+, and social/ethnic origins; policy shared internally and externally.
- Disability policy: Under the sixth social agreement (27 March 2023), systematic recruitment of RQTH candidates on equal skills and incentives for RQTH declarations; applies across UES and banking functions, developed with AFMD and Entreprise pour la Cité. Two major, triannually renewed social agreements—Disability, and Diversity & Professional Equality—evidence long-term commitment.
- Subsidiary initiatives: CNP Assurances’ QWLWC agreement ensures equal treatment based on skills and performance; code of conduct on preventing discrimination/harassment; signatory of the Diversity Charter since 2006; Inclusion Committee (since 2021) to steer and monitor action plans and complaints mechanisms. Louvre Banque Privée has agreements on professional equality and quality of work life.
- Group-wide inclusion actions: Commitments include base agreements, a gender parity indicator for the mission-led company, partnerships with charities, and an Executive Committee–endorsed diversity strategy. Annual action plans cover gender parity (webinars, violence against women conference), pay streamlining with a new package, disability initiatives (Health & Disability Week, European Disability Employment Week, 10 disability officers, workstation adjustments, awareness web series), and broader diversity actions (webinars, managerial support for inclusion cases, mentoring, surveys on everyday sexism/LGBT+, sponsorship, executive advocacy). Over 30 events yearly and five D&I training courses (one mandatory) offered with La Poste Group.
- Reporting and whistleblowing: Established channels for victims or witnesses of discrimination, with processing and system governance referenced elsewhere in the document.
- Human rights policy: La Banque Postale Group aligns with La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy and the UN Global Compact, referencing the UDHR, UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration and core conventions, and OECD Guidelines, aiming to prevent and mitigate human rights risks, particularly within its own workforce.

nodes.title: Human rights policies and measures
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.6 Human rights policies and measures
nodes.start_phrase: The Group’s human rights policies aim to prevent and minimise the negative impacts and risks identified in this area.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on La Banque Postale Group’s Diversity, Inclusion, and Human Rights framework within the Sustainable performance/Social information section of the 2024 Universal Registration Document.
- Disability policy (sixth social agreement, 27 March 2023) mandates systematic recruitment of RQTH-recognized candidates (internal/external) with equal skills, encourages employee RQTH declarations, and applies across all banking functions; developed with experts, AFMD, Entreprise pour la Cité, and HR.
- Two cornerstone social agreements—Disability and Diversity & Professional Equality—renewed every three years, unanimously signed for the sixth consecutive time, underscoring ongoing commitment.
- CNP Assurances: QWL/working conditions agreement promoting equal treatment; code of conduct on anti-discrimination/harassment; signatory of the Diversity Charter since 2006; Inclusion Committee (since 2021) to steer, monitor, and ensure coherence of inclusion actions; complaints mechanisms for discrimination, harassment, and sexist behavior.
- Louvre Banque Privée: agreement on professional equality and quality of life at work.
- La Banque Postale SA commitments to vulnerable groups: two basic agreements (Diversity & Professional Equality; Disability), gender parity indicator for mission-led company, partnerships with charities, and Group-wide Diversity strategy endorsed by the Executive Committee.
- Annual inclusion action plan highlights: gender parity initiatives (webinars, violence against women conference); salary streamlining via a new remuneration package; disability inclusion (Health & Disability Week, European Disability Employment Week, disability officers, workstation adjustments, annual awareness web series); broader diversity actions (webinars, managerial support for inclusion cases, intergenerational/female mentoring, inclusion surveys on everyday sexism/LGBT+, focus groups, sponsorship, executive advocacy).
- Culture and training: 30+ events/year; five Diversity & Inclusion training courses with La Poste Group (one mandatory) available to all employees.
- Reporting and protection: established reporting and whistleblowing channels for discrimination, with referenced sections detailing processing and system independence/accessibility.
- Human rights policies: aligned with La Poste Group and international frameworks (UDHR, UNGPs, ILO core conventions, OECD Guidelines, UN Global Compact); commitments include preventing rights violations; prohibiting violence, forced/child labor and trafficking, and all discrimination; upholding freedom of association, collective bargaining, adequate remuneration, and privacy; compliance with local labor laws while seeking international-standard protection; contribution to SDGs; explicit stance against trafficking/forced and child labor.
- Human rights remediation: primarily France-based operations imply lower exposure to severe risks, but due diligence addresses discrimination/harassment; whistleblowing processing and a system for handling distressing workplace situations are in place (with referenced procedures).
- Social Dialogue policy: HR leads constructive relations with employee representatives, organizes union rights, elections, and representative bodies per regulations to ensure employees’ voice in company policy, with further details in the dedicated section.

nodes.title: Social Dialogue policy
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.2.7 Social Dialogue policy
nodes.start_phrase: In terms of collective relations, the Human Resources Department is responsible for social dialogue, which it develops and builds with employee representatives.
nodes.summary:
- The document outlines La Banque Postale Group’s human rights commitments: preventing violations; prohibiting violence, inhuman/degrading treatment, forced and child labor, and human trafficking; banning discrimination (e.g., gender, age, health/disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, nationality, social background, community, political/union/religious beliefs); defending freedom of association and collective bargaining; ensuring adequate remuneration; and protecting privacy.
- It commits to compliance with labor laws in operating countries while aiming to meet international human rights standards, aligns with international frameworks and the UN SDGs, and references La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy for issues like trafficking and forced/child labor.
- Human rights risk management and remediation: low overall exposure due to French footprint, but vigilance on discrimination and harassment; use of a whistleblowing system and a dedicated process for distressing situations at work; remediation and governance processes are referenced to specific sections.
- Social Dialogue policy: the HR Department leads relations with employee representatives, organizes union rights, elections, and representation bodies to ensure employees’ voice in company policy.
- Dialogue with employees and their representatives: HR Director is accountable; daily communication via managers and HR; employee experience policy; whistleblowing channels as means of expression; a multi-year listening framework anchored by an annual engagement survey on strategy, customers, well-being, teamwork, and management, with departmental action follow-up.
- 2024 listening initiatives: hybrid work survey (2,207 respondents; 59% participation) and targeted surveys (e.g., CLDB transformation); listening workshops on transformation and employee experience; monitoring of Glassdoor feedback; focus groups on Diversity pillars to inform and adjust inclusion policies; feedback also gathered through the Social and Economic Committee (SEC).
- Governance and indicators for social dialogue in 2024: 15 SEC meetings (11 ordinary, 4 extraordinary), 15 SEC commission meetings, 10 Health, Safety and Working Conditions Committee meetings; an SEC Sustainability Commission meeting twice yearly; and five employee representatives on the Group’s Supervisory Board.

nodes.title: Dialogue process with employees and their representatives
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.3 Dialogue process with employees and their representatives
nodes.start_phrase: The Human Resources Director is responsible for the human resources policies implemented by the Human Resources Department.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) detailing employee dialogue, representation, surveys, and reporting/remediation mechanisms, including CNP Assurances.

- Governance and responsibility:
  - Human Resources Department leads HR policy and ensures effective dialogue with employees and their representatives.
  - Strong emphasis on stakeholder representation in governance to reinforce the social dimension of ESG.

- Direct employee dialogue and listening:
  - Multi‑year listening framework with an annual Group‑wide engagement survey (~50 questions on strategy, customers, well‑being, teamwork, management); departments act on results.
  - 2024 special surveys: hybrid work (2,207 respondents; 59% participation) and CLDB transformation follow‑up.
  - Listening workshops on transformation and employee experience; monitoring of Glassdoor ratings.
  - Diversity focus groups collect feedback to inform and adjust inclusion policies.

- Employee representation and social dialogue structures:
  - Five employee representatives sit on La Banque Postale’s Supervisory Board.
  - Group Committee (parent and subsidiaries with SECs) meets regularly on strategic topics and consolidated financials.
  - For La Banque Postale UES:
    - Operates under several agreements (employee representation, social dialogue/right to organize, career paths/skills for office holders), aligned with French Labour Code and sectoral banking agreements; all published on intranet.
    - The Social and Economic Committee (SEC) ensures collective expression and is informed/consulted on workforce changes, structural changes, employment and working conditions (incl. hours, training), new technologies, H&S/working conditions, and environmental impacts.
    - 2024 activity: 15 SEC meetings (11 ordinary, 4 extraordinary), 15 SEC commission meetings (diversity/equality, employment, training, sustainability), 10 HSWCC meetings; monthly meetings with union reps; work on remote tools for exercising the right to organize.
    - Strategic guidelines consultation every three years with annual intermediate updates; early re‑consultation if strategy changes; local/regional representation maintained via alternate SEC members.
    - Discussion workshops with SEC/HSWCC support collaborative, calm transformation.
    - Sustainability Commission established by the SEC, meeting twice yearly; includes four Mission Committee representatives and four SEC representatives.

- CNP Assurances:
  - Two agreements enabling “constructive and effective” social dialogue and governing the SEC.
  - QWLWC survey on engagement and well‑being.
  - “Parlons ambition” dialogue between employees and the Executive Committee.
  - 2024 agreements signed on diversity and professional equality.

- Reporting and remediation of distressing situations at work:
  - Confidential, impartial process respecting presumption of innocence; multiple reporting channels (manager, HR, occupational health, employee reps, harassment officers, social worker, ethics officer/whistleblowing platform).
  - Coverage includes moral/sexual harassment, sexist behavior, broader distress/burnout.
  - Employee awareness via intranet, Internal Rules, and code of conduct; training/communication reinforced; Confirmodoc tool verifies distribution of the code to employees and relevant third parties.
  - Processing:
    - Reports logged; listening phase within 15 days assesses need for occupational health referral and temporary protective measures.
    - If needed, investigation phase led by a joint steering committee (two HR reps, SEC secretary, HSWCC rapporteur); interviews clarify facts and remedies.
    - Outcomes may include support (medical/psychological), disciplinary actions up to dismissal for gross misconduct, and organizational/process changes; HR monitors effectiveness.

nodes.title: Reporting and remediation process
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.4 Reporting and remediation process
nodes.start_phrase: For La Banque Postale UES, the procedure set up by the system for dealing with distressing situations at work is conducted in compliance with the principle of the presumption of innocence, with complete impartiality and with the discretion necessary to protect each person's dignity and privacy.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on social dialogue and employee engagement at CNP Assurances, including two agreements (constructive/effective dialogue and SEC), a QWLWC survey on engagement and well-being, and the “Let’s talk ambition” forum with the Executive Committee.
- 2024 social agreements advancing respect for human rights, notably on diversity and professional equality.
- Comprehensive processes at La Banque Postale UES for reporting and remediating distressing situations at work, grounded in presumption of innocence, impartiality, and confidentiality; covers moral/sexual harassment, sexist behavior, and broader well-being concerns.
- Multiple reporting channels (managers, HR, occupational health, employee reps, harassment officers, ethics officer/whistleblowing, social assistance), with employee awareness via intranet, code of conduct, training, and the 2024 Confirmodoc tool ensuring code of conduct distribution.
- Structured case handling: swift HR intake and registry, a 15-day listening phase, precautionary protections, conditional investigation with a joint steering committee (HR reps, SEC secretary, HSWC rapporteur), and outcomes ranging from support (medical/psychological) to disciplinary actions up to dismissal and organizational/process adjustments with effectiveness monitoring.
- Governance and oversight: Employee Relations Department interfaces with employee bodies and coordinates channels; HR monitors deployment and case management. Group whistleblowing platform accessible to all employees, with whistleblower protection, Compliance/Ethics oversight, and anonymized annual reporting to the Supervisory Board.
- Subsidiary mechanisms at CNP Assurances: Integrity Line whistleblowing (managed by Ethics), Internal Social Mediation (encrypted), and access via managers/HR; systems available across subsidiaries.
- Employee action plans and resources to prevent negative impacts on health and well-being: HR legal support and Life at Work division with health services; 2024 initiatives on traffic accident prevention, visual/hearing fatigue, sedentary lifestyle, workstation adjustments, and guidance on tool use and information overload.
- Hybrid/home-working framework: renewed three-year home-working agreement (2024), manager support planned for 2025, right-to-disconnect awareness, annual leave reminders, and planned 2025 measures for employee carers and a mental health prevention program.
- QWLWC agreement (signed September 2023 for three years) guiding action plan rollout over 2023–2026.

nodes.title: Actions implemented and resources allocated
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.5.1 Actions implemented and resources allocated
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group implements various actions to prevent or mitigate its potential negative impacts on its employees.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and governance: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) detailing HR governance, with the Employee Relations Department and HR overseeing employee dialogue and handling distressing work situations; Compliance/Ethics teams monitor whistleblowing; Supervisory Board and its committees review social and remuneration indicators.

- Whistleblowing and protections: Multiple reporting channels across La Banque Postale and CNP Assurances (Integrity Line platform, internal social mediation, HR/line managers, La Poste Group platform), anonymous options, employee communications via code of conduct, and explicit whistleblower protection; annual anonymized reporting to the Supervisory Board.

- Preventing negative impacts on employees:
  - Working conditions and health: Measures addressing stress, burnout, MSDs, traffic accidents, visual/hearing fatigue, sedentary risks; workstation adjustments; guidance on digital tool use and preventing information overload; renewed three‑year home‑working agreement (2024) with right‑to‑disconnect awareness and annual leave reminders; hybrid work and meeting practices to be manager‑supported in 2025; negotiations for caregiver measures and a mental health prevention program slated for 2025.
  - Resources: Dedicated prevention/health/safety budget, 2024 hybrid work survey, budget for workstation adjustments, €250 equipment loan every five years for home working. CNP offers LYFE (health services, counseling, remote consults) and Ulteam (stress/concentration education) platforms.
  - Remuneration and purchasing power: Annual market benchmarks, manager training on fair treatment, guaranteed salary increase after maternity/adoption leave, annual gender equality index monitoring (all entities ≥92/100 in 2024), €600k/year budget since 2022 to close unexplained wage gaps; local social dialogue at CNP in countries without centrally governed increases to safeguard purchasing power.
  - Anti‑discrimination and harassment: Disability and Diversity/Professional Equality agreements with targets and action plans (role models, ERGs, working groups, awareness activities); executive sponsorship, dedicated D&I team, partnerships and charters (Diversity & Equal Opportunities, L’Autre Cercle for LGBT+, STOPE against sexism); clear alert, prevention, and sanction policy; participation in PAQTE with targets to host 200 youths (2022–2025).

- Promoting positive impacts:
  - Inclusion, development, and fair conditions: Internal training via École de la Banque et du Réseau for business and personal development; La Poste Group data and AI training pathways; gender equality initiatives (mentoring, representation targets, corrective hiring where imbalanced); social fund to support employees facing severe medical or accident‑related hardship.

- HR risk mitigation: Regular medical visit tracking with occupational health partners; occupational health policy with SIAMT (Île‑de‑France); cultural transformation program; comprehensive QWLWC initiative covering work content/organization, health and prevention, work‑life balance, information overload, and a structured, indicator‑driven, multi‑stakeholder prevention approach with continuous improvement.

- Monitoring and decision‑making: Effectiveness tracked via engagement survey, ad‑hoc surveys (e.g., hybrid work 2024), remuneration indicators, social protection scheme reviews, OHS indicators, disability agreement metrics, incidents from whistleblowing, and medical visit completion; HR Management Committee proposes measures, approved by Executive Committee and aligned with strategic/financial planning.

- Business practices and data: Sales practices unlikely to amplify social risks due to regulation; purchasing specifications integrate employee health and safety criteria; strong safeguards for employee data privacy.

- Contribution to SDGs: Primary impacts on SDG3 (Good health and well‑being), SDG8 (Decent work), and SDG10 (Reduced inequalities), with additional links to SDG13 (Climate action) via employee volunteering; SDG‑aligned employee savings fund; leave donation mechanisms (Mathys law) and encouragement to donate time savings; annual public SDG contribution report.

nodes.title: Monitoring the effectiveness of actions
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.5.2 Monitoring the effectiveness of actions
nodes.start_phrase: To assess the effectiveness of the actions implemented, La Banque Postale Group relies on several categories of indicators:
nodes.summary:
- Focus on sustainable performance and social information within La Banque Postale Group, emphasizing HR development, skills building, and innovation.
- Employee development at CNP Assurances through diverse career paths, professional and certifying trainings, and cross‑functional skills (autonomy, innovation, agility), with initiatives on ecology, AI, and quality of life at work, plus individual support (mobility, coaching, mentoring).
- Group-wide Data and AI upskilling via La Poste’s programs (e.g., Data Academy, Objectif AI) to build competencies and foster data/AI-driven projects.
- Robust monitoring of HR actions using multiple indicators: annual engagement/QWL survey, ad‑hoc internal surveys (e.g., hybrid work), remuneration tracking, annual review of social protection schemes, OHS/HSWCC reporting, disability agreement indicators, whistleblowing on discrimination/harassment/sexist behavior, and medical visit compliance.
- Governance and oversight by the Supervisory Board through its Appointments & Governance and Remunerations Committees; annual review of key social indicators including gender parity.
- Decision-making on preventing/mitigating negative workforce impacts led by HR Management Committee and approved by the Executive Committee within strategic and annual target setting.
- Risk management: sales practices pose low amplification of negative impacts due to regulation; purchasing practices incorporate health and safety criteria; strong attention to employee data privacy and responsible data use.
- Contribution to SDGs: primary impacts on SDG3 (Good health and well‑being), SDG8 (Decent work), SDG10 (Reduced inequalities), with additional actions supporting SDG13 (Climate action) via the “Tous Engagés” volunteer program.
- Employee savings options aligned with the UN SDGs and leave‑donation schemes (per Mathys law and its extension) to support carers and families, reinforcing SDG3.
- Annual public reporting of SDG contributions and related indicators.

nodes.title: Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.5.3 Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
nodes.start_phrase: Through its actions, La Banque Postale Group also has positive impacts on other Sustainable Development Goals.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on employee development and innovation:
  - Multiple career paths and professional training to build business expertise and versatile, cross-functional skills (autonomy, innovation, agility).
  - Strategic upskilling on ecology, artificial intelligence, quality of work life, with individual support (mobility, coaching, mentoring).
  - Group-wide Data and AI training programs (e.g., Data Academy, Objectif AI) to foster AI/data capabilities and innovative projects.

- Monitoring effectiveness and governance:
  - Use of diverse indicators: annual engagement survey (QWL), ad-hoc surveys (e.g., hybrid work), remuneration monitoring, social protection scheme reviews, OHS indicators, disability agreement metrics, whistleblowing reports on discrimination/harassment/sexist behavior, and completion of medical visits.
  - Supervisory Board oversight via Appointments & Governance and Remunerations Committees; annual review of social indicators (e.g., gender parity).
  - HR decisions on managing negative impacts approved by the Executive Committee; financial arbitration aligned with fiscal years.
  - Attention to employee health and safety in purchasing specifications; strong employee data privacy practices.

- Contribution to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
  - Core impacts on SDG3 (Good health and well-being), SDG8 (Decent work), and SDG10 (Reduced inequalities).
  - “Tous Engagés” volunteering program supporting SDG13 (Climate action) and SDG10.
  - Employee savings offering SDG-aligned investment funds.
  - Leave donation scheme for carers under Mathys law (SDG3) and encouragement to donate time-savings days.
  - Annual public booklet detailing SDG contributions and indicators.

- Environmental transition and employees:
  - No significant negative impact from the green transition on banking/insurance roles.
  - Extensive “Just Transition Programme” training:
    - Basic track: climate risk regulation, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresco, eco-behavior modules (climate, responsible digital, sustainable consumption), and responsible finance.
    - Specialized tracks by business line: integrating just transition into practices (commercial tools, ESG financing analysis, responsible communication, supplier relations/responsible purchasing, biodiversity in finance).
  - ESG targets embedded in remuneration to reinforce engagement.

- Target setting and review process:
  - Targets derived from policies, ambitions, legal obligations; negotiated with employee representatives where applicable.
  - HR roadmap governed by quarterly committee meetings and annual reviews; agreement-based targets monitored by dedicated commissions.
  - Targets and roadmap communicated to all employees via intranet.
  - Subsidiaries set aligned targets; CNP Assurances includes HR targets within corporate agreements and purpose.

- Current targets:
  - Promote favorable working conditions (working hours, social dialogue, fair pay, social protection, collective agreements).
  - Quality of Work Life (QWL) measured via annual engagement survey across the UES; resources and communications (e.g., leave, right to disconnect) available on intranet.
  - QWL target set at a score greater than 7 for La Banque Postale SA and La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring (UES).

nodes.title: Impact of the environmental transition on employees
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.5.4 Impact of the environmental transition on employees
nodes.start_phrase: As La Banque Postale Group operates in the banking and insurance sector, the activities of its employees are not impacted by a significant negative impact due to the transition to a greener and climate neutral economy.
nodes.summary:
- Assesses the impact of the environmental transition on employees, noting no significant negative effects for a banking/insurance workforce but emphasizing proactive support and awareness-raising.
- Details the “Just Transition Programme” training delivered via the École de la Banque et du Réseau:
  - Basic course for all employees (since 2022): mandatory climate risk training, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresco workshops, and learning cycles on eco-friendly behaviors (climate, responsible digital, sustainable consumption) and responsible finance.
  - Specialized courses by business line: practical integration of just transition into roles, including commercial tools and speaking, ESG analysis of financing, responsible communication, supplier relations and responsible purchasing, and biodiversity in finance.
- Embeds ESG competencies long term and links ESG objectives to all employees’ remuneration, monitored through a mission-led company indicator to boost awareness and engagement.
- Explains the employee target-setting process:
  - Targets aligned with group policies, ambitions, and legal requirements; negotiated with employee representatives under an Executive Committee framework by HR.
  - HR roadmap governed by the HR Management Committee with quarterly monitoring and annual reviews; agreement-based targets tracked by monitoring commissions.
  - Targets and roadmap shared on the intranet; results analyzed annually and adjusted as needed; subsidiaries (including CNP Assurances) align their own HR targets.
- Presents specific employee targets on working conditions and quality of life at work (QWL):
  - QWL measured via the annual engagement survey covering La Banque Postale UES employees; resources and policies (e.g., leave, right to disconnect) communicated on the intranet.
  - QWL score target set at greater than 7, covering employees of La Banque Postale SA and La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring.

nodes.title: Target setting process
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.6.1 Target setting process
nodes.start_phrase: Targets are set in light of La Banque Postale Group’s policies and ambitions, and its legal obligations.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) covering the environmental transition’s impact on employees and employee-related targets.
- Impact of environmental transition on employees:
  - Due to the banking/insurance nature of activities, no significant negative impact expected on employees from the green transition.
  - Proactive support through awareness and training to integrate ESG into daily work.
- Employee training and upskilling (Just Transition Programme via École de la Banque et du Réseau):
  - Basic course for all employees (since 2022): mandatory climate risk training, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresk workshops, learning cycles on eco-friendly behaviors (climate, responsible digital use, sustainable consumption) and responsible finance (concepts and behind the scenes).
  - Specialized business-line courses: integrating just transition into professional practices; adapting offers/processes; commercial tools and communication; ESG analysis of financing; responsible communication; supplier relations and responsible purchasing; biodiversity in finance.
  - Objective: embed ESG skills long-term and strengthen employee commitment.
- ESG integration in remuneration:
  - All employees have ESG targets included in pay, aligned with corporate sustainability objectives; progress tracked via mission-led company indicator 1.2.
- Target-setting governance and process:
  - Targets derived from Group policies, ambitions, and legal obligations.
  - When tied to employee representative agreements, targets are negotiated (framework set by Executive Committee; HR and representatives conduct negotiations) and approved for the agreement term.
  - HR Department roadmap managed by the HR Management Committee with quarterly meetings and an annual review; monitoring commissions oversee agreement-related targets.
  - Results analyzed annually; targets validated/adjusted for Y+1; information shared with all employees via intranet.
  - Subsidiaries set aligned targets; CNP Assurances has HR targets within its agreements and purpose.
- Employee targets and indicators:
  - Focus on favorable working conditions (working hours, social dialogue, fair pay, social protection, collective agreements).
  - Quality of Life at Work (QWL) measured via annual engagement survey; resources and policies accessible on the intranet; communications on leave and right to disconnect.
  - Target: QWL indicator score above 7, covering La Banque Postale SA and La Banque Postale Leasing & Factoring (LBP UES).

nodes.title: Targets set
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.6.2 Targets set
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has set targets with regard to the identified impacts, risks and opportunities.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and context: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) detailing how the Group manages employee-related impacts, targets, and indicators, including governance of target-setting and reporting scope.

- Environmental transition and employees:
  - Minimal direct negative impact on banking/insurance roles.
  - Extensive ESG awareness and capability-building via the Just Transition Programme:
    - Basic course (mandatory climate risk training, sustainability e-learning, Climate Fresk, learning cycles on eco-behaviors and responsible finance).
    - Specialized, business-line courses (adapting practices/offers, ESG analysis of financing, responsible communication, supplier relations, responsible purchasing, biodiversity in finance).
  - ESG targets integrated into all employees’ remuneration; monitored as a mission-led company indicator.

- Target-setting governance:
  - Targets aligned with Group policies, ambitions, legal obligations; negotiated with employee representatives where applicable.
  - HR Department roadmap overseen by the HR Management Committee (quarterly reviews, annual validation/adjustment).
  - Agreement-based targets monitored by dedicated commissions; roadmap shared on intranet.
  - Subsidiaries align targets with their remuneration policy/strategy; CNP Assurances also sets HR targets.

- Key targets, actions, and performance:
  - Working conditions and quality of life at work (QWL):
    - Target: QWL indicator >7; 2024 score 7.2/10 (up 0.1).
    - Broad internal communication of survey results and provisions (right to disconnect, leave, etc.).
  - Health and psychosocial risk (PSR) prevention:
    - Target: 100% of managers trained on PSR; achieved 85% as of 31/12/2024 (ongoing due to managerial turnover).
    - Occupational H&S plan on intranet; coordinated HR/manager actions to prevent absenteeism.
  - Inclusion, equal opportunity, and skills:
    - Disability employment: aim to meet/exceed 6% statutory rate; quarterly/biannual monitoring and regular awareness actions.
    - Training: target 100% completion of regulatory training; monthly tracking and reminders; monitoring of training hours/days and six‑year legal review; quarterly oversight of the Skills Development Plan; Supervisory Board monitors training as a risk metric.
    - Gender diversity: mission target >43% women among strategic managers and senior executives; 40.5% at 31/12/2024.
    - Harassment: zero-tolerance stance with an action-focused approach; cases monitored quarterly; no numeric reduction target to avoid under-reporting.
  - HR risk focus (2024): health and harassment.
    - Medical visit compliance: target full compliance for all employees/types of visits; regional outsourcing to PrestaMed launched to strengthen scheduling/monitoring; ongoing communications and intranet info.
  - Remuneration and purchasing power:
    - Objective of 100% adequate wages; most employees covered by favorable collective agreements; annual wage negotiations.
    - No numeric targets for gender/executive pay gaps; aim for objective, role-based pay fairness.
  - Social dialogue and work-life balance:
    - Robust representative bodies and annual monitoring commissions; quality of dialogue assessed via surveys/relations rather than a numeric target.
    - Professional elections held Nov 2023; next in 2027.
    - New home‑working agreement signed 14 Nov 2024; work‑life balance tracked via QWL and hybrid work surveys.
    - Comprehensive social protection; social fund to cover low-coverage benefits; justified exemptions to healthcare plan.

- Opportunities:
  - Skills development fosters innovation; no separate target beyond existing training/skills objectives.

- Workforce indicators and reporting scope:
  - Coverage: La Banque Postale SA and all financially consolidated subsidiaries; includes permanent, fixed-term, and other contracts (apprentices, professionalization; excludes interns).
  - CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (created 31/12/2024) included for specific indicators (employee characteristics except departures/turnover, collective bargaining coverage, age breakdown, adequate wages, disability, H&S policy).
  - Unless stated otherwise, indicators calculated as of 31 December 2024.

nodes.title: Indicators relating to the Group’s workforce
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7 Indicators relating to the Group’s workforce
nodes.start_phrase: The workforce included in the calculation of the indicators presented in this section covers La Banque Postale Group (La Banque Postale SA and its subsidiaries).
nodes.summary:
- Focus on social policies and workforce data from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, Sustainable performance – Social information section.
- Workplace conduct: Zero tolerance on harassment pursued via an action-based target (not numerical), expected achieved in 2024.
- Remuneration and purchasing power: 100% of employees receive adequate wages; most are covered by collective agreements favorable to the statutory minimum. Annual negotiations address wage measures. No formal targets on gender/executive pay gaps, but measures aim to ensure any gaps reflect objective factors (responsibility, skills, tenure, performance).
- Working conditions and social dialogue: Commitment to high-quality social dialogue without quantified targets; assessed via surveys and ongoing relations with employee representatives. Annual monitoring commissions track the implementation and effectiveness of collective agreements. Employee representative elections held Nov 2023 (4-year term; next in 2027). Internal bodies (e.g., SEC, HSWCC, DSN) ensure employee voices are heard.
- Work-life balance and flexibility: New home-working agreement signed on 14 Nov 2024. Well-being monitored through survey-based indicators, including a QWL index and ad hoc surveys (e.g., on hybrid work in 2024).
- Social protection and benefits: All employees covered for illness, unemployment, work accidents, parental leave, and retirement via public schemes or company offerings. A social fund supplements low/no coverage areas; any healthcare plan opt-outs must be justified by alternative coverage.
- Skills and innovation: No separate “opportunity” target; training and skills development are addressed through existing actions and targets referenced elsewhere.
- Indicator scope and methodology: Workforce indicators cover La Banque Postale SA and all consolidated subsidiaries; include permanent, fixed-term, and other contracts (apprenticeships, professional training; interns excluded). Unless stated, data as of 31 Dec 2024.
- New subsidiary inclusion: CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (formed 31 Dec 2024 from La Mutuelle Générale and CNP Assurances teams) included in several indicators (S1-6 except departures/turnover, S1-8, S1-9, S1-10, S1-12, S1-14). Note on methodological differences between sustainability report and financial statements.
- Workforce profile (31 Dec 2024): 14,512 employees; 55% women; 94% on permanent contracts; 94% full-time. Increase vs. 2023 mainly due to integrating La Mutuelle Générale into CNP Assurances Protection Sociale.
- Organizational changes: Wind-down of Ma French Bank had limited workforce impact due to redeployment offers. Work-study positions at La Banque Postale SA rose by 37% in 2024 to boost employer brand attractiveness.
- Geographic footprint: Operations largely in France; La Financière de l’Échiquier has 6% of staff outside France; CNP Assurances has 27% outside France. Brazil represents over 10% of total Group headcount. Country totals cited: France 12,204; Brazil 1,530.
- Data notes: Gender reporting reflects legal recognition in France and Brazil (Men/Women). Multiple S1-tagged indicators referenced for CSR reporting consistency.

Notes the inclusion of the new subsidiary CNP Assurances Protection Sociale (formed from La Mutuelle Générale and CNP Assurances teams on 31 Dec 2024) in specific disclosures: S1‑6 (all employee characteristics except departures S1_6_11 and turnover S1_6_12), S1‑8 (collective bargaining and social dialogue), S1‑9 (age breakdown), S1‑10 (adequate wages), S1‑12 (employees with disabilities), and S1‑14 (health and safety policy coverage). Unless stated otherwise, all indicators are measured as of 31 December 2024. References: S1_SBM_3_01 and S1_SBM_3_02.

nodes.title: Characteristics of salaried workers
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.1 Characteristics of salaried workers
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group has 14,512 employees, the majority of whom are women (55%), permanent contracts (94%) and full-time employees (94%).
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) covering workforce characteristics, social dialogue, and diversity.
- Workforce profile (31 Dec 2024): 14,512 employees; 55% women; 94% on permanent contracts; 94% full-time. Work-study students at LBP SA up 37% in 2024 due to employer brand efforts.
- Organizational changes: Headcount growth mainly from integrating La Mutuelle Générale into CNP Assurances (forming CNP Assurances Protection Sociale). Wind-down of Ma French Bank had minimal impact thanks to redeployment offers.
- Geography: Operations largely in France; exceptions are La Financière de l’Échiquier (6% of its staff outside France) and CNP Assurances (27% of its staff outside France). Brazil accounts for over 10% of Group headcount. Main country totals: France 12,204 (6,781 women; 5,423 men); Brazil 1,530 (787 women; 743 men).
- Contracts and working time: Breakdown includes permanent, fixed-term, and work-study contracts; no contracts with non-guaranteed hours. Work-study students counted as full-time for reporting.
- Turnover: 9.4% staff rotation (considered moderate). 1,173 permanent employees left; includes movements to La Poste Group and Caisse des Dépôts (72 from LBP SA).
- Data and methodology: Workforce reported as active natural persons at year-end; breakdowns by gender, contract, working time, age, and socio-professional category. Departures counted for permanent contracts (voluntary, dismissal, retirement, death). Data collected by subsidiaries and consolidated with consistency checks. Note on differing scopes: CNP Assurances Protection Sociale included in the sustainability report but not yet in the financial statements.
- Regional working time split: France 11,375 full-time/829 part-time; Europe 641/29; Rest of world 1,621/17.
- Social dialogue: Near-universal coverage by collective agreements in France; some entities also have company-level agreements. For CNP employees outside France, 92% covered by collective agreements. All France-based employees have workplace representation. European Works Council applicability began after the 2023 merger with CNP; HR is adapting representative bodies accordingly. Reported coverage indicators show very high collective bargaining and representation levels in France and strong coverage in Latin America.
- Diversity and leadership: Commitment to balanced gender representation among senior executives; senior management split is 54.5% men (24) and 45.5% women (20). Definition of “general management” provided (top strategic roles).
- Age diversity: Balanced demographic structure with a strong 30–50 cohort, ongoing hiring of under-30 talent, and retention of over-50 expertise.

nodes.title: Social dialogue
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.2 Social dialogue
nodes.start_phrase: All La Banque Postale Group employees based in France are covered by a collective agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document covering social dialogue, diversity, and workforce demographics.
- Social dialogue and collective bargaining:
  - All La Banque Postale Group employees in France are covered by collective agreements; subsidiaries apply sectoral mandatory or voluntary agreements, with some company-level accords.
  - 92% of CNP Assurances employees outside France are covered by collective agreements.
  - All employees in France are represented by employee representatives.
  - Following the 11 April 2023 merger with CNP Assurances, European Works Council provisions now apply; HR is adapting representative bodies to integrate transnational social dialogue.
  - Reported coverage rates: 98.77% of employees covered by collective agreements overall; in France, collective agreement coverage is 100% and workplace representation 99.97%; Latin America shows high coverage (98.89%).
- Diversity in general management:
  - Strong emphasis on ensuring women’s representation in senior executive appointments with equal skills.
  - Definition of “general management” includes roles shaping Group strategy, first/second in command to Executive Committee members, MDs of major subsidiaries, and positions of highest strategic complexity/impact.
  - Senior executives by gender: 54.5% men (24) and 45.5% women (20).
- Workforce age structure:
  - Balanced demographics with a strong 30–50 cohort central to operations and strategy.
  - Notable presence of under-30 employees reflecting talent attraction efforts.
  - Significant over-50 population demonstrating retention of experience and expertise.

nodes.title: Diversity
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.3 Diversity
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group is particularly attentive to ensuring that women are properly represented when appointing senior executives, with equal skills.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Sustainable performance – Social information (sections 2.3.1.7.2 to 2.3.1.7.6) for La Banque Postale Group in the 2024 Universal Registration Document.

- Social dialogue and collective bargaining:
  - All employees in France are covered by collective agreements and have employee representatives.
  - Overall, 98.77% of employees are covered by collective agreements.
  - For CNP Assurances employees outside France, 92% are covered by collective agreements.
  - Following the 11 April 2023 merger with CNP Assurances, European Works Council provisions now apply; HR is adapting representative bodies accordingly.
  - Coverage for collective bargaining and workplace representation is near-universal in France and high in Latin America.

- Diversity in senior management:
  - The Group prioritizes balanced gender representation in senior executive appointments based on equal skills.
  - Definition of “general management” includes roles shaping Group strategy and leading major entities or strategic functions.
  - Senior executives by gender: 54.5% men (24), 45.5% women (20).

- Workforce demographics:
  - Emphasis on generational balance.
  - Employees by age: under 30: 1,915; 30–50: 8,346; over 50: 4,251.

- Adequate wages and social protection:
  - All employees receive an adequate wage (at least the legal minimum per country and/or applicable agreements).
  - 100% coverage for social protection: illness, unemployment, work-related accidents/disability, parental leave, and retirement, via public schemes or company benefits.

- Disability inclusion:
  - Active integration and support for employees with disabilities; rate remains below statutory target.
  - Measures include workstation adaptations, adjusted working hours, and commuting support.
  - Methodology: RQTH used in France; local legal definitions elsewhere.
  - Employees with disabilities: women 5.55%, men 3.29%, overall 4.53%.

- Training and careers:
  - Annual appraisals are central to performance recognition and career development; legally required in France, with international completion rates varying.
  - Strong communication on appraisal importance.
  - Continuous training supports upskilling and adaptation; figures exclude academic training for work‑study students.

nodes.title: Adequate wages and social protection
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.4 Adequate wages and social protection
nodes.start_phrase: All employees receive an adequate wage(1), in accordance with the standards in force, whether applicable legislation, collective bargaining agreements or applicable Company agreements.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information, sections 2.3.1.7.4 to 2.3.1.7.6) outlining wage adequacy, social protection, disability inclusion, and training/career management, with select workforce metrics.
- Adequate wages and social protection: All employees receive at least an “adequate wage” (defined as the legal minimum in each country) in line with laws, collective bargaining, and company agreements. The Group provides universal social protection coverage: 100% for illness, unemployment, work-related accidents/disability, parental leave, and retirement.
- Disability inclusion: The Group prioritizes recruitment, integration, and retention of employees with disabilities, offering individual accommodations (e.g., adapted workstations, adjusted hours, funded commuting). Despite efforts, the disability employment rate remains below the statutory target. Methodology: in France, disability status is tracked via RQTH declarations in payroll; outside France, local legal definitions are used.
- Training and careers: Annual appraisals are central to performance recognition, skill development, and career planning; they are legally required in France but not in all countries, explaining international completion-rate differences. Beyond appraisals, the Group invests in continuous training to build skills, adapt to evolving roles, and support engagement; figures exclude academic training for work‑study students.
- Workforce indicators presented: Employee age distribution—Under 30: 1,915; 30–50: 8,346; Over 50: 4,251. Employees with disabilities—Women: 5.55%; Men: 3.29%; Overall: 4.53%.

nodes.title: Disability situations
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.5 Disability situations
nodes.start_phrase: La Banque Postale Group pays particular attention to the integration of employees with disabilities, while promoting the ability of existing employees to declare a disability should they need to do so.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information) and covers employee-related CSR commitments and metrics.

- Adequate wages and social protection: All employees are paid at least the legal minimum or per applicable collective or company agreements. The Group ensures 100% social protection coverage for illness, unemployment, work-related accidents/disability, parental leave, and retirement, via public schemes or company benefits.

- Disability inclusion: The Group prioritizes integration and encourages disclosure of disabilities, though overall representation remains below statutory targets. Support measures include workstation and schedule adaptations and commuting assistance. In France, disability status is tracked via RQTH; outside France, local legal definitions apply. Reported disability representation: 4.53% overall; women 5.55%, men 3.29%.

- Training and careers: Annual employee appraisals are a strategic tool for performance recognition and career development; they are legally required in France but not in all countries, explaining international variation in completion rates. The Group invests in continuous training to build skills, adapt to evolving roles, and support employee engagement; training figures exclude academic training for work‑study students.

- Workforce demographics: Age distribution shows 1,915 employees under 30, 8,346 between 30 and 50, and 4,251 over 50.

- References: Uses S1 indicator tags and directs readers to a glossary on page 808 for CSR term definitions.

nodes.title: Training and careers
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.6 Training and careers
nodes.start_phrase: Annual employee appraisals play an essential role in career development, offering an opportunity to recognise performance, identify skills to be improved and map out career development prospects.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (Sustainable performance – Social information), covering wages and social protection, disability inclusion, training and careers, and health and safety, with CSR indicator references.

- Adequate wages and social protection:
  - All employees receive an adequate wage (at least the legal minimum in each country).
  - 100% social protection coverage for employee illness, unemployment, work-related accidents/disability, parental leave, and retirement.

- Disability inclusion:
  - Focus on integrating employees with disabilities and encouraging declarations, with tailored support (e.g., workstation and schedule adaptations, commuting support).
  - Measurement: In France via RQTH status from payroll; abroad via local legal definitions.
  - Employees with disabilities: total 4.53%; women 5.55%; men 3.29%—below the statutory rate.

- Training and careers:
  - Annual appraisals are a key lever for performance recognition and career development; legally required in France (leading to international variation in completion rates).
  - Strong internal communication on appraisals; continuous training emphasized; work‑study academic training excluded from figures.
  - Performance review completion (eligible employees): total 82.05% (women 80.38%, men 84.07%).
  - Average training hours per employee: total 21.92 (women 21.70, men 22.18).

- Workforce profile:
  - Employees by age: under 30: 1,915; 30–50: 8,346; over 50: 4,251.

- Health and safety:
  - 99.66% of employees covered by a health and safety policy; indicators tracked monthly.
  - Zero deaths due to occupational accidents or illnesses; 0 recordable cases of ill health.
  - 54 workplace accidents with lost time; 2.32 lost‑time accidents per million hours worked (low vs. French average of 21 per million in 2019).
  - 1,760 days lost due to workplace accidents.

nodes.title: Health and safety
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.7 Health and safety
nodes.start_phrase: Almost all of La Banque Postale Group’s workforce is covered by a health and safety policy.
nodes.summary:
- Focus area: Sustainable performance – Social information from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, covering health and safety, work-life balance, and remuneration equality.
- Health and safety:
  - 99.66% of employees covered by a health and safety policy.
  - Indicators monitored monthly; accident rates remain below the French average.
  - 0 deaths due to occupational accidents or illnesses; 54 workplace accidents with lost time.
  - 2.32 lost-time accidents per million hours worked; 0 recordable cases of ill health.
  - 1,760 days lost due to workplace accidents and related causes.
  - High participation in performance and career reviews; average training around 22 hours per employee, with similar levels across genders.
- Work-life balance and family leave:
  - 100% of employees entitled to a wide range of family leaves (maternity/adoption, paternity, parental, breastfeeding, co-parent, birth/adoption, disability support, etc.).
  - 2024 usage: 5.6% of total workforce took family leave (3.8% men; 6.7% women).
  - Among eligible employees: 11.91% took leave (10.73% men; 12.88% women), indicating persistent gender imbalance in caregiving responsibilities.
- Remuneration gap and pay equity:
  - Overall gender remuneration gap: 16.7%, mainly driven by job/grade structure (more women at lower grades, reverse at higher levels).
  - Actions under the 2024 “Diversity and professional equality” agreement: targeted recruitment of under-represented gender, partnerships to de-segment “gendered” roles, career development for women (e.g., Girlz in the Bank), and anti-sexism initiatives.
  - €600,000 annual budget dedicated to reducing unjustified pay gaps.
  - Pay ratio: highest to median remuneration is 10.4.
- Methodology highlights:
  - Gender pay gap based on gross hourly remuneration (fixed, bonuses, annual and long-term variable; excludes profit-sharing/matching).
  - Pay ratio includes profit-sharing and matching; covers employees with at least three months’ service.
  - Work-study contracts excluded due to statutory pay grid; indicators aggregated across Group entities proportionate to workforce; small number of non-France employees excluded where data unavailable.

nodes.title: Work-life balance
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.8 Work-life balance
nodes.start_phrase: Group employees are entitled to family leave:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR/Social information) covering work-life balance and gender remuneration topics, with methodology notes.
- Work-life balance and family leave:
  - 100% of employees are entitled to family leave based on intrinsic eligibility, regardless of whether a triggering event occurs.
  - Types of leave offered include: maternity/adoption, paternity, parental, breastfeeding leave, conventional maternity top-ups (100% and 50%), co-parent leave (LBP SA), birth/adoption leave, and ASA leave supporting people with disabilities (LBP SA).
  - In 2024, 5.6% of the total workforce took family-related leave: 3.8% of men and 6.7% of women.
  - Among employees eligible for such leave, uptake was higher, with women using it more than men, highlighting a persistent imbalance in parental and family responsibility sharing.
- Gender remuneration gap:
  - Overall 2024 gender pay gap: 16.7%, largely explained by job structure (more women in lower grades, more men in higher grades).
  - Actions under the 2024 “Diversity and professional equality” agreement: targeted recruitment to improve gender mix in business lines, partnerships with schools/charities to attract under-represented genders to “gendered” professions, career support for women (e.g., Girlz in the Bank), and prevention of everyday sexism.
  - €600,000 annual budget dedicated to reducing unjustified pay gaps.
  - Highest-to-median remuneration ratio: 10.4, presented as reflecting moderation and alignment with inclusion and social responsibility values.
- Methodology and perimeter:
  - Gender pay gap compares gross hourly remuneration (annualized fixed pay, bonuses, benefits, annual and long-term variable), excluding profit-sharing and matching contributions.
  - Highest-to-median ratio uses total annual remuneration including profit-sharing and matching.
  - Population: employees on permanent or temporary contracts with at least three months’ service in the year; work-study students excluded due to statutory pay grids.
  - Indicators aggregate CNP Assurances with the rest of La Banque Postale Group weighted by workforce; 10 La Financière de l’Échiquier employees outside France excluded.

nodes.title: Remuneration gap
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.9 Remuneration gap
nodes.start_phrase: In 2024, the overall remuneration gap between women and men was 16.7%.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document (CSR/Social information), covering work-life balance, gender remuneration, and human rights performance and metrics.

- Work-life balance and family leave
  - Broad family leave entitlements (100% of employees eligible): conventional maternity (100% and 50%), maternity/adoption, paternity, parental, breastfeeding leave, co‑parent leave (LBP SA), birth/adoption leave, and ASA leave to support people with disabilities (LBP SA).
  - 2024 usage: 5.6% of total workforce took family leave (3.8% men; 6.7% women).
  - Among eligible employees: 11.91% took leave (10.73% men; 12.88% women), indicating higher uptake by women and a persistent imbalance in caregiving responsibilities.
  - Eligibility rate is based on intrinsic entitlement, not occurrence of a triggering event.

- Gender remuneration gap and pay ratio
  - 2024 overall gender remuneration gap: 16.7%, primarily due to job structure (women overrepresented in lower grades; reverse at higher levels).
  - Actions under the 2024 “Diversity and professional equality” agreement: increase gender diversity in roles (targeted recruitment with equal skills), partnerships with schools/NGOs to attract underrepresented genders to “gendered” jobs, women’s career development initiatives (e.g., Girlz in the Bank), and prevention of everyday sexism.
  - Dedicated annual budget of €600,000 to reduce unjustified pay gaps.
  - Pay ratio: highest total remuneration to median is 10.4, reflecting moderation aligned with inclusion and social responsibility values.
  - Methodology highlights: gender gap based on gross hourly pay (fixed pay, bonuses, benefits, annual and long‑term variable pay; excludes profit-sharing/matching). Pay ratio includes profit-sharing and matching. Includes employees (permanent/temporary) with ≥3 months’ service; excludes work‑study contracts; aggregates CNP Assurances with the rest of the Group proportionally; excludes 10 La Financière de l’Échiquier employees outside France.

- Human rights, discrimination, and complaints
  - Commitments aligned with La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy: prevent violations and complicity; prohibit violence, inhuman/degrading treatment, forced/child labor and trafficking; ban discrimination (gender, age, health/disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, nationality, social background, community, political/union/religious beliefs); uphold freedom of association and collective bargaining; ensure adequate remuneration; protect privacy; ensure GDPR compliance; comply with labor laws in operating countries.
  - 2024 outcomes: no proven severe human rights incidents; no fines, penalties, or compensation related to human rights incidents.
  - Discrimination/harassment and complaints metrics: 5 incidents recorded; 76 complaints received via communication channels; 0 complaints to national contact points; €0 in fines/penalties/compensation.
  - Severe human rights issues and employee-related incidents (including UNGP/OECD non-compliance): 0; associated fines/penalties/compensation: 0.

nodes.title: Severe human rights incidents
nodes.heading: 2.3.1.7.10 Severe human rights incidents
nodes.start_phrase: As part of La Poste Group’s Human Rights policy, La Banque Postale Group is committed to:
nodes.summary:
- Human rights commitments: prevention of violations; prohibition of violence, forced or compulsory labour, child labour and trafficking; ban on all discrimination (e.g., gender, age, health/disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, nationality, social background, community, political/trade union/religious beliefs); defense of freedom of association and collective bargaining; right to adequate remuneration; opposition to invasion of privacy. Strong GDPR and national labor law compliance.
- 2024 outcomes and metrics:
  - Proven severe human rights incidents: 0
  - Non-compliance with UNGP/OECD Guidelines: 0
  - Incidents of discrimination and harassment: 5
  - Complaints received via communication channels: 76
  - Complaints to national contact points: 0
  - Fines/penalties/compensation for discrimination/harassment: €0
  - Fines/penalties/compensation for severe human rights issues: €0
  - No additional background information beyond reported figures.
- Workers in the value chain (La Poste employees and civil servants working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale):
  - Scope: Significant share of the value chain; roles in branches, remote customer relations, IT, and head-office support; report to La Poste or La Banque Postale; work on La Banque Postale or La Poste sites; not part of La Banque Postale’s direct workforce.
  - Risk profile: Activities in France in banking services; no specific risks of forced or child labour; no particularly vulnerable sub-groups identified; no subgroup more exposed to harm.
  - Material IRO: Potential negative impact from poor working conditions or forced/child labour in the value chain identified as material but not widespread/systemic; no specific positive impact identified for these workers.
  - Dependency: Functional dependency on La Poste due to scale and services, not monitored as a risk since La Poste is the parent company.
- Policies and governance:
  - Covered by La Poste’s Human Rights policy; HR policies provided by La Poste and aligned with La Banque Postale’s culture.
  - Two agreements between La Banque Postale and La Poste:
    - Health and safety for seconded workers hosted on La Banque Postale sites.
    - Workforce, recruitment, and regulatory/mandatory training.
    - Regular monitoring; no specific action plan implemented to date.
  - Human rights protections equivalent to La Banque Postale employees; La Banque Postale’s code of conduct applies to all workers in the value chain.

nodes.title: Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
nodes.heading: 2.3.2.1.1 Material IROs and links with strategy and business model
nodes.start_phrase: Among the workers in the value chain, the workforce working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale, with a re-invoicing system by La Banque Postale for the use of La Poste’s employees, is affected by the (positive or negative) impacts identified (see list of IROs in Section 2.1.3.2 “Description of material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs)”).
nodes.summary:
- Focus on ensuring favorable working conditions for workers in La Banque Postale’s value chain, specifically La Poste employees working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale.
- Scope covers a significant workforce of La Poste Group employees and civil servants assigned to La Banque Postale activities (banking advice, post offices, remote customer relations, IT, and head-office support), included in ESRS 2 reporting.
- These workers operate on La Banque Postale or La Poste sites, may report to managers from either entity, and are not counted in La Banque Postale’s own workforce; costs are re-invoiced.
- No vulnerable categories or sub-groups with higher exposure to harm have been identified.
- No specific risk of forced or child labor, as activities are banking services conducted in France; workers are protected by La Poste’s Human Rights policy.
- A material negative impact is recognized: potential poor working conditions (e.g., unequal pay, safety issues) in the value chain; this impact is material but not widespread or systemic.
- No specific positive impacts identified; policies on working conditions and anti-discrimination are aligned with La Poste as the parent company, and La Banque Postale does not significantly influence La Poste’s policies.
- Functional dependency on La Poste due to workforce size and mission is acknowledged but not treated as a risk because La Poste is the parent company.
- Applicable policies: La Poste’s HR and Human Rights policies cover these workers; two inter-company agreements exist—one on health and safety for seconded workers hosted on La Banque Postale sites, and another on workforce, recruitment, and mandatory training; these are regularly monitored, with no specific action plan currently in place.
- Human rights protections mirror those for La Banque Postale employees, and La Banque Postale’s Code of Conduct applies to all value-chain workers.

nodes.title: Applicable policies
nodes.heading: 2.3.2.1.2 Applicable policies
nodes.start_phrase: La Poste workers working for and on behalf of La Banque Postale are, like La Banque Postale workers, covered by La Poste’s Human Rights policy.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and workforce: Focus on La Poste Group employees (including civil servants) who work for and on behalf of La Banque Postale (LBP) in post offices, remote customer relations, banking advice, IT, and HQ support. They may report to La Poste or LBP managers, work on La Poste/LBP sites, are not counted in LBP’s own workforce, and are covered under ESRS S2 disclosures.
- Risk profile: Activities occur in France and involve banking services; no specific risks of forced or child labor identified. No vulnerable sub-groups or sub-groups with higher exposure to harm identified. The potential material negative impact relates to poor working conditions (e.g., unequal pay, safety). Impact is material but not widespread/systemic. No specific positive impacts identified. LBP has a functional dependency on La Poste, but it is not treated as a risk since La Poste is the parent company.
- Policies and governance: Workers are covered by La Poste’s Human Rights and HR policies, aligned with LBP’s culture. Two intercompany agreements govern (1) health and safety for seconded workers on LBP sites and (2) workforce, recruitment, and mandatory training. LBP’s code of conduct applies to value-chain workers. No dedicated action plan tied to these agreements to date.
- Dialogue mechanisms: Feedback gathered through La Poste’s engagement survey and annual appraisals/interviews, with social dialogue managed by La Poste’s bodies.
