    - “Other” Taxonomy-non-eligible activities: €86,829m (48.2%).
    - Total Taxonomy-non-eligible: €86,919m (48.3%).
- New disclosure scope (FAQs Nov 2024): Financial institutions must publish Taxonomy KPIs across all business segments, including asset management, insurance, and investment, beyond core banking. La Banque Postale provides segment KPIs for material businesses.
- Asset management (LBP AM):
  - Portfolio Taxonomy alignment ratio at 31 Dec 2024: 3.0%.
  - Contribution breakdown: 0.6% from debt securities; 2.4% from equity instruments.
- Insurance business (CNP Assurances within Group via equity-accounted shares):
  - Combined Taxonomy KPI (per EC Communication C/2024/6691):
    - Turnover-based alignment: 3.0%.
    - CapEx-based alignment: 4.1%.
- Underwriting indicators (non-life, adaptation objective):
  - Taxonomy-aligned non-life gross written premiums / total non-life GWP: 0.7% at end-2024.
  - Methodology: Eligible premiums must meet technical screening for substantial contribution to climate change adaptation, DNSH, and minimum safeguards; compliance supported by procedures to manage adverse impacts. In France, aligned premiums largely reflect natural disaster coverage in motor and homeowner policies.
- Investment indicators (insurance portfolios):
  - Aim to measure the share of CNP’s investments aligned with the Taxonomy for climate change adaptation and mitigation (turnover and CapEx bases), demonstrating capital reallocation toward sustainable activities.
- Cross-references: Further details in LBP AM’s off-balance sheet exposures section and CNP Assurances’ CSRD report; glossary reference for CSR terms.

nodes.title: Taxonomy indicators by business segment
nodes.heading: 2.5.1.7 Taxonomy indicators by business segment
nodes.start_phrase: The FAQs of November 2024 introduce a requirement for financial players to publish key performance indicators (KPIs) for all their business segments, including assetmanagement, insurance and investment, in addition to their main banking activity.
nodes.summary:
- Context: Excerpt from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, Notes to the sustainability report, detailing EU Taxonomy indicators by business segment.
- Regulatory backdrop: November 2024 FAQs require financial institutions to disclose Taxonomy KPIs for all business segments (banking, asset management, insurance, investment). The Group reports for its material segments.
- Asset management: LBP AM assesses portfolio alignment with the EU Taxonomy; as of 31 Dec 2024, alignment is 3.0% (0.6% from debt securities, 2.4% from equity). Further detail referenced in the Off-balance sheet exposures section.
- Insurance scope and approach: Insurance activities included in Group indicators via equity-accounted subsidiaries, with additional insurance-specific KPIs covering:
  - Non-life underwriting indicators (adaptation target).
  - Investment indicators for euro-denominated and unit-linked savings portfolios.
- Combined KPI disclosure (per European Commission communication C/2024/6691 on Article 8 Taxonomy disclosures): CNP Assurances publishes a combined KPI—3.0% based on turnover and 4.1% based on CapEx.
- Underwriting KPIs: At 31 Dec 2024, Taxonomy-aligned non-life gross written premiums represent 0.7% of total non-life GWP. Methodology follows technical screening for substantial contribution to climate change adaptation, DNSH, and minimum safeguards, supported by procedures to manage actual/potential negative impacts; in France, aligned premiums correspond to natural disaster cover in motor and homeowner insurance.
- Investment KPIs: Measure the share of CNP Assurances’ investments aligned with Taxonomy objectives for climate adaptation and mitigation (using turnover and CapEx), indicating capital reallocation toward sustainable activities.
- Cross-references: Readers are directed to CNP Assurances’ CSRD report for detailed methodology and results, and to the URD section on off-balance sheet exposures for asset management details.

nodes.title: Investment indicators
nodes.heading: 2.5.1.7.2.2 Investment indicators
nodes.start_phrase: The investment KPIs aim to measure the proportion of CNP Assurances’ investments allocated to economic activities compliant with the Taxonomy on the targets of climate change adaptation and mitigation in terms ofturnover and capital expenditure.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and context: Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document detailing sustainability reporting notes, with a focus on EU Taxonomy indicators across business segments per November 2024 FAQs requiring KPIs for banking, asset management, insurance, and investment.
- Asset management (LBP AM): Portfolio Taxonomy alignment at 3.0% as of 31 Dec 2024 (0.6% debt securities, 2.4% equity); detailed results referenced in off-balance sheet exposures.
- Insurance business (CNP Assurances):
  - Combined Taxonomy KPIs per EC Communication C/2024/6691: 3.0% (turnover-based) and 4.1% (CapEx-based).
  - Underwriting KPIs (adaptation target): Taxonomy-aligned non-life gross written premiums at 0.7%; methodology based on substantial contribution criteria, DNSH, and minimum safeguards; in France, alignment mainly via natural disaster cover in motor and homeowner policies.
  - Investment KPIs (euro and unit-linked portfolios):
    - 3.3% of technical reserves investments in Taxonomy-aligned activities (turnover approach) excluding sovereign bonds.
    - 4.5% alignment using investment outlay basis, as a share of technical reserves investments excluding sovereigns.
    - Methodology highlights: exclude sovereign bonds (green/sustainable bonds not treated differently), apply non-financial issuer turnover/CapEx shares to equities/bonds for eligibility/alignment, financial sector holdings treated as invalid at end-2024 due to lack of KPIs on all six environmental targets; property and forest holdings classified as eligible/aligned/non-aligned per Taxonomy criteria.
  - Repeated references to CNP Assurances’ CSRD report for detailed methodology and results.
- Cross-reference tables (ESRS coverage):
  - ESRS 2 General disclosures: reporting scope, methods, changes, incorporation by reference; governance roles, skills, oversight, incentives, due diligence, and internal control; business model, stakeholders, material IROs, strategy resilience, and IRO identification/assessment processes.
  - ESRS E1 Climate change: transition plan, material climate IROs, policies, actions/resources, targets, energy consumption/mix, GHG emissions (Scopes 1–3), carbon credits, internal carbon pricing, anticipated financial effects, and European Green Taxonomy section references.
  - Table maps each disclosure requirement to specific paragraphs/sections demonstrating coverage.

structure.summary:
- Presents cross-reference tables mapping La Banque Postale’s sustainability disclosures to the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) and to specific sections of the 2024 Universal Registration Document.
- Covers ESRS 2 (general disclosures) including reporting scope, methodologies, changes year over year, incorporation by reference, governance roles and skills, remuneration alignment, due diligence, and internal control over sustainability reporting; strategy, business model, stakeholder interests, material impacts/risks/opportunities (IRO), and IRO identification processes.
- Details ESRS E1–E5 environmental topics:
  - E1 Climate change: transition plan aligned with Paris Agreement, climate IROs, policies, actions/resources, targets, energy use/mix, Scopes 1–3 and total GHG, carbon credits and removals, internal carbon price, financial effects of climate risks, and EU Green Taxonomy.
  - E2 Pollution: IRO assessment, policies, action plans, and targets.
  - E3 Water and marine resources: IRO assessment, policies, actions, targets.
  - E4 Biodiversity and ecosystems: transition plan, IROs, policies, actions, targets.
  - E5 Circular economy: resource-use and circularity IROs, policies, actions, objectives, and metrics (including outgoing resources and waste).
- Covers ESRS S1–S4 social topics:
  - S1 Own workforce: policies, social dialogue, grievance/remediation, action plans, targets; workforce characteristics, diversity, adequate wages/social protection, disability inclusion, training, health and safety, work-life balance, pay gaps, and severe human rights incidents.
  - S2 Workers in the value chain: policies, engagement, grievance/remediation, actions/resources, objectives across upstream/downstream segments, including child/forced labor risks.
  - S3 Affected communities: policies, engagement, remediation, action plans, positive-impact commitments, and targets.
  - S4 Consumers and end-users: policies, engagement, remediation, actions/resources, and targets.
- Covers ESRS G1 Business conduct: governance roles/skills, corporate culture, commitments on business conduct, supplier management and payment practices, anti-corruption/bribery prevention, incident reporting, and lobbying transparency.
- Provides extensive linkage of ESRS data points to other EU legislation and frameworks, including SFDR, CRR/Pillar III ESG disclosures, the EU Benchmark Regulation, and the European Climate Law, specifying where metrics such as board diversity/independence, fossil fuel involvement, climate targets, energy use, GHG emissions and intensities, physical/transition risk exposures, labor and human rights metrics, waste, and water appear.
- Notes that only material disclosure requirements are listed in the cross-reference tables; some data points are detailed elsewhere in the document.
- Introduces the Risk factors – Pillar III disclosures section on ESG risks:
  - Defines ESG risks as the negative impact of environmental, social, and governance factors on financial performance/solvency, affecting counterparties and assets, and transmitting through traditional risk categories.
  - Outlines the evolving regulatory framework: ECB (2020) supervisory expectations, EBA (2021) report, EU Green Taxonomy with first-time Green Asset Ratio (GAR) calculation at 31 Dec 2023 (annual for taxonomy, semiannual for Pillar III), and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2453 governing semiannual qualitative and quantitative ESG risk disclosures (transition and physical risks).
  - References French regulations on business ethics (duty of care, Sapin II) and corporate governance codes.
  - Points to related sections with quantitative indicators and methodologies (e.g., Sections 6.8.7–6.8.10 and 6.1).

structure.title: Certification of consolidated sustainability information and control of the disclosure
structure.heading: 2.7 Certification of consolidated sustainability information and control of the disclosure
structure.summary:
- Scope and purpose
  - Extract from La Banque Postale’s 2024 Universal Registration Document, Pillar III disclosures on Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) risks.
  - Explains definitions, regulatory context, governance, identification, measurement, management and reporting of ESG risks, plus required Pillar III templates and EU Taxonomy KPIs.

- Regulatory framework and definitions
  - ESG risks defined as the potential negative impact of environmental, social, and governance factors on financial performance/solvency.
  - Key references: ECB 2020 climate and environmental risk guide; EBA 2021 report on ESG risk management; EU Green Taxonomy Regulation (EU) 2020/852; Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2453 on ESG Pillar III disclosures.
  - French requirements on ethics and governance (duty of care, Sapin II, governance code).
  - Double materiality principle (outside-in financial materiality and inside-out impact materiality).

- ESG risk typology
  - Environmental: climate risk (physical acute/chronic and transition) and nature risk (dependencies/impacts per TNFD; systemic risks such as ecosystem collapse, contagion).
  - Social and societal: impacts from employment, health and safety, inclusion, data protection; risks from regulatory/market changes.
  - Governance: failures in governance practices and integration of E/S factors; reputational risks and strategy execution failures.
  - ESG as a standalone category and as a driver across traditional risk types (credit, market, operational, liquidity).

- Governance and organization
  - Mission-led company since 2022; ESG embedded in Articles of Association and strategic planning.
  - Oversight by Supervisory and Executive Boards; Sustainability Department reporting to the Executive Board; Group Risk Department (ESG Risk unit) sets framework and second line monitoring; Group Compliance oversees compliance/reputational dimensions.
  - Training for employees (climate modules, Climate Fresk); subsidiaries align frameworks; group steering committees.

- Risk identification, assessment and mapping
  - Integration of ESG in lending and product design (pre-deal climate analysis, sector exclusions, support for renewables).
  - Climate risk assessed across short, medium, long horizons; links to credit, market, liquidity, operational, strategic risks with mitigation frameworks.
  - Annual ESG risk map with environmental (physical/transition climate and nature), social/societal, and governance risk families; tracking indicators (e.g., flood exposure, SBTi alignment, fossil fuel exposure, HR and customer protection metrics).
  - Criticality of ESG risk rated “major”; biodiversity added in 2023.

- Measurement and monitoring
  - ESG embedded in Risk Appetite Framework (non-financial ratings, reputational risk).
  - Physical risk indicators: exposure of LBP buildings to 1-in-100-year flood; exposure of real estate book to flooding (2.6% of residential book at risk; concentration in Île-de-France).
  - Transition risk indicators:
    - Alignment with SBTi pathways (annual gap tracking).
    - Financed emissions (PCAF-based): ~10,920 ktCO2 for corporate and real estate books (c.74% coverage) at 30 June 2024; Pillar III table shows 2.97 MtCO2e as of 31 Dec 2024 for covered scope.
    - Sector exposures and near-zero net exposure to fossil fuels (0.005% of corporate book in Q4 2024); coal/oil & gas phase-out policies.
    - EU Taxonomy Green Asset Ratio (GAR) 2024: 5.7% mandatory (stock, turnover view), plus 2.3% voluntary = 8.0% total; data and interpretation caveats noted.
  - Social/societal indicators: customer satisfaction 7.5/10; gender equality index ≥91/100 across entities.
  - Governance indicators: 50% women on Supervisory Board (2024); 39% of offers labeled “socially responsible” in 2023; target 80% by 2025.

- Time horizons, provisions, and stress testing
  - ESG Risk Management Policy covers short/medium/long-term impacts; sector policies for coal and oil & gas (exit by 2030), aviation financing principles (2022), and deforestation (2023).
  - 2024 provisions: transition risk on corporates (carbon price impacts) and physical flood risk on retail mortgages (recoveries).
  - Participation in ACPR (2020/21) and ECB (2022) climate stress tests; internal stress testing based on NGFS scenarios over 1–3 years with intent to extend >10 years in 2025; market and operational risk scenarios (e.g., Seine flood, greenwashing).

- Business model integration and incentives
  - Commitments: PRB, Finance for Biodiversity Pledge, SBTi-approved portfolio pathways with targets for Scope 1–2–3 reductions, 100% renewable electricity, and temperature alignment for portfolios by 2025.
  - ESG integrated in credit approval and client reviews (transition plans, IWF scores); Disputes and Exclusions Committee for counterparties.
  - Remuneration: ≥40% of individual variable pay tied to non-financial targets since 2022; profit-sharing includes ESG ratings metric (25% weight); budget for gender pay equity.

- Products, tools, and client support
  - ESG checklist mandatory in product approvals; eco-design approach.
  - Impact Weighting Factor included in impact mortgages and specialized financings; Carbo app for client carbon footprinting/offsets.
  - Retail: extensive home energy renovation financing (e.g., Prêt Avance Rénovation), impact consumer finance, solidarity savings.
  - Corporate/public sector: green and impact loans; SRI offering via LBP AM (GREaT methodology).

- Monitoring and reporting model
  - Three lines of defence with ESG in Internal Audit scope.
  - Internal dashboards to GRMC; regulatory disclosures; reliance on external data; ESG data platform underway.

- Pillar III ESG templates and key results
  - Credit quality by sector and financed emissions (Template 1):
    - Method to identify firms excluded from EU Paris-Aligned Benchmark (via NACE + GOGEL/GCEL, minus SBTi-aligned renewables); exposure €411m; sustainable exposures €498m.
    - Financed emissions in table: 2.97 MtCO2e (incl. 2.24 Mt Scope 3) as of 31 Dec 2024.
  - Energy efficiency of real estate collateral (Template 2):
    - €85.3bn loans; EP score distribution; EPC labels; majority without EPC label; mix of obtained/estimated data; stability vs 2023.
  - Sectoral low-carbon pathways (Template 3): alignment metrics and distance to IEA NZ2050 2030 milestones for autos, air transport, cement.
  - Exposure to top 20 global emitters (Template 4): €43m (0.14% of covered assets), mostly green-aligned exposure; decreased since June 2024.
  - Physical risk exposures (Template 5): 5.9% of total exposures sensitive to physical risks (12.3% corporates; 4.7% residential RE; 0.1% commercial RE); sector/maturity breakdown.
  - EU Taxonomy KPIs:
    - GAR stock 5.7% (turnover) and 6.0% (CapEx); flow 1.7%; households (mortgages and renovations) dominate aligned assets.
    - Voluntary GAR +2.3% (stock); off-balance sheet alignment for assets under management; inclusion of CNP Assurances via equity method.
    - Detailed numerator/denominator composition and sector splits (Templates 6–9).
  - Other climate mitigation not covered by Taxonomy (Template 10): ~€11bn of green-targeted assets (green/sustainability bonds, renewable energy loans, Eco-PTZ and other green retail loans, RT 2012/RE 2020 housing) outside mandatory GAR.
